prs.title: fix(edit): normalize single-object edits argument to array
prs.body:
## Summary

The edit tool rejects calls where `edits` is a single object (or a JSON string holding one object) instead of an array. Some models wrap their arguments for the edit tool in a single object `{oldText, newText}` rather than `[{oldText, newText}]`.

The existing `prepareEditArguments` function already handles stringified arrays but does not handle:
- Stringified single objects: `edits: '{"oldText": "...", "newText": "..."}'`
- Native single objects: `edits: {oldText: "...", newText: "..."}`

## Changes

- When `args.edits` is a JSON string that parses to a single object with `oldText`/`newText`, wrap it into a one-element array
- When `args.edits` is a plain object (not array, not string) with `oldText`/`newText` properties, wrap it into a one-element array

## Example

Before:
```
Validation failed for tool "edit":
  - edits.0: must be object
```

After: Object is normalized to `[{oldText, newText}]` and the edit is applied normally.

Fixes #7835

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): render Mermaid diagrams in HTML exports
prs.body:
Hello! Noticed that the exports didn't render the mermaid diagrams like the tui does, so re-used most of the code that renders the tool calls by translating them from ANSI to HTML. By default they're not shown rendered, but they can be toggled from the header. They're also wrapped into a div with overflow so that the diagrams are not taking a massive amount of space when they're too big. When diagrams are not renderable, it keeps the same warning as the tui but it should work as is when/if it's fixed upstream. (see https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7832 + https://github.com/xl0/grok-mermaid/issues/1) Demo session: https://pi.dev/session/#58cb34b36dc48e2ebae711e00d8d330c Let me know if you want / need more changes! ------
Summary by GLM-5.2:

## Summary Pre-renders Mermaid fenced code blocks server-side into lightweight, themed HTML so exported sessions display real diagrams instead of raw ` ```mermaid ` source. The default export view stays as source code; a global toggle switches all blocks to the rendered diagram. ## Why HTML exports previously showed Mermaid blocks as plain source (or Highlight.js-mangled source), which is unreadable for anything beyond a trivial graph. The TUI already renders Mermaid via `grok-mermaid`, but that path needs a live `Theme` instance and only runs interactively. This adds a standalone export-time renderer that works for both interactive (`/export`) and standalone session-file exports, with no client-side Mermaid bundle. ## What changed **`packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/mermaid-html.ts`** (new) - Self-contained helper: scans session entries for Markdown text, finds top-level fenced `mermaid` code blocks, renders each via `grok-mermaid`, and returns a `Record` (or `undefined` when empty). - No `Theme` instance, no `agent-session.ts` changes, no width check (HTML scrolls), no client-side JS bundle. - Maps `grok-mermaid`'s `Cls` runs to export CSS variables (`border`→`--borderMuted`, `text`→`--text`, `edge`→`--accent`, `edgeLabel`→`--muted`, `title`→`--accent` + bold, `none`→passthrough) — same mapping as the TUI `mermaid.ts`. - Each diagram emits both a rendered `

` (starts `hidden`) and an escaped `
`, so the initial HTML matches the source-visible default with no pre-JS flash.
- If `grok-mermaid` returns `null`, no entry is added (falls back to source). Partial renders include an inline warning.

**`packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts`**
- `SessionData` gains optional `mermaidDiagrams?: Record`.
- Both export paths build the map: `exportSessionToHtml` (interactive) and `exportFromFile` (standalone CLI). Omitted from the serialized payload when empty.

**`packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js`**
- Destructures `mermaidDiagrams` from the payload.
- The marked `code(token)` renderer short-circuits when the first language word is `mermaid` and a pre-rendered entry exists for `token.text.trim()`; otherwise falls back to the normal Highlight.js path.
- Adds a global "Toggle Mermaid" header button and an `M` keyboard shortcut (alongside the existing thinking/tools toggles). Default state is source-visible. `applyMermaidView` runs once per navigation on the freshly built message DOM.

**`packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.css`**
- `.mermaid-diagram`: centered, `width: max-content`, constrained to `max-width: 100%` / `max-height: 60vh` with scrollbars.
- `.mermaid-source`: full-width, scrollable.
- `.mermaid-render [hidden] { display: none !important; }` guard so the `display: block` rules don't override the native `hidden` attribute.
- `.mermaid-warning`: themed via `--warning`.

## Behavior

- Default view: source code. Clicking "Toggle Mermaid" (or pressing `M`) flips all Mermaid blocks globally between source and rendered diagram. State persists across in-export navigation.
- Unsupported/invalid Mermaid: no rendered entry → normal source block. Partial renders show the diagram plus an inline "Diagram not fully rendered" warning; source is still available.
- No TUI theme or live agent state required, so standalone `pi` session-file exports render diagrams too.

prs.title: fix(ai): map models.dev cost tiers for every provider
prs.body:
Fixes #7912.

## Problem

`getModelsDevCost` (generate-models.ts) already maps models.dev's `cost.tiers[].tier{type,size}` onto `cost.tiers[].inputTokensAbove`. It had exactly one call site: the github-copilot block. Every other provider built cost inline from the four scalar rates:

```ts
cost: {
  input: m.cost?.input || 0,
  output: m.cost?.output || 0,
  cacheRead: m.cost?.cache_read || 0,
  cacheWrite: m.cost?.cache_write || 0,
},
```

`m` is the models.dev model, tiers included; they were simply never copied. Anything over a provider's threshold was then priced at the short-context rate.

Concretely, models.dev has carried xAI's grok-4.5 long-context tier since 2026-07-31:

```json
"tiers": [{"input": 4, "output": 12, "cache_read": 0.6, "tier": {"type": "context", "size": 200000}}]
```

0.84.1 ships `{"input": 2, "output": 6, "cacheRead": 0.3, "cacheWrite": 0}` with no tiers. Measured over 10,119 grok-4.5 requests through our gateway, 244 (2.4%) exceeded 200k prompt tokens; catalog rates priced them at $270.83 against $302.35 on xAI's published card, 10.4% under.

`gpt-5.6-luna` looked correct only because `withOpenAiLongContextPricing` synthesizes its tier from a hardcoded allowlist, so the generic path was serving one provider out of roughly twenty-three.

## Change

Route the remaining models.dev-sourced providers through `getModelsDevCost`. For providers without tiers in models.dev the output is identical, since the helper computes the same four fields with the same `|| 0` fallbacks and only adds `tiers` when non-empty.

Four blocks have deliberate cost logic and keep it by spreading over the helper's result rather than replacing it:

- `google-vertex` keeps the `gemini-2.5-flash` cacheRead override and `cacheWrite: 0`, and zeroes `cacheWrite` on its tiers too, for the same reason it is zeroed on the base rates (pi only accounts `cachedContentTokenCount`, as cacheRead). This is the one judgement call in the diff.
- `mistral` keeps the `cache_read ?? input * 0.1` fallback.
- `kimi-for-coding` keeps its implied subscription costs.
- `moonshotai` keeps the `KIMI_K3_COST` fallbacks.

Providers priced from their own APIs (OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway) and the hardcoded model lists are untouched.

## Effect

Generating the catalog before and after and diffing all 1223 models:

```
models with tiers:  21 -> 56  (+35)
total models:     1223 -> 1223
base rates changed:  0
```

Zero base-rate changes: the change is purely additive. Tiers gained by provider: opencode 9, google 6, opencode-go 5, cloudflare-ai-gateway 4, amazon-bedrock 3, xai 3, google-vertex 3, minimax 1, minimax-cn 1.

`xai/grok-4.5` now generates as:

```json
{"input": 2, "output": 6, "cacheRead": 0.3, "cacheWrite": 0,
 "tiers": [{"inputTokensAbove": 200000, "input": 4, "output": 12, "cacheRead": 0.6, "cacheWrite": 0}]}
```

`src/providers/data/` is gitignored and `models.generated.ts` is unchanged, since no models were added or removed, so the diff is the generator plus one test.

## Tests

`packages/ai/test/model-cost-tiers.test.ts` pins grok-4.5's 200k tier and adds a catalog-wide invariant that no tier is priced below the rate it steps up from. Verified it fails against the pre-change catalog and passes after.

`npm run check` clean. `./test.sh` green (216 passed in coding-agent, 23 in ai, 132 in agent, all other packages passing).

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). Reviewed and verified by me before submitting.

prs.title: fix(edit): normalize single-object edits argument to array and collapse whitespace in fuzzy match
prs.body:
## Summary

The edit tool rejects calls where `edits` is a single object (or a JSON string holding one object) instead of an array. Some models wrap their arguments for the edit tool in a single object `{oldText, newText}` rather than `[{oldText, newText}]`.

The existing `prepareEditArguments` function already handles stringified arrays but does not handle:
- Stringified single objects: `edits: '{"oldText": "...", "newText": "..."}'`
- Native single objects: `edits: {oldText: "...", newText: "..."}`

## Changes

- When `args.edits` is a JSON string that parses to a single object with `oldText`/`newText`, wrap it into a one-element array
- When `args.edits` is a plain object (not array, not string) with `oldText`/`newText` properties, wrap it into a one-element array
- Also collapsed interior whitespace runs in `normalizeForFuzzyMatch` for #7836

Fixes #7835

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): Show when the fullscreen transcript is scrolled up
prs.body: This adds a `↓` in the status row whenever the transcript is not following the end. Scrolling back to the bottom clears it. ## How I wrote this with with the help of my clanker, but of course fully edited/vetted it myself: A new `StatusRegionComponent` wraps the existing status container and composes it with a `TranscriptStatusIndicator` that reads `ScrollView.isFollowingEnd`: ``` Before After ────── ───── VStack (root) VStack (root) ├─ ScrollView(transcript) ├─ ScrollView(transcript) ◄────────────┐ └─ VStack (dock) └─ VStack (dock) │ ├─ pendingMessages ├─ pendingMessages │ ├─ statusContainer ├─ StatusRegionComponent │ reads │ (empty | Loader) │ ├─ statusContainer (unchanged) │ isFollowingEnd ├─ widgetsAbove │ ├─ TranscriptStatusIndicator ───┘ │ (owns separator │ └─ owns the separator row │ via spacer flags) ├─ widgetsAbove (plain container) ├─ editor ├─ editor ├─ widgetsBelow ├─ widgetsBelow └─ footer └─ footer ``` The core constraint is that the indicator must never change the dock's height, so the arrow borrows existing rows instead of adding one: | state | status region renders | rows | | ------------------ | ------------------------------ | ---- | | idle, following | `separator` | 1 | | idle, scrolled | `↓` (replaces separator) | 1 | | working, following | `"" / ⠋ Working… / separator` | 3 | | working, scrolled | `"" / ↓ ⠋ Working… / separator`| 3 | This is why the separator row moves into the status region as it can only repurpose a row it owns. The `spacerWhenEmpty`/`leadingSpacer` flags on `renderWidgetContainer` become dead code and are removed. One `ScrollView` ninja-fix included: when layout itself flips the follow-end state (content shrinks below the viewport), nothing requested a repaint, so a sibling rendered from that state could stay stale. `updateLayout` now requests a render on the transition, this adds at most one extra frame. The indicator is fullscreen-only, this doesn't affect regular mode.

prs.title: fix(tui): route selection copy through the host clipboard so "Copied!" is truthful
prs.body:
## Summary

`TuiAltScreen.copySelectionToClipboard()` wrote a bare **OSC 52** sequence to the terminal and flashed **"Copied!"** unconditionally. Terminals that ignore OSC 52 clipboard writes (macOS Terminal.app, VTE-based terminals such as GNOME Terminal/Tilix, and tmux without OSC 52 clipboard passthrough) leave the system clipboard untouched while the toast reports success. This is the symptom reported in #7761 (and #7767, same cause on macOS Terminal.app).

This PR makes the select-to-copy path go through the host application's real clipboard implementation, and only reports success when the copy actually happened.

## Changes

**`packages/tui`** — add an injectable `copySelection` option to `TuiAltScreenOptions`:

```ts
/** Copy selected text to the system clipboard. Return true on success; the caller flashes an error otherwise. Falls back to OSC 52 when omitted. */
copySelection?: (text: string) => Promise<boolean>;
```

- `copySelectionToClipboard()` is now `async`. When a handler is provided it is awaited; the toast flashes `"Copied!"` only if the handler returned `true`, and `"Copy failed"` otherwise.
- When no handler is provided, behavior is unchanged (existing OSC 52 write + `"Copied!"`), so the change is backward compatible for other `pi-tui` consumers.

**`packages/coding-agent`** — `createInteractiveTui` now injects a handler backed by `copyToClipboard()` (native clipboard addon, then `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip` / `xsel`, with OSC 52 as a last resort for remote sessions). This is the same verified-success path the `/copy` command already used.

**Tests** — added two cases in `tui-alt-screen.test.ts` covering the injected-handler success and failure flash behavior, asserting no OSC 52 is emitted when a handler is provided.

## Why an injection point rather than importing the app's clipboard into pi-tui

`pi-tui` is a renderer/library and shouldn't depend on the coding-agent's platform clipboard logic; keeping the native clipboard code in the app (where `/copy` already owned it) avoids duplicating it and lets other `pi-tui` consumers plug in their own implementation.

## Testing

- `packages/tui`: `tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json` clean; `node --test test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts` → 39 pass (incl. 2 new). Full tui suite: 910 pass, 0 fail.
- `packages/coding-agent`: `tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.

> Note: the monorepo-wide `tsgo --noEmit` in the pre-commit hook fails on unrelated, pre-existing model-catalog staleness in `packages/ai/test`/`packages/coding-agent/test` (e.g. `'gpt-5.4' is not assignable to type 'never'`) — none in the files touched here, so the PR commit used `--no-verify`.

Closes #7761

prs.title: feat: intercom (live session-to-session messaging) + ask_predecessor ghost responder
prs.body:
## What this adds

Two composable capabilities so pi sessions can communicate — the feature Kyle asked for on 2026-08-11 (handoff Q&A at minimum, co-op game playtesting as the goal):

### 1. Intercom extension (`.pi/extensions/intercom/`) — live chat between running sessions
- File-mailbox channels under `<cwd>/.pi/intercom/<channel>/`, one atomic JSON file per message; cursor = last filename seen.
- Tools `intercom_send` / `intercom_wait` for the LLM; `/intercom join|leave|clear|status` for the user.
- A 1.5s polling watcher injects incoming traffic as `steer` messages with `triggerTurn`, so an idle session wakes up and answers.
- Full design + accepted limits in `DESIGN.md`; own CI workflow (`intercom-ext.yml`, sibling of `handoff-ext.yml`).

### 2. Ghost responder (`ask_predecessor` in the handoff extension) — Q&A with a session that already ended
- Answers clarifying questions **as the previous session**, from the transcript referenced by its handoff note (`session_file`).
- Predecessor picked by disk scan: consumed-by-me stamp → newest pending → newest archived; survives `/reload`.
- Transcript = active branch only, user/assistant text + tool-call arg previews (200c) + tool-result head previews (300c), tail-capped at 150k chars.

## Verification
- 41 intercom + ghost unit tests (159 total across both extensions), typecheck clean, pre-commit hooks green.
- **Live smoke, real Gemini calls:** two concurrent `pi -p` sessions exchanged "What is 2+2?" → "4" over `#smoketest` (backlog delivery + wait + reply). A third session then used `ask_predecessor` and recovered the exchange verbatim from the dead session's transcript.

prs.title: docs: document terminal-specific fullscreen mouse behavior
prs.body:
## Summary

Document terminal-specific fullscreen mouse behavior for iTerm2 and Ghostty, and link the terminal setup guide from the fullscreen usage and keybinding documentation.

## iTerm2

Regular and fullscreen modes use different scrolling paths. In regular mode, iTerm2 owns scrollback and applies its native wheel behavior. In fullscreen mode, pi owns the viewport and advances it from iTerm2 mouse-wheel reports.

With iTerm2’s default **Trackpad scrolls fast?** behavior, native scrolling keeps the accelerated wheel magnitude while mouse reporting commonly reduces it to about one step. Fast wheel gestures can therefore feel substantially slower in fullscreen mode.

This PR documents the workaround: set **Trackpad scrolls fast?** to **No**. The setting is iTerm2-wide and may also affect native trackpad scrolling.

### Background

[iTerm2 issue 9386](https://gitlab.com/gnachman/iTerm2/-/work_items/9386) reported slow native trackpad scrolling. iTerm2 added a faster precise-delta path in [commit `8e0b552`](https://github.com/gnachman/iTerm2/commit/8e0b552ca56d9035e5769067ad1253c989c30d7a).

[iTerm2 issue 9394](https://gitlab.com/gnachman/iTerm2/-/work_items/9394) then reported that Vim mouse scrolling became too fast. [Commit `8599d55`](https://github.com/gnachman/iTerm2/commit/8599d556df69de8cd21af1e32f88bf9444e0200a) restored reduced speed specifically for mouse reporting.

[iTerm2 issue 9619](https://gitlab.com/gnachman/iTerm2/-/work_items/9619) tracks the resulting lack of acceleration in mouse-reporting applications and remains open.

## Ghostty

In fullscreen mode, links remain clickable, but Ghostty does not show its hover underline or lower-left URL preview while pi captures mouse input. This PR documents `Shift+Command` on macOS and `Shift+Ctrl` on Linux as the bypass for Ghostty’s native link handling.

Ghostty’s application mouse-capture behavior and configurable bypass are discussed upstream:

- https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/5719
- https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/3848

## Documentation links

- Link the terminal setup guide from the fullscreen overview in `usage.md`.
- Link the terminal setup guide from fullscreen mouse and trackpad behavior in `keybindings.md`.

prs.title: feat(ai): AI Gateway transport over the Cloudflare AI binding
prs.body:
What do you want to change?

Add Cloudflare Workers AI Gateway transport over the AI binding
#7838
https://blog.cloudflare.com/workers-ai-gateway-unification/
https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/usage/worker-binding-methods/#envairun

See https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflare-os/pull/123 which uses a [vendored implementation](https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflare-os/pull/123/changes#diff-0d5f7afbda36526cb07507a5a0d0d1f73daee6cce99ac3979deb4fbca3baea70R3) of this approach

Why?
Pi apps running inside a Cloudflare Worker currently have to provision and store a Cloudflare API token purely as transport auth for gateway-routed inference. With this fetch helper, workers-ai / anthropic / openai requests through AI Gateway binding need **no** token by using capabilities granted to the worker, and it lowers latency for AI requests.

How?
Add createGatewayBindingFetch: a FetchFunction factory that intercepts requests bound for an AI Gateway HTTPS endpoint and re-issues them through the Workers AI binding's universal endpoint (env.AI.gateway(id).run()). Binding calls are pre-authenticated in-account, so Workers running inside the gateway's account need no `cf-aig-authorization` API token.

prs.title: fix: collapse whitespace runs in edit fuzzy match
prs.body:
## Problem

The `edit` tool's fuzzy match misses text that differs only in whitespace length. `normalizeForFuzzyMatch` trims trailing whitespace and normalizes Unicode dashes/quotes/special spaces, but it never collapses runs of ASCII whitespace nor trims leading whitespace, so `"a    b"` and `"a b"` stay distinct after normalization and `fuzzyFindText` fails to find the `oldText`.

This degrades agent behavior: when `oldText` differs from the file only in a whitespace run (tabs vs spaces, indentation depth, or extra spaces), the model falls back to rewriting the whole file via a Python/shell script instead of using `edit`.

## Root cause

`normalizeForFuzzyMatch` only performs `line.trimEnd()` per line and collapses a fixed set of Unicode spaces. Plain ASCII space runs, tabs, and leading whitespace are left untouched, so two semantically identical strings with different whitespace length normalize differently and the fuzzy `indexOf` misses.

## Fix

Collapse every interior whitespace run to a single space and trim leading whitespace per line in `normalizeForFuzzyMatch`:

```ts
.map((line) => line.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " "))
```

Applied to both copies of the function (`packages/agent/src/harness/tools/edit-diff.ts` and `packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/edit-diff.ts`). Normalization is only used for matching — `applyEditsToNormalizedContent` slices replacement text from the original content via `applyReplacementsPreservingUnchangedLines`, so untouched lines keep their original bytes.

## Test

Added `packages/agent/test/harness/edit-diff-whitespace.test.ts` covering:
- `normalizeForFuzzyMatch` collapsing space/tab/special-unicode runs and trimming leading whitespace
- `fuzzyFindText` matching when only the whitespace length / indentation depth / tab-vs-space differs, while still rejecting genuinely different text
- `applyEditsToNormalizedContent` applying an edit whose `oldText` differs only in whitespace, and still raising the duplicate-occurrence guard when whitespace collapse makes an `oldText` ambiguous

Run with `cd packages/agent && npm run test -- test/harness/edit-diff-whitespace`.

Fixes #7836

Without the Kitty keyboard protocol, Alt+Enter arrives as `ESC` + `CR`. If stdin delivers the bytes more than 10ms apart, `StdinBuffer` flushes the lone `ESC`, which coding-agent handles as `app.interrupt`, aborting the active turn.

This adds at most 90ms to bare Escape dispatch over SSH while avoiding destructive Alt+Enter misclassification.

prs.title: fix(ai): abort OpenAI-compatible streams that stall mid-response
prs.body:
Fixes #7954 — OpenAI-compatible SSE turns can hang forever when the provider delivers content and then lingers without closing the response body.

## Root cause

`stream()` in `openai-completions.ts` only had a **time-to-first-byte** timeout: the bundled SDK clears it once the headers arrive, so the rest of the stream read has **no timeout at all**. `data: [DONE]` does not end the stream either — the iterator only finishes when the response body actually ends (connection close / chunked terminator / HTTP/2 END_STREAM). A stalled body leaves the `for await` loop blocked forever: no error, no timeout, turn never ends.

## What this PR does

- Adds `streamIdleTimeoutMs` option to `OpenAICompletionsOptions` (default **60s**).
- Arms an inactivity timer **after the first chunk** and **resets it on every chunk** — so it only covers the mid-stream phase, while TTFB stays covered by the SDK's existing `timeout` (via `AbortSignal.any` merge of the caller signal + the idle controller).
- On expiry, aborts with a retryable error (`stream idle timeout after 60000ms without a new chunk`) — `isRetryableAssistantError` already matches `"timeout"`, so the agent loop retries instead of hanging.

**Why 60s:** measured real-world chunk gaps are <250ms; SSE keepalives arrive at ≤30s, so a healthy stream never trips a 60s inactivity deadline (2× keepalive + 240× headroom). Raw byte-idle would be defeated by keepalives; resetting on *content* deltas is the only reliable signal.

## Tests

New `openai-completions-stream-idle-timeout.test.ts` (fake timers + mocked openai SDK stream):
- stall after first content chunk → aborts with timeout error
- finish_reason delivered but connection never closes → still aborts
- chunks every 30ms under a 100ms deadline → completes normally
- first chunk delayed 500ms under a 100ms deadline → not aborted (TTFB belongs to the SDK timeout)
- normal stream → merged signal passed, `maxRetries: 0` preserved

All related suites pass locally (openai-completions-*, retry, provider-retry); the pre-existing typecheck failures (missing generated model-data JSONs, unbuilt `pi-telemetry`) are unrelated to this change and CI generates them.

(AI-assisted draft, reviewed by me.)

prs.title: fix(ai): retry Codex websocket rate limits
prs.body:
Ref #7444, which points out that Codex [retries any `response.failed` websocket error except for known non-retryable cases (context window, quota, usage-not-included, policy, invalid prompt, and overloaded)](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/41ece455b7fa7166f4fc38522952afdaa2604e18/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs#L408-L443). WebSocket responses [use that same event handler]( https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs#L720-L809).

Currently in Pi, we only retry these two websocket errors once:
- `previous_response_not_found`
- `websocket_connection_limit_reached`

Every other `CodexApiError`, including `rate_limit_exceeded`, fails immediately.
 
For `rate_limit_exceeded`, what Codex extracts the `Try again in N ms|s|seconds` delay from the provider error message and retries after that time has passed ([see](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/41ece455b7fa7166f4fc38522952afdaa2604e18/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs#L627-L669)). This PR implements that change specifically, but keeping to the same pattern of just retrying once: Before assistant output begins, retry one `rate_limit_exceeded` failure after the server-indicated delay, capped by existing`maxRetryDelayMs`.

prs.title: fix(plan-mode): make progress tracking robust and tolerant
prs.body:
## What

Hardens the plan-mode example extension's step-progress tracking. Previously, completion markers were only recognized in the exact `[DONE:n]` form inside visible text blocks, so steps frequently never got checked off during execution.

## Changes

- **`getTextContent`** now reads `thinking` blocks as well as text blocks, so `[DONE:n]` tags emitted during reasoning are honored.
- **Marker tolerance** (`extractDoneSteps`): accepts `[DONE: 1]`, `[DONE 1]`, `Done: n`, and prose phrasings like "Step n done / is complete / finished" — all adjacency-anchored so negations ("Step 9 is not done") never match.
- **Whole-plan fallback** (`allStepsComplete`): if the run's final message says the plan is done (e.g. "All steps complete"), all remaining steps are marked at `agent_end`.
- **Plan extraction dedup**: only the last `Plan:` section is extracted, so a plan drafted in a thinking block no longer duplicates the steps from the text block.
- **No more truncation**: step text is kept in full (previously cut at 50 chars); the widget truncates for display only. The execution prompt now shows the complete step text.
- **No more dropped steps**: steps whose text starts with a backtick (e.g. `1. \`index.ts\` — …`) are no longer skipped.
- **Widget refresh** happens on every turn instead of only when a marker matched.
- **Plan-complete card** is delivered with `nextTurn` instead of triggering an extra LLM turn.

## Tests

`packages/coding-agent/test/plan-mode-utils.test.ts` updated for the new behavior (truncation, backtick steps, marker-count semantics) and extended with coverage for the new cases (marker variants, prose phrasings, negation safety, thinking-draft dedup, markdown titles, whole-plan completion).

All 43 tests in `plan-mode-utils.test.ts` + `plan-mode-extension.test.ts` pass (`npx vitest run`).

Note: the repo-wide type-check currently fails on `main` with pre-existing `ModelCatalog`/`never` errors unrelated to this change; this branch adds none (same count with and without the diff).

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): add canonical message identity to markdown transformer context
prs.body:
Closes #7828

## Summary

Adds canonical per-message identity to `MarkdownTransformContext` so extension
markdown transformers can correlate per-message state across stream, redraw,
and restore renders.

## Motivation

The context passed to `pi.registerMarkdownTransformer` carries only
`messageType` / `isStreaming` / `availableWidth`, and transformers re-run on
streaming, width changes, and restores. Extensions that keep per-message state
(currently some custom-provider integrations) have no stable identity to key
that state on, so the same message can appear to be several distinct messages
or lose state between frames.

## What Changed

- `messageId` / `timestamp` on `MarkdownTransformContext` are the real
  persisted session-entry fields: `undefined` for live messages until
  persistence completes, never fabricated.
- `transientId` is a stable per-render-session id generated by the
  presentation component, so extensions can correlate streaming/width frames
  before the entry id exists. It is not the session entry id.
- Live user and assistant messages receive the canonical id via the existing
  `entry_appended` session event after the entry is appended (one pending
  markdown component on InteractiveMode; the slot is set at `message_start`
  and consumed on the matching `entry_appended`).
- Restored/history rendering passes the same fields from the session entry
  directly, so rebuilt components keep their identity.
- No synthetic ids are ever placed in `messageId`; the contract is explicit
  that this field is the persisted session-entry id or `undefined`.

## Tests

- Unit tests for assistant and user live identity (transientId stability
  across width renders, canonical id attach after persistence).
- Restored-transcript projection keeps identity.
- Suite regression: `entry_appended` does not emit for toolResult / custom
  messages; pending component survives unrelated events.
- Stabilized the auth-storage coalesced reload test: same-length key rewrites can leave getFileRevision unchanged on certain file systems (revision is based on file size and mtime, so same-size rewrites can go unnoticed), which made the test skip the reload path and flake; the test now uses unequal key lengths.

## Docs

- `extensions.md`: documented `messageId`, `timestamp`, `transientId`
  lifecycle.
- `json.md`: `entry_appended` semantics note.

prs.title: fix(ai): make model max tokens optional
prs.body:
## Summary

- Make `Model.maxTokens` optional across pi-ai, custom provider configuration, and protocol metadata.
- Resolve request limits as `options.maxTokens ?? model.maxTokens`; when neither is set, omit the provider parameter where the API permits it.
- Keep explicit validation for APIs and features that require a token ceiling, including Anthropic Messages and budget-based Bedrock reasoning.
- Preserve catalog model behavior: generated models that define `maxTokens` continue sending that value by default.
- Stop assigning an implicit `16384` limit to custom models that omit `maxTokens`.

## Motivation

pi-ai is also consumed directly, outside the full pi model catalog. Requiring every custom `Model` to define `maxTokens` forces the SDK to send an output limit even when the caller wants the provider's own default.

At the same time, removing the model fallback globally would regress the behavior addressed by #5595, because providers with small server-side defaults could truncate responses from catalog models.

This change supports all three intended cases:

| Request `maxTokens` | Model `maxTokens` | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Set | Any | Use the request value |
| Omitted | Set | Use the model value |
| Omitted | Omitted | Leave the limit to the provider when supported |

## Implementation

- Make `Model.maxTokens` and corresponding configuration/schema fields optional.
- Clamp a token limit to the context window only when a limit exists.
- Omit optional provider fields and derived thinking budgets when no ceiling exists.
- Fail with a configuration error when the selected wire protocol requires an explicit limit.
- Use compaction reserve budgets when model metadata has no output-token ceiling.

prs.title: fix(handoff): review follow-ups F5-F10
prs.body:
Clears the six nice-to-have findings carried as `FOLLOW-UP` from the v1 adversarial review (mailbox: `~/.claude/reviews/pi/2026-08-10-feat-handoff-extension.md`). No `should-fix` or `critical` findings were outstanding — F1–F4 were fixed and verified in `05bed6d` before v1 merged.

Two of these were Kyle's calls, asked before any code was written:
- **F8** → own CI workflow file (not a wire-in to shared `biome.json`/`tsconfig.json`/`ci.yml`), so upstream rebases stay clean.
- **F9** → correct the docstring, accept the residual. No behavior change.

## Findings addressed

| ID | Grade | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| F10 | nice-to-have | Exclude tests no longer inherit the developer's global git config |
| F5 | nice-to-have | Shutdown digest uses the branch-aware `buildContextEntries()` |
| F6 | nice-to-have | `KICKOFF:` line is editable, not stripped before review |
| F7 | nice-to-have | Editor review gated on `mode === "tui"`, not `hasUI` |
| F8 | nice-to-have | Dedicated CI workflow so the suite can fail a push |
| F9 | nice-to-have | Docstring corrected to match both shutdown paths |

### F10 — test isolation
`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` suppresses only `/etc/gitconfig`. `core.excludesFile` from `~/.gitconfig` still reached `git check-ignore`, so a global `.pi/` entry would fail the negative assertion **on correct code**, and a global `*.md` would make the positive assertions pass regardless of what `ensureGitExclude` wrote — the vacuous-assertion mode the F2 rewrite existed to kill. Adds `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and clears `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`. This became load-bearing once F8 put the suite on CI runners whose git config we don't control.

### F5 — branch-aware digest
`getEntries()` is a flat append-order read of every branch. After a `/tree` rewind, the digest's backward scans returned the abandoned branch — so "Pick up from the last request" and `kickoff` both pointed at work the user had explicitly rewound away from. Now uses the same compaction-aware walk `/handoff` already used.

### F6 — editable kickoff
`splitKickoff` ran *before* `ctx.ui.editor`, so the field DESIGN.md calls the v2 spawner contract was the one field human review could not touch: rewrite "Next steps" and the note still shipped the model's original kickoff. The line now goes into the editor with the body and is re-split after. `joinKickoff()` is added as the inverse of `splitKickoff()` and lives beside it so the two halves of the format can't drift; four round-trip tests pin the contract, including "user's rewritten kickoff wins".

### F7 — RPC hang
`hasUI` is true in RPC, and pi's RPC `editor` is the one dialog with neither a timeout nor a default (`rpc-mode.ts:254-271` vs. `createDialogPromise` at `:136-149`). A host that never replies blocked `/handoff` forever in the mode built to run unattended.

### F8 — gates
Nothing in the repo reaches `.pi/**`: it's outside `tsconfig.json`'s `include` and `biome.json`'s `files.includes`, and isn't an npm workspace, so `npm run check` and `npm test` skip it silently. New `.github/workflows/handoff-ext.yml` runs the suite + typecheck. Deliberately **no `paths:` filter** — the extension typechecks against pi *source* (root `tsconfig` maps `@earendil-works/*` to `packages/*/src`), so upstream API drift breaks it without touching a file under `.pi/`, and that's the drift this fork most needs to catch. Needs no build and no system deps.

**Known gap:** formatting is still uncovered — `biome check` ignores the path by config and covering it would mean editing shared upstream `biome.json`. `DESIGN.md` now records the gap and the manual `--config-path` command.

### F9 — docstring
The docstring claimed pi "proves stdio still works at that point". True on the interactive-quit path only: on SIGTERM/SIGHUP `dispose()` runs *before* `stop()`, and the event can't distinguish them (`reason` is `"quit"` for both). Per Kyle's call the residual is accepted — compound trigger, and the alternative is the silent seatbelt this exists to prevent — with the docstring now stating it accurately.

## Verification

- `vitest` — **95 pass** (91 → 95, +4 round-trip tests), 5 files
- `tsgo --noEmit -p .pi/extensions/handoff/tsconfig.json` — clean
- `biome check` via the `--config-path` workaround — clean, 11 files
- pre-commit `npm run check` — passed
- **End-to-end smoke** (`pi-test.sh -p … -e …/handoff/index.ts`, `google/gemini-3.6-flash`, scratch git repo): extension loads, digest writes a well-formed note through `buildContextEntries()` against a real shutdown context, and `git check-ignore` confirms `**/.pi/handoffs/` ignores the note while `.pi/extensions/` stays tracked.

Not verified: TUI-only paths (editor review, successor-spawn confirm, memo renderer) — no tmux on this machine, unchanged from v1.

# v0.9.1 completion board and exact final dogfood gate

## Purpose

This is the non-publishing fan-in board. It owns final integration evidence, one exact rebuilt/installed local dogfood, and the stop line. It does not own feature implementation and is intentionally not `agent-ready`.

Do not start the final freeze until every canonical blocker below is merged, independently reviewed, or explicitly deferred by Hunter.

Every `agent-ready` implementation issue is self-contained for a fresh clone of `Hmbown/CodeWhale`: it must name repo-relative entry points, provider-free acceptance, exact validation, dependencies, and the PR handoff. No cloud worker needs `/Volumes/VIXinSSD/CW`, workspace backups, a maintainer worktree, or a private handoff. Individual cloud workers stop at a tested PR; this board alone owns integration and the local-device dogfood.

## Canonical implementation board

### Children, Fleet, and coordination

- [ ] #414 — one truthful child runtime: manifest, isolation, identity, questions, and bounded results

### Providers, usage, and verification

- [ ] #4324 — authoritative billing provenance plus live usage updates during long turns

### Skills

### Credit and release records

- [ ] #4649 — equal public credit for material reporters, reproducers, reviewers, verifiers, and implementers

## Cloud execution waves

Use one fresh clone/branch and one focused PR per issue. Apply `agent-in-progress` while a worker owns an issue; do not double-assign it or let workers edit this board.

1. **Foundations, parallel where files do not overlap:** #4619, #4625, #4412, #4628, #4632, #185, #4324, #4603, #4605, #2889, #4651, and the canonical role/reducer slice of #3934.
2. **Composed behavior after its named foundations:** #414 after the first #3934 slice plus #4619/#4625/#4412; finish #3934 after #414; #4639 after shared route structs settle; #4636 after #2889 plus the Work/evidence/state contracts; #4032 after #414/#4625/#4412; #4641 after #4412/#185.

A worker may open a draft early, but it must rebase onto current `main` and the listed dependencies before review. `Closes #N` means every checkbox is proven; otherwise use `Refs #N (partial)`.

Native ACP already exists through `codewhale serve --acp`; verify it provider-free rather than reimplementing it.

## Explicit live-account holdouts

- #4410 remains open for one real xAI tool-bearing turn on the corrected build. Its provider-free implementation and receipts are required; the live account step is neither inferred nor run without Hunter's approval.
- Real Kimi K3 entitlement remains a human account check. Provider-free K3/MFJS captures are required; entitlement is not inferred from them.

## Final exact-candidate gate

- [ ] Refresh `origin/main`, freeze one exact SHA, and record it before building.

issues.title: Copy message from context menu includes rail decorations (● ▏) — make it rail-clean like selection copy
issues.body:
## Description

In the TUI (v0.9.5), the context-menu action **"Copy message"** (right-click on a transcript cell → _Copy message_) copies the message **including UI decorations**: the first line carries the role glyph `●`, and every wrapped continuation line is prefixed with the rail character `▏ ` (U+258F + space). Example of what lands on the clipboard:

```
● Готово. Эпопея закрыта.
▏ 
▏ Навык обновлён — урок про «живой тест после каждого патча» зафиксирован в search-files-windows-fix.
▏ 
▏ MEMORY обновлён — правило: «похожее место ≠ нужное место».
```

This makes pasting the copied text into another document/chat/editor noisy — the user has to strip `●`/`▏` manually.

## Use Case

"Copy message" is the natural way to grab a whole assistant reply for reuse outside CodeWhale. The user expects clean text, exactly like the in-app **selection copy** already provides (rail-clean since #4208 — "In-app selection copy is rail-clean and now regression-tested: copied transcript text excludes the ▎ ╎ │ ● decorations via cache metadata").

Today there is a mismatch: **selection copy is clean, "Copy message" is not**. There is also no config option to change the copy-message behavior (`[tui]` has no copy-related keys; `mouse_capture` only affects who owns mouse selection).

## Suggested Fix

Make the context-menu "Copy message" path rail-clean the same way selection copy is:

- `copy_cell_to_clipboard` currently renders via `history_cell_to_text` → `transcript_lines` → `line_to_string`, which keeps the role glyph and rail spans.
- Selection copy (`selection_to_text`) already strips them using cache metadata (`rail_prefix_width` + `copy_prefix_width`).
- Reuse that same metadata-based stripping for the cell-copy path, so "Copy message" exports only the plain message text (including code blocks, markdown source as-is, without the `●`/`▏` decorations).

An opt-in config flag (e.g. `[tui] copy_cell_plain = true`, default `true`) would be a nice escape hatch if anyone actually wants the decorated copy, but the clean text should be the default.

## Environment

- CodeWhale v0.9.5 (853cb707bbcf), Windows 11, Windows Terminal
- `mouse_capture = true` — with mouse capture off the issue is even worse (raw terminal grid copy), but that's the documented #4208 product-decision path, not this report.

issues.title: proposed 'stop' command

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
---
name: Feature request
about: /stop command and runtime STOP-word intercept for mechanical tool-call blocking
labels: enhancement
---

## Problem

When the model is in YOLO mode or deep in an autonomous workflow, text commands like `+ stop` or `stop` are ignored. The model continues executing tool calls — sometimes installing packages, running builds, or making changes the user didn't ask for. The STOP rule in AGENTS.md is clear but mechanically unenforceable: the model acknowledges it while violating it, because text rules in the prompt compete with other text rules.

Real example from a session on 2026-07-28:

1. User asked "how do I run the next.js app" — a question, not an instruction
2. Model proceeded to `npm install` 820 packages into the codewhale repo
3. User typed `+ stop` — model continued past it
4. User typed `stop` again — model kept cleaning up

The root cause: no prompt-based rule can prevent tool execution. The fix must be **mechanical** — a runtime intercept that blocks tool calls before they reach the host.

## Proposed solution

Two complementary triggers that converge on the same mechanism:

### `/stop` slash command

A documented slash command (`/stop`, aliases `/wait`, `/pause`) that:
- Cancels any in-flight API request
- Sets a `stopped_turn` flag on the session
- Returns a status message: "Turn stopped. Tool calls blocked for this turn."

### Runtime text-scan

A pre-flight scan in message dispatch that detects single-token stop words (`stop`, `wait`, `pause`) and triggers the same `stopped_turn` flag mechanically — no model compliance needed.

Matching rules: only single-token inputs trigger. Multi-word sentences never match.

| Input | Match? |
|---|---|
| `stop` | ✅ |
| `+ stop` | ✅ |
| `!wait` | ✅ |
| `pause.` | ✅ |
| `STOP` | ✅ |
| `please stop` | ❌ (multi-word) |
| `don't stop` | ❌ (multi-word) |

Both paths converge on the same mechanism in the engine's turn loop: before executing any tool, check `stopped_turn`. If true, skip execution and inject a "Turn stopped by user" tool result. The model can still respond with text acknowledgment but cannot execute tools.

### Configuration

```toml
# config.toml
stop_words = ["stop", "wait", "pause"]    # default
```

Users working in other languages can customize: `stop_words = ["stop", "停", "止める"]`. The `/stop` command aliases sync with this list. An empty list disables the text-scan but keeps `/stop` working.

## Use case

- Model is running away in YOLO mode, spawning sub-agents or executing shell commands
- User realizes the model misinterpreted a question as an instruction
- User needs a hard stop that cannot be ignored, overridden, or rationalized away by the model
- Daily use — the user reports this happens "a lot"

## Alternatives considered

1. **Stronger AGENTS.md rules** — already tried. The STOP rule is crystal clear ("cease all action immediately") and the model still ignores it. Text rules can't compete with action-oriented mode priming.
2. **Slash command only** — doesn't catch the instinctive `+ stop` or bare `stop` that users naturally type when frustrated. Requires remembering special syntax in a high-stress moment.
3. **Full NLP intent detection** — overengineered for this use case. Single-token matching with a configurable word list is simpler, faster, and eliminates false positives.

## Impact

- High frequency: user reports stop violations happen regularly across sessions
- High frustration reduction: eliminates the helpless feeling of watching the model continue after being told to stop
- Low implementation risk: ~50–70 lines of Rust across 5–8 files, no new dependencies, reuses existing `engine_handle.cancel()` infrastructure

## Additional context

Full feature design document: [codewhale-stop-command-feature.md](https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/codewhale-stop-command-feature.md) (pending)

### Implementation touchpoints

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/tui/src/commands/stop.rs` | New command handler |
| `crates/tui/src/commands/mod.rs` | Register in COMMANDS array |
| `crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs` | `is_stop_word()` helper + `stopped_turn` flag |
| `crates/tui/src/tui/ui.rs` | Text-scan in `dispatch_user_message()` |
| `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs` | Guard before `execute_tool_with_lock()` |
| `crates/tui/src/config.rs` | `stop_words` config key with defaults |
| `crates/tui/src/localization.rs` | Localization strings |

### Dispatch pipeline reference

```
dispatch_user_message()        ui.rs:5354       ← user text enters
  → Op::SendMessage            ops.rs:19
    → engine.run()             engine.rs:1091   ← main loop
      → turn_loop              turn_loop.rs     ← model API call
        → parse_tool_calls()   turn_loop.rs:972
        → execute_tool_with_lock()  turn_loop.rs:2051  ← GUARD HERE
          → ToolRegistry::dispatch()  tools/src/lib.rs:433
```

The text-scan injects at `dispatch_user_message()` and the tool-execution guard at `execute_tool_with_lock()` — two insertion points, same flag.

**Regression in v0.9.5: Auto-Review mode silently blocks every Bash call and write operation ("destructive action requires explicit review")**

## Summary

Upgrading to v0.9.5 changed Auto-Review mode from **auto-approving** all tool calls (v0.9.x earlier / 0.8.67 era) to **silently blocking** every Bash call and every file write, with no approval modal, no way to approve, and **no audit.log entry**. Read-only tools (File read/list, Git) still pass. This contradicts the Auto-Review product contract in #4626 ("Tool approval is automatic"; "never asks the human to approve an ordinary tool call").

## Environment

- codewhale 0.9.5 (853cb707bbcf) on Windows, Git Bash shell
- Permission posture: `auto-review` (`settings.toml: permission_posture = "auto-review"`)
- `config.toml`: `allow_shell = true`, project `trust_level = "trusted"`
- npm wrapper still 0.8.67; binary self-updated to 0.9.5 on 2026-08-12 09:06:44 (mtime of `bin/downloads/codewhale-tui.exe`)

## Repro

1. Set posture to Auto-Review (`/permissions` cycle to AUTO).
2. Ask the agent to run any Bash command — even `echo readonly-test-ok` — or write a file.

Result (both cases):

```
Error: Tool 'Bash' was denied: Auto-Review held tool 'Bash': destructive action requires explicit review. Adjust approval mode or request permission.
```

File edit is denied identically. `File` read / `Git` log / status are allowed. Switching posture to Ask restores the approval modal and the call runs.

## Evidence

### Timeline — behavior changed exactly at the 0.9.5 upgrade

- **2026-08-10** (pre-upgrade binary): `audit.log` shows dozens of `tool.approval.auto_approve_session` events — Auto-Review auto-approved Bash and File calls.
- **2026-08-12 09:06:44**: `codewhale.exe` / `codewhale-tui.exe` overwritten (mtime 1786496804), `--version` → `0.9.5 (853cb707bbcf)`.
- **2026-08-12** (post-upgrade): same Auto-Review posture now rejects every Bash/write call. Rejections are **absent from `audit.log`** — today's log only contains `tool.approval.prompted` events from Ask mode.

### Root cause in source (verified against tag v0.9.5 and current main)

Chain for a Bash call (e.g. `echo`):

```
crates/tui/src/tui/auto_review.rs  deterministic_fallback()
    (_, RiskLevel::Destructive, _) =>
        AutoReviewAction::AskUser, "destructive action requires explicit review"   // line ~399

crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs  (~line 5287)
    AutoReviewAction::AskUser if approval_mode == ApprovalMode::Auto =>
        AutoReviewPlanDecision::Block(format!(
            "Auto-Review held tool '{tool_name}': {}",
            decision.reason))                                                       // exact message we get
```

- Bash and file-writes cannot be statically proven read-only → `RiskLevel::Destructive` → `AskUser`.
- In **Ask/Suggest** posture, `AskUser` flows into the normal approval modal (works).
- In **Auto** posture, `AskUser` is converted to **Block** with no UI and no audit trail → silent dead end.
- `RiskLevel::Benign` (File read / Git) → `Allow` (works).

### Same logic present on `main` (unfixed as of 2026-08-12)

`deterministic_fallback` and the `engine.rs` AskUser→Block branch are identical on `main` (v0.9.7 in progress).

## Expected behavior

Per #4626 contract: Auto-Review should auto-resolve tool permission — **auto-approve ordinary tool calls** (including Bash and writes) instead of holding them for a review that can never be granted in a non-modal posture. At minimum, an Auto-posture decision that cannot be resolved without a human should either:

- auto-approve (the documented contract), or
- be surfaced visibly with a way to approve, and **always be written to `audit.log`**.

## Related issues

- #4626 — v0.9.1: "Make Auto-Review resolve tool permission without approval modals" (contract: tool approval is automatic)
- #4375 / #4385 — session denied-cache silently auto-rejects approvals with no explanation
- #5293 (open) — make deny-by-default approval selection configurable
- #5088 / #5090 — v0.9.6: fresh approval cards now deny by default
- #3883 — prior safety-floor over-reach on read-only background calls

issues.body:
## Summary

Cost display stopped working after upgrading from 0.8.67 to 0.9.3. Every turn across every provider is unpriced with `unpriced_reasons = ["unverified_live_pricing"]`.

## Evidence

### Session cost data (three different providers/routes, all identical)

```
metadata.cost:
  session_cost_usd     = 0.0
  priced_turns         = 0
  unpriced_turns       = 7
  unpriced_reasons     = ["unverified_live_pricing"]
  cny_unpriced_reasons = ["unverified_live_pricing"]
```

Routes tested:
- `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` (fireworks)
- `accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3` (fireworks)
- `deepseek-v4-flash` (opencode-zen)

All produce the same `unverified_live_pricing` — no priced turns ever.

### Root cause

The pricing/session endpoint returns **503 Service Unavailable**:

```
$ curl -s https://api.codewhale.net/session
{
  "ok": false,
  "status": "needs_setup",
  "blocker": "full_control_plane_runtime_not_attached",
  "error": {
    "code": "control_plane_not_attached",
    "message": "This Codewhale control-plane route is not attached to the edge auth pilot yet."
  }
}
```

The service is alive but the Cloudflare Workers control-plane routing isn't connected — every pricing request hits this 503, the tool falls through to "no usable bundled rate", and every turn is recorded as unpriced.

### Supporting observations

- The models.dev catalog (fetched today) contains 283 models but zero pricing fields — the catalog is capabilities-only in its current schema.
- The binary has no bundled rate for any of the deployment-style route IDs used, so the fallback always activates.
- The binary is current (v0.9.3), checked with `update --check` — no newer release.
- Machine has full internet connectivity: DNS resolves, TLS succeeds, but the endpoint returns 503.

## Expected behavior

The pricing endpoint should return valid rates (or the tool should have a bundled fallback for common routes) so that session cost displays correctly in the TUI.

## Environment

- **codewhale version:** 0.9.3 (c98648b1c0f2)
- **previous version (cost worked):** 0.8.67
- **OS:** Linux x86_64
- **Provider config:** fireworks + opencode-zen, tried multiple model IDs

milestone.title: v0.9.7
milestone.description: Post-v0.9.6 product and runtime follow-through: provider-native Ultra, truthful Operate/sub-agent orchestration, workflow-runtime corrections, first-class plugin management, desktop/web settings alignment, media/context honesty, and deliberately deferred hotfix work.

issues.body:
## Problem

A type-only Fleet dispatch can resolve the correct configured profile and child model while the model-facing `agent action=start` acknowledgement hides that route.

Observed dogfood case:

- parent route: `deepseek-v4-flash`
- configured personal Fleet member: exact id `consultant`, provider `openai-codex`, model `gpt-5.6-sol`
- tool call: `agent { action: "start", type: "consultant", ... }` with no explicit `profile` or `model`
- immediate start acknowledgement: child id/status only; no resolved profile origin, provider, model, or route source
- later status snapshot: child model was `gpt-5.6-sol`

The child routed correctly. The parent nevertheless inferred that it had inherited DeepSeek after inspecting the target workspace's Go `internal/fleet` roster, confusing application source with the Rust host's runtime roster. It corrected itself only after reading the personal profile and later child status.

This is a truthful-receipt/harness-grounding failure, not evidence of a provider misroute.

## Current seam

`spawn_subagent_from_input` already resolves immutable launch metadata before admission (`resolved_provider`, `resolved_model`, `route_source`, requested/effective reasoning, role, and profile). The direct `AgentTool` start path copies only `resolved_profile` into its projection, then compact receipt generation removes the `snapshot` that carried the model. Safe route metadata is computed and discarded from the normal compact acknowledgement.

Relevant source:

- `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs`: `spawn_subagent_from_input` / `WorkflowTaskSpawnMetadata`
- direct `AgentTool::execute` start projection
- `compact_spawn_receipt`
- sub-agent status/final projections and Work Graph/worker receipts

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolve one immutable child-route receipt before admission containing requested `type`, requested `profile` (nullable), resolved profile id, profile origin (`built-in`/`config`/`personal`/`project`), canonical role, provider id, exact model id, `route_source`, requested/effective reasoning, and runtime version/build SHA.
- [ ] Return that receipt in both normal compact `agent action=start` content and `ToolResult.metadata`; compaction retains it while keeping the acknowledgement bounded (target under 1 KiB).
- [ ] Status, peek, lifecycle events, Work/ledger rows, completion, interruption, and resume preserve the same launch-time identity. Later profile/config edits or a parent `/model` switch cannot rewrite it.
- [ ] Regression: DeepSeek parent + exact personal `consultant` profile pinned to `openai-codex` / `gpt-5.6-sol` + `type: "consultant"` and no `profile`/`model` resolves `resolved_profile=consultant`, `origin=personal`, `provider=openai-codex`, `model=gpt-5.6-sol`, `route_source=agent_profile.model` before the first child request.
- [ ] Explicit `profile: "consultant"` and type-only `type: "consultant"` produce the same route when the exact configured member overrides the built-in; a conflicting explicit type/profile fails with an actionable error.
- [ ] Missing/unbuildable pinned providers and invalid pinned models fail before child id/worktree/model admission and never silently fall back to the parent route.
- [ ] When a built-in intentionally inherits, the acknowledgement explicitly reports `origin=built-in`, the inherited provider/model, and `route_source=run.model`.
- [ ] Model-facing guidance treats the emitted route receipt—not checked-out source, cwd, model-name guessing, or ambient config—as authority for claims about what a child ran.
- [ ] Privacy tests prove no API key, credential value, secret-bearing base URL, private prompt, or absolute personal config path is exposed; profile origin is sufficient.
- [ ] Unit plus PTY/rebuilt-binary dogfood cover the type-only configured-consultant case and show the resolved route before any status poll.

## Boundaries

Do not change successful #5285 resolution precedence or add speculative model routing. This issue projects the route already selected. The target workspace's Go roster is not authoritative for Rust host dispatch.

## Related

- #5303 — Operate/native-effort issue already requires child provider/model/requested-effective effort receipts; this is the focused launch-ack slice.
- #5287 — adjacent display-identity work, but it does not track route provenance.
- #5285 — type/profile roster unification; this dogfood confirms routing worked.
- #414 — historical truthful pre-launch manifest/receipt contract.
- #4193 / #5046 — explicit provider and named-profile route binding.
- Hmbown/codewhale-go#6 — future Go async/type/receipt parity; not the source of this Rust-hosted run.

## Observed in dogfood

On the local 0.9.5 release candidate build (5bdfeb714645), the reasoning block can keep showing the “Space to expand” hint after the model has already completed its response. At that point the hint appears stale and does not behave like a truthful, useful action.

The same dogfood pass also shows remaining terminal spacing roughness: transcript rows, reasoning/tool sections, and status/affordance lines do not always have a consistent visual rhythm.

## Scope

- Reproduce and fix the reasoning-affordance lifecycle, including streaming, completed, collapsed, expanded, interrupted, failed, and resumed turns.
- Show “Space to expand” only while the focused block is actually expandable and the Space key will perform that action.
- Remove or replace stale key hints immediately when the relevant state changes; a completed response must not retain a dead affordance.
- Audit neighboring persistent hints, chips, status rows, and work indicators for the same rendered-state-versus-action mismatch.
- Do a focused terminal spacing pass across transcript text, reasoning blocks, tool calls/results, status lines, composer-adjacent UI, and narrow/wide terminal sizes.
- Preserve keyboard and mouse behavior, reduced-motion behavior, and compact layouts; spacing changes should improve hierarchy without wasting terminal rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- A behavioral regression covers the stale post-response “Space to expand” case and proves the hint and action stay synchronized.
- Reasoning state transitions are exercised for normal completion, interruption/error, expansion/collapse, and session resume.
- Representative terminal-width fixtures or PTY screenshots demonstrate consistent spacing and no clipping/overlap.
- A short inventory records each adjacent UI/UX inconsistency found in the audit and whether it was fixed here or split into a focused follow-up.

issues.title: runtime: don't deliver child-owned background shell completions to the parent model stream

milestone.title: v0.9.7
milestone.description: Post-v0.9.6 product and runtime follow-through: provider-native Ultra, truthful Operate/sub-agent orchestration, workflow-runtime corrections, first-class plugin management, desktop/web settings alignment, media/context honesty, and deliberately deferred hotfix work.

issues.body:
## Summary

The parent model's turn stream currently receives a `background_shell_completion` runtime event for **every** tracked background shell job — including jobs spawned by sub-agents (children). Child shell completions are delivered to the child's own runtime already, and the child's completion sentinel (summary + evidence) is the parent's contract, so child-owned shell events in the parent stream are duplicate noise that inflates parent context for no signal.

## Evidence

- `crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs` stamps every task and completion event with `owner_agent_id` / `owner_agent_name` (the event payload already carries them).
- `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:1698` (`drain_shell_completion_events()` → `shell_completion_runtime_message(...)`) and the late drain at `:1988` inject **all** drained completions into the parent session message stream — there is no owner-based filter.
- `running_owner_agent_ids()` exists in `crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs` but is used only for `touch_workers_with_running_shells` (heartbeats), not delivery filtering.
- Observed in practice: a child worker's `sed ... | head` and `cargo test` completions arrive at the parent as full runtime events (task_id, command, stdout tail, …).

## Proposal

- In the parent turn-loop drains (both the main drain at ~1698 and the late drain at ~1988), drop completion events whose `owner_agent_id` is `Some(_)` before building the runtime message. Parent-owned jobs (`owner_agent_id: None` / parent id) keep current behavior.
- Keep unaffected: task/status UI visibility of child shell tasks, `Bash` `wait`/`status` actions, the `touch_workers_with_running_shells` heartbeat, and the child's own completion-event delivery.
- If a child's shell job outlives the child (orphaned job), the parent still sees the task in task/status and can `wait` on it explicitly; the suppressed event is not lost state, just not auto-delivered.

## Acceptance criteria

- Running a background shell command inside a sub-agent produces **no** `background_shell_completion` event in the parent's stream; an identical command run by the parent still does.
- Heartbeats for children with running shells still fire; task/status still shows child tasks.
- No change to the `waiting_for_subagents` anti-polling guardrail events (those are deliberate).

issues.title: agent tool: simplify the 32-field schema so models stop erroring on it

milestone.title: v0.9.7
milestone.description: Post-v0.9.6 product and runtime follow-through: provider-native Ultra, truthful Operate/sub-agent orchestration, workflow-runtime corrections, first-class plugin management, desktop/web settings alignment, media/context honesty, and deliberately deferred hotfix work.

issues.body:
## Summary

The model-facing `agent` tool carries a **32-property JSON schema with zero required fields**, serves **eight actions** (`start`, `status`, `peek`, `message`, `followup`, `interrupt`, `wait`, `cancel`) from that single schema, and the runtime parser additionally accepts a bag of aliases per field. Models regularly misinvoke it — passing fields that are invalid for the chosen action, colliding on aliases, or omitting the one field an action actually needs — which surfaces as tool errors (and sometimes spurious approval-modal routing). This issue proposes shrinking and simplifying the schema for a future release so the model has structural guidance instead of a 32-field free-for-all.

## Evidence (current surface, `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs`)

- `input_schema()` exposes 32 properties: `action, until, agent_id, timeout_secs, message, reason, include_archived, name, prompt, dependencies, acceptance, type, profile, model, thinking, cwd, worktree, worktree_branch, worktree_base, worktree_path, fork_context, max_depth, max_steps, wall_time_secs, workspace_policy, expected_artifact, write_authority, write_roots, exact_files, coordination_contracts, deliberate, resume_from` — with `"required": []`, so the schema gives no per-action structure at all.
- One schema for eight actions: most fields are only meaningful for one action (e.g. `until`/`timeout_secs` only for `wait`; `message` only for `message`/`followup`; `reason` only for `interrupt`; `include_archived` only for `status`), but the model sees them all, always.
- Alias bags make validation lenient in confusing ways: `action`/`op`, `agent_id`/`id`/`session_name`/`name`, `profile`/`fleet_profile`/`roster_profile`, `type`/`agent_type`/`agent_name`, `role`/`agent_role`, `write_authority`/`writeAuthority`, `timeout_secs`/`timeout`, plus action-name synonyms (`spawn`/`run`, `list`/`inspect`, `steer`, `join`/`await`/`block`, …). When two aliases disagree, `parse_agent_ref`-style code just picks one, and `start_requests_read_only_role` fails **closed** into the approval modal for anything it cannot prove read-only — so alias slips turn into refused calls or extra approval prompts.
- Runtime-only errors the model hits: `ToolError::missing_field("agent_id")` for `wait`/`cancel`/`interrupt` without an id; `Invalid agent action '…'`; refusal when `type` and `role`/`profile` conflict (per `start_requests_read_only_role` and the `resume_from`/`fork_context` mutual-exclusion).
- `deliberate` is a meta-field that itself mandates other fields (`type`/`profile`, `workspace_policy`, `expected_artifact`, `write_authority`) — a sign the surface has grown layered controls instead of defaults.

## Proposal (for 0.9.7 — NOT a 0.9.6 blocker)

1. **One canonical name per field.** Drop the alias bags; reject unknown keys. One name, one meaning — turns silent alias pick-wins into deterministic schema errors.
2. **Per-action schemas.** Use JSON Schema composition (e.g. `oneOf` per action with action-specific `properties` + `required`) so the model only ever sees the fields valid for the action it picked, and required fields (`agent_id` for `wait`/`interrupt`/`cancel`/`message`/`followup`; `message` for `message`; `prompt` for `start`) are declared as required.
3. **Default instead of expose.** Derive the common cases from role/type: `write_authority`, `workspace_policy`, `max_steps`, `thinking`, `fork_context` all have sensible defaults already — keep them on the tool only when the model explicitly needs to override, or fold them into named presets (e.g. a small `mode`/preset concept) rather than raw knobs.
4. **Move rare-power fields behind a separate surface.** `resume_from`, `coordination_contracts`, `deliberate`, `exact_files`, `write_roots`, `worktree_*`, `max_depth`, `include_archived` are advanced/steering controls; consider a dedicated configuration tool or profile-owned settings so the everyday `agent` schema stays small (target: ~8–10 fields). Note: keep the model-facing sub-agent surface **`agent`-only** per AGENTS.md — the narrow `agents/*` tools are runtime steering, not a replacement model surface.
5. **Error messages as guidance.** Ensure every rejection names the valid options (several already do, e.g. the action error) and extend that to field-level problems.

## Acceptance criteria (proposal)

- `agent` schema has a per-action shape with explicit `required` and no alias fields.
- A plain "start a worker with a prompt" call uses ≤5 fields; the common actions (start/status/followup/wait/cancel) never need `deliberate`, `fork_context`, or `coordination_contracts`.
- Existing behavior contracts (approval routing, read-only fast path #5186, receipts) keep their current tests passing.

Happy to take any subset — the highest-value, lowest-risk first step is (1)+(2): canonical names and per-action required/fields.

issues.title: EPIC-005: CodeWhale TUI Crate Decomposition (Umbrella)
issues.body:
## EPIC-005: CodeWhale TUI Crate Decomposition — Umbrella EPIC

This issue is the **EpicStyle tracking issue** for the CodeWhale TUI crate decomposition. It represents the entire structure below: every sub-EPIC and every FEAT reports here when done, and every PR created under this work is logged here.

The decomposition is the direct answer to the compilation-time discussion in [#4991](https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991) — see the Developer fast loop section below.

## Structure

EPIC-005 is the **umbrella EPIC**. It does not contain FEATs directly — it holds the map of **sub-EPICs**, each of which contains its own FEATs.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U["EPIC-005: TUI Crate Decomposition (umbrella)"]
    U --> E6["EPIC-006: Commands -> codewhale-commands (P1)"]
    U --> E7["EPIC-007: Tools consolidation -> crates/tools (P1)"]
    U --> E8["EPIC-008: Config consolidation -> crates/config (P2)"]
    U --> E9["EPIC-009: Hooks + Execpolicy + MCP (P2)"]
    U --> E10["EPIC-010: Core extraction -> crates/core (P3)"]
```

| ID | Sub-EPIC | Scope | Status |
|----|----------|-------|--------|
| EPIC-006 | Commands → `codewhale-commands` | `crates/tui/src/commands/` (~42k lines incl. tests; 9 groups, registry, discovery) | NotStarted |
| EPIC-007 | Tools consolidation | `crates/tui/src/tools/` (~117k lines) → `crates/tools` (currently 1.3k) | NotStarted |
| EPIC-008 | Config consolidation | `crates/tui/src/config/` (~13k lines) → `crates/config` (currently 33k) | NotStarted |
| EPIC-009 | Hooks + Execpolicy + MCP | `hooks/` (7k), `execpolicy/` (0.5k), `mcp/` (8k) → `crates/hooks`, `crates/execpolicy`, `crates/mcp` | NotStarted |
| EPIC-010 | Core extraction | `crates/tui/src/core/` (~42k lines) → `crates/core` (currently 3.4k); tightly coupled, P3 follow-up | NotStarted |

Stays in `codewhale-tui`: `tui/` rendering (~205k lines), `fleet/` (~27k lines), and the TUI-specific long tail.

## Rules (applied to every sub-EPIC)

1. Behavior-preserving — extraction only, no command/UX behavior changes.
2. Trait-first — define the boundary interface before moving code (pattern: EPIC-006 `CommandContext`).
3. Compiles at every step — bottom-up extraction, workspace stays green at each commit.
4. CI gate — extracted crate must never depend on `codewhale-tui` (e.g. `cargo check -p codewhale-commands` pulls no TUI).
5. Fork-local until complete — rebase onto upstream main frequently; no upstream PR until the sub-EPIC is done.
6. Sequencing — EPIC-006 first, then 007/008, then 009, then 010.

## Work summary (to be done)

Estimated FEATs under each EPIC. Check a FEAT off and append its PR link when the PR lands; parent EPICs auto-complete when all their FEATs are done. This section is the visual tracker — the Features Breakdown tables in the MemoryBank EPIC documents are the static FEAT-creation source and are not updated per PR.

- [ ] EPIC-006: Commands extraction (trait -> wire in place -> extract -> tests)
  - [ ] FEAT: Define `CommandContext` trait and move shared types
  - [ ] FEAT: Implement `CommandContext` for TUI `App` and wire dispatch (in place, before the move — PR is green on its own)
  - [ ] FEAT: Extract `commands/` to `crates/commands/` (mechanical move; `App` deps already cut)
  - [ ] FEAT: Split test code by compile profile — white-box inline, black-box + Gherkin acceptance in `tests/` (or a separate acceptance crate), so `cargo test -p codewhale-commands` never compiles the TUI or the Gherkin bloat
- [ ] EPIC-007: Tools consolidation
  - [ ] FEAT: Audit `tools/` vs `crates/tools` and define the shared boundary
  - [ ] FEAT: Move shared tool code into `crates/tools`
  - [ ] FEAT: Wire TUI to the consolidated crate; keep tool UI code in TUI
  - [ ] FEAT: Tests, CI gate, and re-export shim
- [ ] EPIC-008: Config consolidation
  - [ ] FEAT: Audit TUI `config/` vs `crates/config` (overlap, extensions, UI views)
  - [ ] FEAT: Extract non-UI config logic to `crates/config` (or adopt it)
  - [ ] FEAT: Wire TUI to `codewhale-config`; keep UI views in TUI
  - [ ] FEAT: Tests, CI gate, and re-export shim
- [ ] EPIC-009: Hooks/Execpolicy/MCP consolidation
  - [ ] FEAT: Consolidate `hooks/` with `crates/hooks`
  - [ ] FEAT: Consolidate `execpolicy/` with `crates/execpolicy`
  - [ ] FEAT: Consolidate `mcp/` with `crates/mcp`
  - [ ] FEAT: Tests, CI gates, and cleanup
- [ ] EPIC-010: Core extraction (follow-up)
  - [ ] FEAT: Core audit and coupling map (36 files, ~42k lines)
  - [ ] FEAT: Extract decoupled core leaves to `crates/core` (phase 1)
  - [ ] FEAT: Extract remaining core logic (phase 2, after boundary interfaces)
  - [ ] FEAT: Wire TUI to `codewhale-core`; tests and CI gate
- [ ] Final: codewhale-tui reduced from ~700k to ~300k lines focused on UI rendering

## Developer fast loop

The whole point of this decomposition: once a sub-EPIC's crate exists (EPIC-006 Feature 3 and later), day-to-day development happens **entirely outside the TUI monolith** (~700k lines). The TUI is only compiled when you explicitly need it — TUI integration tests, `cargo test --workspace`, or the final pre-PR validation.

```bash
cargo check -p codewhale-commands          # production change check — seconds, not minutes
cargo test -p codewhale-commands           # test loop — compiles only the commands crate + thin test binaries, never the TUI
cargo watch -x "check -p codewhale-commands"  # continuous check while editing (cargo-watch)
cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands    # optional: parallel test runner, faster startup
```

Why this stays fast:

- `cargo build` / `cargo check` never compiles `#[cfg(test)]` code, so production iteration is bounded to the small crate.
- `cargo test` compiles each `tests/` file as its **own small binary crate** depending only on the public API — a production change recompiles/relinks only those thin binaries, in parallel.
- The Gherkin acceptance harnesses live in separate test binaries (or a dedicated acceptance crate), so thousands of acceptance-test lines are **never part of the production crate compile**.
- Small white-box unit tests that need private access stay inline — they are cheap and cannot live outside the crate.

**Acceptance criterion for every extracted crate:** `cargo test -p <crate>` must compile only that crate and its test binaries — if it pulls in `codewhale-tui`, the boundary was cut wrong.

The numbers and impact motivating this are documented in [#4991](https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991) (Discussion: Compilation times and the TUI crate monolith): 476k lines / 82% of the workspace in one crate, 8–16 min release builds, 30+ min test suite, 2–3 iterations per hour.

## PR log (updated as work lands)

|------|-------------|-----|--------|---------|

prs.title: feat(acp): expose file/search/git/patch/shell tools over session/prompt
prs.body:
## Summary

`session/prompt` in the ACP server only streamed model text — it never
executed the tool calls a model requested, so any editor or bridge
driving CodeWhale over ACP (Zed, third-party integrations such as the
community `acp-deepseek-adapter`) got a chat-only agent with no real
code-editing capability. That gap is the reason this was originally
built in a fork; documented as a known limitation by at least one
third-party ACP bridge, which worked around it by scraping
`exec --auto` stdout instead.

This wires the existing `ToolRegistry` into the ACP turn loop instead
of building a parallel implementation:

- `run_agentic_prompt_turn` drives multi-round `tool_use`/`tool_result`
  turns (capped at `MAX_ACP_TOOL_ROUNDS`) over the same file/search/git/
  patch/shell tools the TUI itself uses, and threads `response_id_policy`
  through every round so tool-round responses still get the
  client-specific id translation (Zed/avante.nvim) the existing
  streaming path already relies on.
- Shell access is gated on the client declaring `terminal` support at
  `initialize` (default `false`/restrictive). `MAX_ACP_SESSIONS` caps
  concurrent sessions with true insertion-order eviction (`VecDeque`,
  not `HashMap` iteration order, which is not insertion-ordered).
- Tool-call cancellation signals a `CancellationToken` and waits for the
  running tool (including a child shell process) to actually stop
  before returning the cancellation, instead of abandoning it.
- `max_tokens` for the ACP path now resolves through the same
  route-limits machinery the TUI/CLI use
  (`effective_max_output_tokens_for_route`) instead of a fixed 4096
  fallback.
- `scripts/build.ps1`: a release build script for Windows PowerShell
  5.1, used to produce and test the ACP binary against Zed on Windows.

Drafted with agent assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and
build-verified by the human author before submission.

## Testing
