issues.title: [Security] `exec.allowPatterns` shell-chain bypass allows unintended command execution
issues.body:
### Advisory Details

**Title**: `exec.allowPatterns` shell-chain bypass allows unintended command execution

**Description**:

### Summary

`nanobot`'s `exec` tool can be configured with `tools.exec.allowPatterns` so operators can limit which shell commands are allowed to run. In affected versions, the allowlist check is applied to the raw command string with `re.search(...)`, and the same raw string is later executed via `bash -c`. This lets an attacker append an extra shell segment such as `&& touch ...` after an allowlisted prefix and get the appended segment executed inside the `nanobot` process context.

### Details

The issue is in `ExecTool._guard_command()` and `ExecTool._spawn()` inside `nanobot/agent/tools/shell.py`.

`_guard_command()` lowercases the full user-controlled shell string and marks it as explicitly allowed when *any* configured allow-pattern matches *anywhere* in that raw string:

```python
explicitly_allowed = bool(self.allow_patterns) and any(
    re.search(p, lower) for p in self.allow_patterns
)
```

Once that happens, the code does not require the rest of the shell string to satisfy policy. Later, `_spawn()` executes the entire raw string through the shell:

```python
args.extend(["-c", command])
```

That combination breaks the operator's expected security model. For example, a deployment that intends to allow only:

```text
echo allowlisted
```

but configures a loose allow-pattern such as:

```json
"allowPatterns": ["\\becho\\s+allowlisted\\b"]
```

will also allow:

```text
echo allowlisted && touch /workspace/canary-created
```

because the prefix matches the allowlist and the shell then parses and executes the chained `touch` segment as part of the same `bash -c` invocation.

I verified this end-to-end through the public OpenAI-compatible HTTP API (`POST /v1/chat/completions`) using two live `nanobot serve` instances:

- A vulnerable instance with `allowPatterns: ["\\becho\\s+allowlisted\\b"]`
- A control instance with `allowPatterns: ["^echo\\s+allowlisted$"]`

The vulnerable instance created the canary file and recorded `Exit code: 0`. The control instance rejected the same payload with `Error: Command blocked by allowlist filter (not in allowlist)`.

### PoC

#### Prerequisites

- A local Python environment that can run `nanobot`
- Access to a checkout of the affected project
- `gh` authenticated if you want to fetch the same gists directly
- A deployment that enables:
  - `tools.exec.enable = true`
  - `tools.exec.allowPatterns` with a loose prefix/substring regex
- The provided fake provider and two local `nanobot serve` processes listening on:
  - `127.0.0.1:18081`
  - `127.0.0.1:18901`
  - `127.0.0.1:18902`

#### Reproduction Steps

1. Download the orchestration script from: [run_e2e.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/f5ec905ff95a50025bf22dde3cdd2144)
2. Download the fake provider from: [fake_provider.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/0543f4ddb9188af792c74cc8244dc00b)
3. Download the vulnerable config from: [vuln-config.json](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/d000e4060c2b05613d0dc24a747652a4)
4. Download the control config from: [control-config.json](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/15ef06324886a89bb2da30b14475959d)
5. Download the vulnerable-side verifier from: [verification_test.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/bd0665d768ce7375e09832bef3ff9d4e)
6. Download the control-side verifier from: [control-policy-enforced.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/798a2928437f208f256e87c4144a7681)
7. From the repository root, run:
   `python3 llm-enhance/cve-finding/similar/RCE/Advisory-GHSA-5326-6f73-m96w-exec-allow-pattern-shell-chain-bypass-exp/run_e2e.py`
8. Observe that the vulnerable service accepts the tool-call command:
   `echo allowlisted && touch "<canary-path>"`
9. Confirm the vulnerable workspace now contains:
   `llm-enhance/cve-finding/similar/RCE/Advisory-GHSA-5326-6f73-m96w-exec-allow-pattern-shell-chain-bypass-exp/runtime/vuln-workspace/canary-created`
10. Confirm the control service does **not** create its canary and instead records an allowlist error in its session log.

### Log of Evidence

The reproduced end-to-end run returned `[DEFECT-CONFIRMED]`.

Observed runtime evidence:

```text
control_returncode: 0
control_canary_exists: false
control session result: Error: Command blocked by allowlist filter (not in allowlist)

vuln_returncode: 0
vuln_canary_exists: true
vulnerable session result: allowlisted

Exit code: 0
```

The vulnerable run created:

```text
.../runtime/vuln-workspace/canary-created
```

and the control run did not.

### Impact

This is a command-execution policy bypass in the shell tool boundary. It allows a caller who can cause an `exec` tool call to smuggle additional shell segments past an operator-defined allowlist. The direct impact is unintended command execution with the same OS-level privileges as the running `nanobot` process. In practical terms, that can mean modifying files in the agent workspace, deleting data, planting follow-on scripts, or chaining into broader host compromise if the process is not isolated by a real sandbox.

### Affected products

- **Ecosystem**: pip
- **Package name**: nanobot
- **Affected versions**: <= 0.2.1
- **Patched versions**: <None>

### Severity

- **Severity**: High
- **Vector string**: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:H

### Weaknesses

- **CWE**: CWE-88: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command

### Occurrences

| Permalink | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| [https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/f309982bb0a2dca76dd038473ee6f1be803bd503/nanobot/agent/tools/shell.py#L563-L586](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/f309982bb0a2dca76dd038473ee6f1be803bd503/nanobot/agent/tools/shell.py#L563-L586) | `_guard_command()` approves the whole raw shell string when any configured allow-pattern matches somewhere in it. This is the policy decision that lets a chained payload inherit allowlist approval from its first segment. |
| [https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/f309982bb0a2dca76dd038473ee6f1be803bd503/nanobot/agent/tools/shell.py#L440-L474](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/f309982bb0a2dca76dd038473ee6f1be803bd503/nanobot/agent/tools/shell.py#L440-L474) | `_spawn()` executes the exact same raw string with `bash -c`, so shell metacharacters such as `&&` are parsed and the extra appended command segment runs after the allowlisted prefix. |

issues.title: Security: CLI apps run with full os.environ — API keys leaked to installed app subprocesses
issues.body:
## Summary

When running installed CLI apps, the subprocess is launched with `os.environ.copy()` — the full, unfiltered OS environment. This includes all provider API keys that `_setup_env` writes to `os.environ` (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, etc.). Contrast this with the shell tool, which builds a minimal curated environment with only `HOME`, `LANG`, `TERM`, and `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`.

## Affected Code

- `nanobot/apps/cli/service.py:1338-1345` — `subprocess.run([resolved, *clean_args], env=os.environ.copy())`
- `nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py:465-477` — `_setup_env` writes API keys to `os.environ`
- `nanobot/agent/tools/shell.py:542-589` — `_build_env()` does proper minimal env (positive example)

## Root Cause

The CLI app subprocess launcher copies the full environment. It should filter to a minimal safe subset, similar to what the shell tool already does.

## Suggested Fix

Filter the environment for CLI app subprocesses to the same minimal set used by the shell tool (`HOME`, `LANG`, `TERM`, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`), plus explicitly configured allowlist vars. Never pass API keys to untrusted subprocesses.

issues.title: Security: Provider API keys leaked between providers via global os.environ mutation
issues.body:
## Summary

`OpenAICompatProvider._setup_env()` writes provider API keys directly into the process-global `os.environ` dict. For gateway-type providers, `os.environ[spec.env_key] = api_key` **overwrites** any previous value. For non-gateway providers, `os.environ.setdefault(spec.env_key, api_key)` **leaves stale keys** from the first instantiated provider visible. In multi-provider configurations, keys can leak between provider instances.

## Affected Code

- `nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py:465-477` — `_setup_env()` mutates `os.environ`:
  - Line 467: `os.environ[spec.env_key] = api_key` (overwrites for gateways)
  - Line 471: `os.environ.setdefault(spec.env_key, api_key)` (first-write wins for non-gateways)
  - Lines 475-477: `env_extras` also written to `os.environ`

## Root Cause

Provider key management uses process-global `os.environ` as shared state. The `setdefault` pattern means the first provider to initialize "wins" for a given env key; the `os.environ[key] = value` pattern means the last gateway provider overwrites.

## Suggested Fix

Use per-provider-instance state (`self._api_key`) rather than process-global env vars. If env vars are required by third-party SDKs, scope them with context variables or thread-local state that is set/restored around each provider call.

### Problem / Motivation

**First of all, thank you for creating such an amazing project. I really appreciate it.**

---

OpenRouter supports many server tools (such as Web Search, Web Fetch, Fusion, etc.). The common way to use them is to add them to the `tools` field.

I noticed an earlier commit (<https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/3974>). In that commit, extra body configuration is supported. I edited the `extraBody` of the openrouter provider and added the following:

```json
{
    "tools": [
        { "type": "openrouter:web_search" },
        { "type": "openrouter:web_fetch" }
    ]
}
```

*(I know nanobot already has search and fetch tools built in, but possibly due to network issues, the default DuckDuckGo experience is honestly not great, and I'd rather not register more accounts just to get API keys. OpenRouter's server tools are clearly convenient alternatives.)*

As a test, I picked a task that involves searching, organizing material, and writing to a local file. After using `/goal`, I went off to do other things.

About ten minutes later, I switched back to the webui. It worked great and found the material I wanted. But then it said it couldn't write to the local file.

After re-reading the wiki, I got some bad news:

```markdown
`extraBody` follows the selected OpenAI API surface. With Chat Completions, nanobot passes it through as the SDK extra_body value.
```

I'm not deeply familiar with this area, but I suspect the openrouter provider uses Chat Completions, and the `tools` field I added simply overrode nanobot's built-in tools.

---

I sincerely hope you could consider adding handling logic for the `tools` field in `extraBody` under Chat Completions, similar to how it's handled under the Responses API — or alternatively, add Responses API support for the openrouter provider (given that OpenRouter's server tools include Responses-API-only tools like `shell`, this option seems worth considering).

---
*(It seems that many issues use English, so I use llm for translation.) ^_^*

 Add handling logic for the `tools` field in `extraBody` under Chat Completions, similar to how it's handled under the Responses API.

issues.title: Bug: /goal message produces dozens of repeated replies when waiting for user's answer

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ### Bug Description ### Summary A single /goal message produced dozens of near-identical replies, all sent while the agent was waiting for an answer from the user. It ended only when the user intervened, or when the model finally recognised as a system loop and marked the goal cancel. The trigger is a goal in active state plus a final response that waits on the user, which is typically a question back to them. nanobot then re-prompts the model to "continue working toward the objective and loops. The model has no substantial work to do (it needs the answer) and cannot mark the goal complete (the objective is unmet), so it rephrases the same message. Every rephrase is a visible reply. That re-prompt is exempt from the brake that limits ordinary mid-turn injections: `_MAX_INJECTION_CYCLES` is only advanced for real user injections, so the goal continuation never advances it (`nanobot/agent/runner.py`, `_try_drain_injections`). What is left is max_iterations within a turn, and `_MAX_GOAL_CONTINUATION_ROUNDS` across turns. ### Impact - A single user message can burn the whole per-turn iteration budget (`max_iterations`), and `maybe_continue_turn` then schedules further turns until `_MAX_GOAL_CONTINUATION_ROUNDS` is spent, so one message can maximally cost roughly `max_iterations × 13` requests. - Every reply and re-prompt is appended to session history, so context and cost keep growing. - This is agent-loop behavior, so it is channel-independent. ### Steps to Reproduce **On a real channel.** The goal needs several rounds of tool work, and something the model will want clarified afterwards. 1. Send `/goal plan a two-week Rust study schedule, write it to workspace/rust-plan.md, then follow up on my progress daily` 2. Let it finish its first round of work. It then asks a question ("which day do you want to start?") — the loop begins there, with no further input from user. e.g. ### Expected Behavior A turn that has stopped making substantial progress should be bounded, rather than re-prompting the model and replying to the user until the budget is gone. The goal itself can stay active when the objective is genuinely unfinished - but it should not stand in the way of the user's next message, whether that message continues the goal or changes the subject. ### Relevant Logs ```shell ``` ### nanobot Version 0.3.0 ### Python Version 3.11 ### Operating System Linux ### Channel / Platform Telegram ### LLM Provider DeepSeek ### Configuration (Optional) ```yaml ``` ### Additional Context _No response_

prs.title: fix(mcp): preserve credentials when OAuth store read fails
prs.body:
# PR draft

## Title

fix(mcp): preserve credentials when OAuth store read fails

## Body

MCP OAuth storage previously treated a read failure as an empty store. A later
token update or credential removal could then overwrite credentials belonging to
another server.

The storage layer now treats only a missing file as an empty store. Invalid or
unreadable content raises `MCPAuthorizationStoreError`, so mutation paths stop
before writing. Read paths handle store and lock failures by returning safe
defaults, and MCP connection setup reports store errors without crashing the
connection task.

MCP config replacement and removal now clear OAuth credentials before saving the
new config. If cleanup fails, the API returns 503 and leaves the config unchanged.
This avoids committing a config change while an old token is still available for
the same server name.

## Tests

- `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_oauth.py tests/webui/test_mcp_presets_api.py tests/webui/test_mcp_oauth_api.py tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py tests/agent/test_mcp_connection.py tests/agent/test_mcp_reconnect_crash.py -q` (83 passed)

prs.title: fix(exec): terminate one-shot process trees on cleanup
prs.body:
## Summary

  Fix a one-shot `exec` cleanup gap where timeout, cancellation, or an
  unexpected execution error killed only the root shell process.

  Child processes spawned by the shell could survive after the command had
  already returned an error, continue running in the background, and still
  produce side effects.

  ## Root Cause

  The one-shot path in `ExecTool.execute()` called `_spawn()` with the default
  `process_tree=False`, then used `_kill_process()` for timeout and cancellation.

  On Unix, this kills only the shell process instead of its descendants. The
  session-based exec path already uses an isolated process tree and
  `_kill_process_tree()`.

  ## Fix

  - Start one-shot commands with `process_tree=True`.
  - Use `_kill_process_tree()` for:
    - timeout cleanup
    - `CancelledError` cleanup
    - unexpected-error cleanup after a process has started
  - Keep existing session execution behavior unchanged.

  This uses the existing cross-platform tree termination implementation:

  - Unix: isolated session plus `killpg(..., SIGKILL)`
  - Windows: `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`

  ## Tests

  Added and updated regression coverage for:

  - one-shot timeout starts the process with `process_tree=True`
  - one-shot timeout calls tree-level termination
  - external cancellation calls tree-level termination and propagates
    `CancelledError`
  - a real Unix integration case where a background child would write a marker
    after the root shell times out; the marker is now not created
  - existing `_spawn` test doubles accept the new keyword argument

prs.title: feat: add inline keyboard support for Telegram messages
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds native inline keyboard support for Telegram messages, allowing nanobot to send messages with interactive buttons and receive callbacks when users click them.

## Motivation

Enables richer user interactions through:
- Confirmation dialogs (Yes/No, Approve/Reject)
- Quick action buttons for reminders/tasks
- URL links alongside messages
- Multi-row button layouts

## Changes

### `nanobot/channels/telegram.py`
- Added `CallbackQueryHandler` for receiving button click callbacks
- Added `_pending_callbacks` in-memory storage for button definitions
- Added `callback_query` to `allowed_updates` in polling
- Added `_store_callback()`, `_get_callback()`, `_on_callback_query()` methods
- Updated `_build_inline_keyboard()` and `_create_button()` for new button format
- Added null check for deleted messages in callback handler

### `nanobot/agent/tools/message.py`
- Added `inline_buttons` parameter for defining interactive buttons
- Added `callback_id` parameter for grouping buttons across messages

### `workspace/TOOLS.md`
- Documented the `message` tool with new parameters
- Added inline buttons section with usage examples
- Added callback handling documentation for the agent

## Usage

### Sending a message with inline buttons

```python
message(
    content="Reminder: Drink water!",
    channel="telegram",
    chat_id="6176528759",
    callback_id="reminder_001",
    inline_buttons=[
        {"id": "done", "label": "✅ Done", "data": "Mark this as completed"},
        {"id": "snooze", "label": "⏰ Snooze", "data": "Remind me in 10 minutes"}
    ]
)
```

### Button format

```python
# Callback button (triggers callback to agent)
{"id": "approve", "label": "✅ Approve", "data": "Instructions", "metadata": {...}}

# URL button (opens link, no callback)
{"label": "Help", "url": "https://example.com"}

# Row layouts (multiple buttons per row)
[
    [{"id": "yes", "label": "Yes"}, {"id": "no", "label": "No"}],
    [{"label": "Help", "url": "..."}]
]
```

### Receiving callbacks

When a user clicks a button, the agent receives an InboundMessage with:
- `content`: structured message indicating which button was clicked
- `metadata.event_type`: `"callback_query"`
- `metadata.callback_id`: the group identifier
- `metadata.button`: `{id, label, data, metadata}`

The agent should check `metadata.event_type == "callback_query"` to handle button clicks.

## callback_id Design

The `callback_id` is a **message-level** identifier that groups buttons:
- Multiple messages can share the same `callback_id` (e.g., recurring reminders)
- Each button has its own `id` within the group
- Telegram receives `callback_data` as `"callback_id:button_id"` (fits in 64 bytes)
- If not provided, a short UUID is auto-generated

## Tested

Working in production on a personal nanobot instance.

prs.title: fix(agent): warn instead of silently spiraling on repeated identical tool calls
prs.body:
## Problem

The tool-call loop has no repeat/loop detection at all. A stuck agent can burn its entire `max_iterations` budget calling the exact same tool with the exact same arguments over and over, with no signal to the user or the model that it's happening -- it just looks frozen from the outside until the iteration cap finally kicks in.

Ran into this directly: an agent spiraled for several minutes checking the same env var through half a dozen different mechanisms (`exec`, `grep`, reading its own session log, etc.) before eventually landing on the right answer -- no single one of those calls repeated identically enough times in a row to be an obvious "stuck" signal by iteration count alone, but a simpler variant of the same problem (identical tool + identical args, repeated) is easy to construct and easy to detect.

## Fix

Adds a lightweight, order-independent per-turn signature tracker (tool name + arguments) to `AgentRunner.run()`. After 3 identical tool-call rounds in a row, it injects one `system`-role warning into the conversation telling the model to stop and try something else, then resets the tracker -- it informs, it does not block, so legitimate repeated reads/checks still execute normally.

## Scope

This catches repeats **across separate iterations** (the failure pattern above). It intentionally does **not** catch several identical calls bundled into a single turn (e.g. 3 parallel `read_file` calls in one response) -- confirmed live during testing that this is genuinely a different pattern. Happy to extend coverage there too if maintainers think it's worth it, but wanted to keep this PR scoped to the pattern actually observed.

## Testing

- Two new tests in `tests/agent/test_runner_safety.py`: warn-once-after-three-identical-calls, and no-false-positive-on-two-repeats-or-varied-arguments.
- Full suite: 4885 passed, 0 failed, 33 skipped (pre-existing skips, unrelated).
- `ruff check` clean on both changed files.
- Manually verified against a live gateway (patched the installed copy, restarted, dispatched real test tasks) -- confirmed the change imports and runs cleanly against a real running instance, not just the test suite.

## Non-goals

Not attempting a more general loop-detection framework here (state hashing across N steps, progress detection, etc.) -- keeping this to the smallest change that addresses the concrete failure pattern, per the contributing guide's "prefer the smallest change that solves the real problem."

## What

[OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai) is an OpenAI-compatible model routing gateway that brings 150+ models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and xAI behind a single endpoint and API key. Beyond routing, it runs gateway-level, zero-trust security for AI agents on the same endpoint — screening every prompt/response and governing every tool call on a default-deny basis, with no application code changes. This PR registers it as a named provider so users can opt in directly.

I'm an engineer on the OrcaRouter team.

prs.title: feat(workspace): per-session sandbox isolation for non-WebUI channels
prs.body:
## What

Adds an opt-in `per_session_sandbox` mode: each non-WebUI session gets its own isolated filesystem sandbox under `<workspace>/workspaces/<sanitized_session_key>/`, created lazily on the first turn and operated in **restricted** mode so agent file tools stay within that directory. Sessions no longer share a single global workspace.

## Why

For multi-tenant / multi-chat deployments (IM channels etc.), a single shared workspace means sessions can trample each other's files. This gives each session an automatic, isolated working directory without manual project selection — while leaving WebUI's manual project picker untouched.

## How to enable

```json
{ "agents": { "defaults": { "perSessionSandbox": true } } }
```

Default `off`; existing behavior unchanged.

## Behavior

- **Default off** → zero behavior change (regression-protected).
- **On, non-WebUI channel** → lazily creates `<workspace>/workspaces/<sanitized_key>/`, restricted mode, agent file ops confined there.
- **WebUI (websocket)** → keeps manual project selection, unaffected.
- **No-session messages (system, etc.)** → safely degrades to default workspace.
- **Session history** (`sessions/`) stays on the data-home root — preserves the data-home / sandbox role separation.

## Changes

- `nanobot/security/workspace_access.py` — `WorkspaceScopeResolver` gains `per_session_sandbox` flag; `for_turn()`/`for_message()` gain a `session_key` param; new `_per_session_scope()` + `_sanitize_session_key()`.
- `nanobot/agent/loop.py` — threads `session_key` through the four scope-resolution call sites; constructs the resolver with the flag; reads it from `defaults`.
- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — `AgentDefaults.per_session_sandbox: bool = False`.
- `tests/agent/test_workspace_scope.py` — 4 tests at the resolver seam.

## Testing

TDD (red → green). `tests/agent`, `tests/security`, `tests/session`, `tests/config`, and WebUI-related suites all green (1700+); the one failing test is pre-existing and environment-related (timezone DB), verified unrelated via `git stash`.

## Not included (YAGNI)

Directory cleanup on session delete/TTL, directory-name template, access-mode config. `per_session_sandbox` is a `bool` today, can evolve to `{enabled, dir_template, access_mode}` later.

prs.title: fix(agent): bound sustained-goal continuation when the turn goes idle
prs.body:
## Summary

Two problems, one at each end of a sustained goal's life.

**Admission.** A request carrying a recurring cadence ("follow up with me daily,
forever") could be recorded as a sustained goal even though it has no terminal
condition. Once recorded it stays `active`, which keeps internal continuation armed
and the session on sustained-goal runtime limits until something explicitly ends it.

**Execution.** Goal continuation bypassed `_MAX_INJECTION_CYCLES`, so every plain-text
final response injected another "keep working" nudge. A model waiting on the user
could only rephrase the same answer, burning the whole iteration budget.

### Changes

1. **Bounded idle continuation.** Count continuations that produce no tool call
   against `_MAX_GOAL_IDLE_CONTINUES`; any tool execution clears the streak. Real
   user injections are drained before the guard is consulted, so user input is never
   suppressed. The goal stays active because it is waiting, not done.

2. **`completion_evidence` required** on `create_goal` and on `update_goal(replace)`.
   A request with no nameable terminal condition can't be recorded without the model
   noticing. Persisted and replayed as a `Done when:` line, so it also serves as the
   completion criterion after compaction — `update_goal` guidance now points at it.

3. **Single-shot admission window.** When the model ends a `/goal` turn without
   recording anything — it asks a clarifying question and stops — the current mutation
   permission (`_GOAL_MUTATION_ALLOWED`) dies with that turn, so the user's plain-language answer can't create
   the goal and the old guidance told the model to ask them to resubmit the whole
   command. A persisted `_goal_admission_pending` flag opens admission for exactly
   one following user-authored turn. It is closed in `_persist_turn`, and also in the
   command short-circuit, which returns before `_persist_turn` runs — otherwise
   `/help` or `/new` would carry the window into an unrelated turn.

4. **Routing and pending-goal guidance in the prompt.** Recurring parts go to `cron`,
   only the bounded remainder is recorded with `create_goal`, and no goal is recorded
   if nothing bounded remains. When a goal admission is pending and no goal is active,
   the prompt guides resolving that pending request instead.

Invariant preserved: every recorded goal traces back to an explicit `/goal`, either
in that turn or the one immediately before it. The window can't chain — it only opens
from a `/goal` turn, so a non-`/goal` turn can consume it but never re-open it.

## Fix

Fixes #5256

## Out of scope / to be aware

1. **This does not guarantee the failure cannot recur.** It is model-compliance
   dependent with no deterministic repro. Only change 1 is runtime-enforced; 2–4
   reduce frequency. 

2. **Nothing expires a stale active goal.** The idle guard bounds the loop, not the
   record. While `status == "active"`, later turns still re-arm continuation up to the
   per-goal `_MAX_GOAL_CONTINUATION_ROUNDS` budget; only `cancel`/`complete`/`replace`
   clears it. 

3. **The admission window can outlive its one turn** if a turn never reaches `_persist_turn` —
   an exception, or `/stop`. The flag only ever *grants* capability and never denies,
   so a stale window can't block a later `/goal`; the exposure is one turn of
   unintended `create_goal` permission. A TTL backstop is possible — `since` is already
   persisted and unread — but the right TTL value trades a silently-expired window
   against that exposure, so I left it for discussion rather than guessing.

## How to test

```bash
pytest tests/agent/tools/test_long_task.py tests/session/test_goal_state.py \
       tests/agent/test_runner_goal_continue.py \
       tests/agent/test_loop_runner_integration.py tests/command/ -q
# 150 passed

ruff check nanobot/ tests/   # All checks passed!

prs.title: feat(spawn): allow subagents to use configurable model presets
prs.body:
## Summary

Subagents can now run with a different model than the parent agent. The LLM specifies a named model preset when calling `spawn`, and the subagent executes using that preset's provider, model, temperature, and token limits. Only presets explicitly listed in `agents.defaults.spawnPresets` are callable — an empty list (the default) preserves the current single-model behavior.

## Why

All subagents previously shared the parent agent's model and provider. This means a single model handles every task type — even when a cheaper/faster model would suffice for simple subagent work, or a reasoning-specialized model would produce better results for complex analysis. Operators had no way to let the agent choose the right model per task.

## How it works

1. The operator declares allowed presets in config: `agents.defaults.spawnPresets: ["fast", "reasoning"]`.
2. Config validation ensures every listed name exists in `modelPresets`.
3. `SpawnTool` exposes an optional `model_preset` parameter and dynamically lists available presets in its description so the LLM knows what's available.
4. When `model_preset` is provided, `SubagentManager` resolves it via the existing `ProviderSnapshot` pipeline — the same mechanism used for runtime model switching on the main agent.
5. A temporary `AgentRunner` is created with the snapshot's provider, and the subagent runs with the preset's model, temperature, max_tokens, and reasoning_effort.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant LLM
    participant SpawnTool
    participant SubagentMgr
    participant SnapshotLoader
    participant AgentRunner

    LLM->>SpawnTool: spawn(task, model_preset="fast")
    SpawnTool->>SubagentMgr: spawn(task, model_preset="fast")
    SubagentMgr->>SubagentMgr: validate "fast" in spawn_presets
    SubagentMgr->>SnapshotLoader: snapshot("fast")
    SnapshotLoader-->>SubagentMgr: ProviderSnapshot
    SubagentMgr->>AgentRunner: new AgentRunner(snapshot.provider)
    AgentRunner->>AgentRunner: run with snapshot.model/temperature
```

## Changes

- **`config/schema.py`**: Add `spawn_presets: list[str]` to `AgentDefaults` with validation that every entry exists in `model_presets`.
- **`agent/subagent.py`**: `SubagentManager` accepts `spawn_presets` and `preset_snapshot_loader`. `spawn()` validates the preset allowlist. `_run_subagent()` creates a scoped `AgentRunner` with the preset's provider when a preset is specified.
- **`agent/tools/spawn.py`**: Add `model_preset` parameter to the tool schema. Description dynamically lists available presets.
- **`agent/tools/context.py`**: Add `spawn_presets` field to `ToolContext`.
- **`agent/loop.py`**: Build `spawn_presets` dict from config in `from_config()` and pass to `SubagentManager` and `ToolContext`.
- **Tests**: 7 new tests covering preset selection, rejection of unknown presets, default behavior without presets, tool description rendering, and temperature override.

## Config example

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "spawnPresets": ["fast", "reasoning"]
    }
  },
  "modelPresets": {
    "fast": { "model": "deepseek-v4-flash", "temperature": 0.3 },
    "reasoning": { "model": "gpt-5.5", "reasoningEffort": "high" }
  }
}
```

## Test plan

- [x] `test_spawn_with_model_preset_uses_different_model` — preset model, temperature, and max_tokens reach AgentRunSpec
- [x] `test_spawn_rejects_unknown_preset` — preset not in allowlist is rejected with error message
- [x] `test_spawn_without_preset_uses_default_model` — omitting model_preset uses parent model (no regression)
- [x] `test_spawn_presets_empty_rejects_any_preset` — empty allowlist rejects all presets
- [x] `test_spawn_tool_description_lists_presets` — tool description includes preset names
- [x] `test_spawn_tool_description_no_presets` — no presets → no mention in description
- [x] `test_spawn_with_preset_temperature_override` — explicit temperature overrides preset default

prs.title: fix(skills): make weather workflow Windows-safe
prs.body:
## Problem

On Windows PowerShell, bare `curl` may resolve to the `Invoke-WebRequest` alias instead of the native cURL executable.

The weather skill previously used bare `curl` in its examples. This could cause the first weather command to fail, requiring the agent to analyze the error and retry with `curl.exe`. Requests for today's weather could also trigger separate current-condition and daily-forecast calls.

These retries introduce avoidable tool calls, LLM iterations, latency, and token usage.

## Changes

- use `curl.exe` for weather requests on Windows PowerShell
- document the platform-specific difference between Windows PowerShell and macOS/Linux shells
- use explicit HTTPS wttr.in URLs
- instruct the agent to use a single `?1&m` request for today's weather
- add a regression test for the bundled weather skill guidance

## Result

Manual verification with “北京今天天气怎么样？” confirmed that the agent directly called:

```text
curl.exe -s "https://wttr.in/Beijing?1&m"
```

This avoids the failed bare `curl` attempt, the follow-up recovery iteration, and a redundant separate current-weather request, reducing avoidable response latency and token usage.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/agent/test_builtin_weather_skill.py -v` — 1 passed
- `pytest tests/agent/test_context_builder.py -q` — 49 passed
- `ruff check tests/agent/test_builtin_weather_skill.py` — all checks passed
- manually verified the workflow on Windows PowerShell with:
  `nanobot agent --logs -s cli:weather-skill-test`
- confirmed that the agent directly called:
  `curl.exe -s "https://wttr.in/Beijing?1&m"`
- confirmed that no failed bare `curl` attempt or redundant current-weather request occurred

prs.title: refactor: move MCP lifecycle out of AgentLoop

## Summary

- add an application-owned `MCPProvider` that owns merged configuration, connections, status, reload/reconnect, tool registration, and shutdown
- inject one shared `ToolRegistry` into an MCP-agnostic `AgentLoop`, with provider composition at the gateway, CLI, API, and SDK entry points

- unregister dynamic tools during reload/shutdown, roll back partially connected batches on timeout or cancellation, and finish closing every connection before propagating cancellation

## Design

This moves lifecycle ownership out of the agent loop instead of only wrapping its existing MCP fields. `AgentLoop` now consumes tools and focuses on turns; application composition roots own infrastructure readiness and cleanup. This keeps the same provider instance and registry visible to every supported entry point without weak references or runtime-control events.

prs.body:
## Summary
Room-level Matrix responses were sent as bare top-level events, so the client never linked the bot answer back to the user message that started the turn.

## Problem
For non-thread room prompts, Matrix's reply feature was not used on outbound messages. Threaded turns already attach `m.thread` + `m.in_reply_to`; room-level turns did not.

## Solution
1. Inbound Matrix events now set `message_id` to the event id (alongside existing `event_id`) so the agent loop / message tool can round-trip a reply target the same way Telegram and Discord do.
2. Outbound `send` / `send_delta` use a small helper that:
   - keeps the existing `m.thread` relation for threaded turns
   - otherwise attaches a plain `m.in_reply_to` pointing at `message_id` / `event_id`

python -m pytest nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py \
  -k 'thread_metadata or message_id_for_room or in_reply_to_for_room or prefers_thread or thread_relates_to_for_thread' -q

  -k 'send_ or on_message_sets or build_matrix_text or thread' -q

```

- I did not run a live Matrix homeserver e2e here; verification is unit coverage of inbound metadata + outbound relation shape.
- Progress/stream edits still use the existing replace path; this only changes the relation attached to new room-level sends.

prs.title: fix(matrix): isolate thread sessions
prs.body:
## Summary

- derive a stable Matrix session key from the room ID and `m.thread` root event ID
- apply the override to both text and media messages while preserving top-level room sessions
- cover same-thread reuse, cross-thread isolation, thread-scoped `/new`, and media routing

## Why

Matrix already preserved thread relation metadata for replies, but inbound messages still fell back to the room-level session. Threads in the same room therefore shared history, serialization, and commands such as `/new`.

Thread events now use `matrix:<room_id>:thread:<root_event_id>`, matching the isolation model used by other threaded channels without changing outbound routing through the room ID.

## Scope and prior work

This focuses on session isolation. Fetching and injecting the root event into the first turn of a newly observed thread remains a separate follow-up.

This is a current-main adaptation of the approach proposed in #1732 by @zcxixixi, after the Matrix channel package refactor, with additional coverage for stable same-thread routing and `/new` isolation.

Addresses #5275.

## Validation

- `uv run --no-sync pytest nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py -q` (`89 passed`)
- `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/command/test_router_dispatchable.py tests/agent/test_unified_session.py tests/agent/test_loop_save_turn.py -q` (`111 passed`)
- `uv run --no-sync pytest -q -n auto` (`5907 passed, 17 skipped`)
- `uv run --no-sync ruff check nanobot/channels/matrix/runtime.py nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py`

prs.title: fix(channels): preserve indentation across message splits
prs.body:
## Summary

- preserve indentation after newline-based message splits
- avoid whitespace-only chunks when an indented line requires a hard split
- keep Signal UTF-16 style offsets aligned with the actual emitted chunks

## Root cause

`split_message` used `lstrip()` after every boundary. When a long response was split at a newline, that removed both the delimiter and all indentation from the next line. Signal's style partitioner also assumed every boundary stripped all whitespace, so preserving indentation without updating the mapper would shift rich-text offsets.

The fix consumes only the selected newline, keeps the existing ordinary space-boundary behavior, and locates Signal chunks sequentially in the original text.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/utils/test_helpers.py nanobot/channels/signal/tests/test_signal_markdown.py nanobot/channels/signal/tests/test_signal_channel.py::TestSend::test_send_split_message_redistributes_text_styles nanobot/channels/mattermost/tests/test_mattermost_channel.py::test_message_splitting -q` - 64 passed
- `python -m ruff check` on all four changed files - passed
- randomized check across 2,000 inputs and five chunk limits - chunk bounds and progress passed
- `python -m pytest -q` - collection blocked in the local environment because `watchfiles` is not installed; no full-suite result claimed

prs.title: fix(webui): reject discarded temporary chat messages
prs.body:
# PR draft

## Title

fix(webui): reject discarded temporary chat messages

## Body

The WebSocket message path reads the Temporary Chat policy and then waits for
later work. If the user discards the chat during that wait, the request could
resume and persist the scope as a normal chat before publishing the message.

The handler now checks the chat owner and transient session again immediately
before persistence and message-bus changes. A message that loses its Temporary
Chat state returns `temporary_chat_unavailable` instead of recreating the session
or entering the bus.

## Tests

- `uv run --no-sync pytest nanobot/channels/websocket/tests/test_websocket_channel.py tests/utils/test_webui_workspaces.py tests/agent/test_loop_session_policy.py tests/session/test_session_cache.py -q` (200 passed)

prs.title: fix(webui): surface MCP runtime connection failures
prs.body:
## Summary

- project MCP `connecting` / `connected` / `failed` state from real gateway connection attempts, separately from persisted configuration
- exclude failed or unknown MCPs from Ready, render failures without a success check, and expose recovery for OAuth, custom, and non-OAuth servers
- preserve the existing desktop two-column MCP catalog while allowing card contents to wrap without overlap at constrained widths
- keep settings GET/list local-only and serialize only the safe runtime enum

## Design

The gateway owns a minimal process-local snapshot of the last real MCP connection attempt. Settings receives that snapshot through explicit dependency injection; it does not probe remote servers, persist errors, or expose exception, token, or URL details. While a visible Apps page contains a `connecting` item, the WebUI rereads only this local snapshot until the attempt settles; it never triggers a remote probe. OAuth failures restart authorization with credential reset, while other configured servers use the existing live reload path.

`Ready` now means an MCP is installed, configured, and runtime-connected. A configured MCP whose last real attempt failed remains visible in the MCP catalog with a failure status and recovery controls, but not in Ready.

## Testing

- focused Python MCP/settings/CLI suite: `283 passed, 1 skipped`
- focused Apps OAuth/runtime UI suite: `10 passed`
- full WebUI coverage suite passed
- WebUI ESLint and production build/typecheck passed
- Ruff passed on affected Python production/tests
- strict basedpyright: `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes`
- Xmind-style OAuth HTTP 403, handshake failure, missing authorization, and OAuth/custom reconnect regressions covered
- browser verification at 1400x800: two-column catalog, no card overlap, failed item absent from Ready, no success check, working Reconnect and overflow menu, clean console

## Limitation

Runtime status is intentionally the last known real attempt rather than continuous health monitoring. It resets with the gateway process, and a later silent disconnect is learned on the next runtime interaction or reconnect.

prs.title: fix(webui): pad PWA icons for Android launchers
prs.body:
## Summary

- add opaque white backgrounds and consistent padding to the 192x192 and 512x512 general-purpose PWA icons
- keep a separate 512x512 maskable icon, but reduce the nanobot mark to 40% of the source canvas so Android's adaptive mask leaves visible breathing room
- version the general-purpose icon URLs with `?v=2` and the revised maskable icon with `?v=3` so browsers do not reuse the gateway's one-year immutable cache entries

## Why

Android may install a web app as either a WebAPK or a browser-badged website shortcut. Chromium's current Android add-to-home-screen path requests the primary icon with `prefer_maskable_icon = true` before it performs the WebAPK eligibility check. Therefore an HTTP origin that falls back to a browser shortcut can still receive the maskable icon and pass it to Android as an adaptive bitmap.

Keeping the cat merely inside the maskable safe zone was not enough: it occupied almost the entire launcher-visible region after Android applied its adaptive mask. The revised asset keeps the white background but reduces the mark from about 59% to 40% of the 512px canvas, matching the intended padded launcher appearance.

The Web App Manifest update guidance recommends changing an icon's `src` when its pixels change. This is required here because the gateway serves static files with `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

## Verification

- `bun run test -- src/tests/sw.test.ts` (9 passed)
- `bun run build`
- built maskable asset SHA-256 matches the public source asset
- pixel audit: 512x512 opaque PNG, white corners, centered non-white content bounds `205x194+153+159`
- built manifest references `/brand/nanobot_icon_maskable.png?v=3`

## Installation note

A public HTTP origin is not eligible for WebAPK installation in Chrome; it falls back to a browser-badged shortcut. Existing pinned shortcuts keep their installation-time icon, so remove the old shortcut and add it again after deploying this head. Exact launcher masking and the Chrome badge remain device-owned.

prs.body:
## Summary

Adds PWA support to the WebUI: installable to the home screen, standalone launch, and an offline-capable shell. This PR takes the PWA portion of #4494 (authored by @zpljd258) with the original author's agreement; the commit was cherry-picked with authorship preserved. The sidebar swipe-gesture portion of #4494 is intentionally excluded — it conflicts with the mobile responsive-layout fixes already merged in #4693 and stays tracked in #4494 / #4479.

Three commits: ① PWA support (original, @zpljd258) ② service worker hardening (reviewer feedback) ③ iOS presentation polish.

## Changes (10 files, no Python / build-system changes)

- **manifest.json** — `display: standalone`, icons 180/192/512 + maskable; named `.json` (the gateway doesn't map `.webmanifest`).
- **sw.js** — network-first navigation (shell refreshed on every successful load, with offline shell + deep-link fallback); cache-first only for hashed `/assets/`; `/api`, `/auth`, `/__nanobot`, `/webui` excluded from caching; the original `request` is passed to `fetch()` as-is so credentials are preserved; stale hashed assets pruned on both `activate` and shell refresh to prevent unbounded growth.
- **index.html** — manifest link + iOS metas + `viewport-fit=cover` + zoom disabled (system-level accessibility zoom unaffected). **main.tsx** — SW registered after `load` with `updateViaCache: "none"`; registration failures ignored. Plus 3 brand icons.
- **3 test files** — SW strategy / path exclusion / credentials / prune / offline / registration timing.

## Reviewer feedback addressed

- **hamb1y** — API/WebSocket paths excluded ✅, credentials preserved ✅; points 3–4 (backdrop-blur, vertical-only viewport) concern the swipe gesture, which is not part of this PR.
- **Automated review** — unbounded cache growth ✅, cached `index.html` staleness ✅.

## Testing

- `build` and `lint` clean; 11 new tests pass.
- Full suite: 997/999 pass; the 2 failures are pre-existing parallel-execution flakes that also reproduce on unmodified `main` and are unrelated to this PR.
- Manually verified on a real iPhone (iOS Safari): install, standalone launch, offline reload.

## Notes

- Server `immutable` headers for un-hashed brand assets are a possible follow-up.
- The mobile-layout fixes in #4693 are a prerequisite and are already on `main`.

Closes the PWA portion of #4479.

prs.title: feat(plugins): integrate Agent Plugins with CLI Apps
prs.body:
## Why

Agent Plugins v1 gives nanobot a vendor-neutral package boundary for portable skills and MCP runtimes. Projects such as `nanobot-dev/computer-use` can remain independent packages while nanobot stays a small generic host. CLI Apps also stop emitting an ad hoc workspace skill and use the same discovery path.

References:
- https://agent-plugins.org/specification
- https://github.com/HKUDS/CLI-Anything
- https://github.com/nanobot-dev/computer-use

## What changed

- discover and validate installed Agent Plugins v1 under `<workspace>/plugins/*`
- load direct-child plugin skills with deterministic precedence: workspace, plugin, built-in
- support explicitly enabled v1 `stdio` MCP components with `PLUGIN_ROOT` and isolated `PLUGIN_DATA`
- keep installed packages inert until the user enables them in the existing WebUI **Apps** catalog
- support skills-only, MCP-only, and combined packages through the same activation path
- reuse the existing MCP enable, disable, and hot-reload path
- show packaged identity, logo, and requested permissions before enable
- keep explicit `tools.mcpServers` configuration authoritative on host/UI name collisions
- package CLI Apps as skills-only Agent Plugins while preserving legacy installed skills
- preserve legacy underscore CLI App skill references and `disabledSkills` entries after migration
- reject path escapes, unsupported transports, reserved environment overrides, and unsafe executable paths
- reject duplicate manifest identities and bind activation to the package's canonical install root
- keep Agent Plugin catalog entries out of the composer's MCP `@` attachment candidates
- document the package layout, trust boundary, and current transport scope

## Design boundary

The agent core only asks `plugins.py` for plugin skills and MCP servers. Discovery, validation, activation state, path containment, and WebUI projection remain behind that boundary.

This PR intentionally does **not** add a second package manager. Downloading/acquiring and preparing a package belongs to its source or a future marketplace; presence under the plugins directory means installed, while activation remains an explicit nanobot trust decision. The portable v1 core currently hosts skills and local `stdio` MCP servers. Unsupported components are skipped independently.

## Security and compatibility

- one activation identity maps to exactly one canonical installed package
- a moved or replacement package cannot inherit an earlier package's enable marker
- duplicate package identities are ignored instead of being resolved by directory order
- legacy CLI Apps, explicit MCP configuration precedence, and installations with no plugins retain their existing behavior
- migrated CLI Apps retain their previous `$skill_name` and `disabledSkills` identity as an alias

## Hands-on verification

- validated the real `nanobot-dev/computer-use` package against the host after its external prerequisites were prepared
- compiled its universal macOS helper and connected its MCP server
- nanobot registered both `browser` and `computer_use` tools, then disconnected cleanly
- full Python suite: `6276 passed, 11 skipped`
- full WebUI suite: `990 passed`
- WebUI production build: passed
- `ruff`: passed
- `basedpyright`: 0 errors, 0 warnings

## Reduction pass

The branch is rebuilt as one commit on current `main`, including the split Settings architecture. The host setup/version/locking subprocess lifecycle remains excluded as premature distribution policy. The final diff is `+1111/-110`; the added compatibility seam preserves legacy CLI App identities without weakening the portable Agent Skills naming contract.

prs.body:
## Summary

- merge Chat Completions `extraBody.tools` into nanobot's generated top-level tool list
- keep ordinary `extraBody` fields on the existing recursive last-write-wins path
- document optional OpenRouter web search and fetch server tools

OpenRouter server tools through `extraBody.tools` therefore replaced every generated nanobot
function, including unrelated capabilities such as `write_file`.

The provider now treats `tools` as a reserved Chat Completions field and appends configured tool
lists, matching the existing Responses API behavior.

Closes #5333.

beta-service execution was not exercised locally; the verification covers nanobot's outbound wire
contract without external requests or charges.

prs.title: fix(providers): DeepSeek message hardening — preserve content, sanitize null/empty
prs.body:
## 问题

DeepSeek（v4-pro / v4-flash）在以下情况会拒绝消息或产生异常输出：

1. **null 内容导致 400 错误** — `tool` 或 `user` 消息的 `content` 字段为 `null` 时，DeepSeek API 直接返回 400
2. **"(empty)" 占位符泄漏** — `_coerce_content_to_string` 的兜底值 `"(empty)"` 被当作普通文本注入对话，模型会尝试"解释"这个占位符
3. **assistant 文本被无条件丢弃** — `_sanitize_messages` 在存在 `tool_calls` 时一律将 `content` 置为 `None`，即使用户本应看到"我帮你查一下"这样的对话文本

## 改动（1 个文件，+16/-10）

### 1. `_coerce_content_to_string` — 不再返回 None 或 "(empty)"

| 场景 | 之前 | 之后 |
|------|------|------|
| `content=None` | 返回 `None` → DeepSeek 400 | 返回 `" "`（单空格，DeepSeek 接受） |
| `content="(empty)"` | 直接透传 → 模型"解释"占位符 | 返回 `" "` |
| 兜底 fallback | `"(empty)"` 字符串 | `" "` |
| 返回类型 | `str \| None` | `str` |

### 2. `_sanitize_messages` — DeepSeek 下保留 assistant 文本

- `clean["content"] = None`（清空 assistant 文本）仅在 **非** DeepSeek 提供者时执行
- 移除 `force_string_content` 块中对 `assistant + tool_calls` 的豁免：所有角色均走内容清洗

## 决策：方案 A 胜出

针对 assistant 消息含 `tool_calls` 时是否保留文本，有过两种方案：

| | 方案 A（采用） | 方案 B（否决） |
|--|:--:|:--:|
| 行为 | **保留** assistant 文本 | **丢弃** assistant 文本 |
| 用户体验 | ✅ 看到"我帮你查" + 工具调用 | ❌ 只剩工具调用，对话断裂 |
| 兼容风险 | 低（DeepSeek 原生支持 content+tools） | 无风险但 UX 退化 |

**核心理由**：用"可能"的远端网关兼容问题，去换"确定"的用户体验退化，不划算。

## 测试验证

在 [Nanobot Staging 空间](https://huggingface.co/spaces/DreamShepherd2006/Nanobot-Staging) 使用 `deepseek-v4-pro` 实测：

- 天气查询 → 3 次工具调用 → assistant 文本完整保留 → 无 400 错误
- tool/user 消息 null 内容 → 成功清洗为单空格
- `"(empty)"` 占位符不再出现
- 非 DeepSeek 提供者：行为不变

## 审核反馈响应 (2026-05-19)

### Point 1 — `"(empty)"` 向上游修复
- 将 `_sanitize_empty_content` 中两处 `"(empty)"` 替换为 `""`
- 所有 provider 不再收到泄露的占位字符串，各自在 provider 层处理空内容

### Point 2 — 保留返回类型
- `_coerce_content_to_string` 恢复 `str | None` 签名
- 调用方（`_sanitize_messages` 内 `force_string_content` 分支）处理 `None → " "`

### Point 3 — 声明式 ProviderSpec 字段
- 新增 `preserve_content_with_tool_calls: bool = False`
- DeepSeek 设为 `True`，替代原有 `not force_string_content` 硬编码条件
- 后续 provider 可直接设置此字段，无需修改 `_sanitize_messages`

### Point 4 — API 兼容性依据
- DeepSeek API 遵循 OpenAI Chat Completions 格式
- OpenAI spec 定义 `content` 字段为 `string or null`，与 `tool_calls` 可并存
- 实证验证：Staging 环境 (deepseek-v4-pro, thinking=enabled) 持续通过，无 400 错误
- 用户侧收益：保留模型自然语言引导语（如 "Let me look that up for you"），改善多步工具调用体验

This fixes a limitation in the current openai_codex provider.

prs.title: refactor: comprehensive hardening and feature improvements
prs.body:
Security:
- Replace global _processing_lock with per-session locks: messages for different sessions/channels now run concurrently; only same-session messages are serialised (eliminates the de-facto single-threaded agent)
- Scrub sensitive arg names (token/api_key/secret/password/etc.) from logs
- Show workspace path as ~/... in system prompt instead of full absolute path
- Add 30-second timeout to MCP HTTP client (was timeout=None)
- Gateway warns loudly at startup when allowFrom is empty for any channel
- Gateway refuses to run as root on Linux/macOS (prints warning)
- WhatsApp bridge token passed via temp 0600 file (BRIDGE_TOKEN_FILE) instead of plain env var to avoid /proc/<pid>/environ exposure
- Docker: add dedicated nanobot user; container no longer runs as root (config dir moves to /home/nanobot/.nanobot — update volume mounts)

Features:
- Per-channel model routing: each channel config accepts an optional model field; when set it overrides the global agents.defaults.model
- Subagents now inherit MCP tools and cron scheduling from the parent AgentLoop (SubagentManager receives mcp_servers + cron_service)
- Session cleanup CLI: `nanobot sessions list` and `nanobot sessions cleanup --days N` for managing JSONL history files

Fixes:
- Memory consolidation race: snapshot session.messages before first await in background consolidation task, preventing non-deterministic inclusion of concurrently written messages
- _TOOL_RESULT_MAX_CHARS raised 500 → 5000 to preserve tool context across resumed sessions

Tooling:
- Add .github/workflows/ci.yml: Python (ruff, pytest, pip-audit) and Node.js (npm audit, npm build) CI pipeline

Docs:
- CHANGELOG.md: first changelog covering all changes since v0.1.4

prs.title: feat(telegram): per-chat group policy overrides
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds per-chat `group_policy` overrides for the Telegram channel (RFC #3309).

### Problem

The Telegram channel only supported a single global `group_policy` setting. Users running one bot across multiple groups couldn't express:
- Group A: respond to all (copilot mode)
- Group B: respond only when mentioned (helper mode)
- Group C: outbound-only, ignore inbound (cron/Dream posting)

### Solution

New `chat_policy` config dict maps chat IDs to per-chat policies:

```yaml
telegram:
  groupPolicy: mention  # default fallback
  chatPolicy:
    "-1001234567890": "open"   # Group A - respond to all
    "-1009876543210": "muted"  # Group C - receive nothing
```

New policy value `"muted"` means inbound messages are dropped before reaching the agent loop, but outbound (cron, scheduled tasks) still works.

### Changes

1. **TelegramConfig**: Added `chat_policy: dict[str, Literal["open", "mention", "muted"]]`
2. **_is_group_message_for_bot**: Checks per-chat policy first, handles "muted" to drop inbound
3. **New group logging**: First message from a new group logs at INFO level for discoverability
4. **/chatid command**: Returns current chat ID so users can copy it into config

### Backward Compatibility

- `chat_policy` defaults to `{}` - absent entries fall back to `group_policy`
- No behavior change for existing users

## Testing

- 8 new tests covering: open override, muted drops inbound, mention fallback, logging
- All 61 telegram tests pass

Fixes #3309

prs.title: feat(agent): skip LLM processing for read_only sessions
prs.body:
## 需求

支持通过 session metadata 标记只读会话。平台构建者可通过设置 `metadata.read_only = true`，让指定的 pinned 会话（如系统配置页、项目指南、FAQ 等）禁止触发 LLM，仅返回静态提示。

## 方案

在消息循环入口 `run()` 中，`create_task(_dispatch)` 之前检查 session metadata 的 `read_only` 字段。若为 true，直接回复提示并 `continue`——不创建 task，不消耗并发槽位，不获取 session lock/gate。

```python
session = self.sessions.get_or_create(effective_key)
if session.metadata.get("read_only"):
    await self.bus.publish_outbound(OutboundMessage(...))
    continue
task = asyncio.create_task(self._dispatch(msg))
```

**与上一版的主要区别**：guard 从 `_dispatch` 内部（`async with lock, gate:` 之内）hoist 到 `run()` 中 `create_task` 之前——真正零开销，且覆盖所有消息路径（含 mid-turn injection）。

## 改动

`nanobot/agent/loop.py` `run()` 方法，+9 行。

## 影响

- pinned 会话的误触消息不再发起 LLM 调用
- metadata 纯扩展字段，不影响现有会话

prs.title: feat(ws): accept target_chat_id hint in new_chat for session recovery
prs.body:
## 背景

这是原始云平台 PR（#4139）讨论后拆出的第二个小 PR。
审核者 @chengyongru 建议将大的部署层改动拆分为聚焦的单点 PR。

本 PR 处理 **会话恢复**：云/本地部署中，页面刷新后 WebUI 发送 `new_chat`
导致历史丢失的问题。

## 问题

nanobot WebSocket 的 `_dispatch_envelope` 在处理 `new_chat` 时无条件生成新
`chat_id`：

```python
if t == "new_chat":
    new_id = str(uuid.uuid4())  # 永远新建
```

这意味着页面刷新 → WebUI 重新连接 → `new_chat` → 全新会话 → 历史清空。

外部身份层（OAuth proxy / gatekeeper）无法干预——envelope 里没有字段能提示
"请回到之前的会话"。

## 解决方案

在 `new_chat` envelope 中接受可选的 `target_chat_id` 字段。存在且有效时复用，
否则回退到 `uuid.uuid4()`。

### 改动

`nanobot/channels/websocket.py` — `_dispatch_envelope` 中 `new_chat` 分支：

```diff
 if t == "new_chat":
+    target_cid = envelope.get("target_chat_id")
+    new_id = target_cid if _is_valid_chat_id(target_cid) else str(uuid.uuid4())
-    new_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
```

仅用现有 API（`_is_valid_chat_id`），零新抽象。

### 端到端场景

```
用户刷新页面 → OAuth proxy / gatekeeper 注入 target_chat_id
                ↓
        envelope: {"type": "new_chat", "target_chat_id": "abc123"}
                ↓
        _dispatch_envelope → 复用 "abc123"，会话恢复
```

Gatekeeper 维护 `external_user → chat_id` 映射，在转发前注入字段——与客户端
使用 `attach` 恢复会话等价，但不需要客户端感知 chat_id。

## 为什么这个改动不同于 #4134

#4134 试图在 `_dispatch_envelope` 里加 `is_allowed` 权限检查——但那已经被
WebSocket upgrade 阶段的 token 校验覆盖了，是死代码。

本 PR 的 `new_chat` 分支**不在任何前置鉴权之后**——只要客户端通过了 WS upgrade
（token 认证已由 nanobot 自身处理），发送 `new_chat` envelope 必然走到这里。
不涉及安全模型的改动，纯粹是协议能力增强。

## 影响

- **向后兼容**：无 `target_chat_id` 时，回退到 `uuid.uuid4()`，行为完全不变
- **1 文件，2 行**：`nanobot/channels/websocket.py`
- **无安全影响**：不影响 token 认证流程，不新增攻击面

## 关联

- PR #4134（已关）：从中确认了 token 是唯一安全边界的设计哲学
- PR #4139（原始）：完整云平台部署层讨论，按建议拆分

prs.body:
## Summary

Add per-turn token usage logging to `{workspace}/usage/log.jsonl` and a
`/insights [days]` slash command to query historical usage by model.

This directly addresses community requests:
- Closes #2020 — Simple usage logging for token/cost tracking
- Closes #3731 — `/insights` command for historical token usage tracking

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `nanobot/utils/usage_log.py` | **New** — Append-only JSONL logger with aggregation and 90-day rotation |
| `nanobot/agent/loop.py` | Log per-turn `result.usage` to the usage log after each LLM call |
| `nanobot/command/builtin.py` | Add `/insights [days]` command (default: 7 days) |

## Design

- **No new dependencies** — stdlib `json` + `time` only
- **Zero overhead when unused** — single `open().write()` per turn
- **Auto-rotation** — records older than 90 days are pruned on write
- **"零件" (parts) strategy** — exposes raw usage data without building
  dashboards, visualizations, or alerting. Users get visibility into
  consumption but still need external tools (e.g. Token Efficiency) for
  cost dashboards and anomaly detection.

### /insights output example

```
📊 Usage — last 7 day(s)

Turns:      142
Tokens:     1,283,450
  Prompt:   1,021,200
  Output:   262,250

Models:
  deepseek-v4-flash: 1.1M tokens
  mimo-v2.5-pro: 180k tokens
```

## Test Plan

- [ ] Run `pytest tests/` to verify no regressions
- [ ] Start nanobot, send a few messages, run `/insights` — verify output
- [ ] Check `{workspace}/usage/log.jsonl` exists and contains valid JSONL

prs.title: feat(ws): emit peers_update event from NANOBOT_PEER_* env vars
prs.body:
# PR: feat(ws): emit peers_update event from NANOBOT_PEER_* env vars

**Target:** `upstream:nightly` ← `feat/peers-update-ws-event`

**Link:** https://github.com/DreamShepherd2006/nanobot/compare/nightly...feat/peers-update-ws-event?expand=1

---

## 问题

`NANOBOT_PEER_*` 环境变量允许用户声明多 agent 拓扑信息，但前端无法获取这些数据——既不能走 `/webui/bootstrap`（那是 human-facing 的 token 端点），也没有其他机制暴露。

## 改动

1 个文件 (`nanobot/channels/websocket.py`)，+46/-0。

| 改动 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| `import os` | `_read_peers()` 需要读环境变量 |
| `WebSocketConfig.peers_enabled: bool = False` | 新配置项，默认关闭，向后兼容 |
| `_read_peers()` 函数 | 解析所有 `NANOBOT_PEER_*` env var，返回 `{name: {id, gateway_port, ws_port}}` |
| `peers_update` WS 事件 | 在 `_connection_loop()` 中，hydration 完成后立即 emit |

**数据流：**

```
NANOBOT_PEER_* (env)
       ↓
WS connect → auth → ready → hydrate
       ↓
peers_update event (if peers_enabled and peers exist)
       ↓
Frontend via onAnyEvent listener
```

## 决策

| 方案 | 位置 | 结论 |
|------|------|------|
| A. 注入 bootstrap 响应 | HTTP，未认证可访问 | ❌ bootstrap 是 human-facing token 端点，不应承载服务发现数据 |
| B. 独立 `/api/peers` 端点 | HTTP，需认证 | ❌ 需要额外认证层，WS 已有认证通道 |
| **C. WS `peers_update` 事件** | **WebSocket，已认证** | **✅ 与现有 WS 通道一致，hydration 后立即推送** |

**关键设计决策：**

- **默认关闭** (`peers_enabled=False`)：单 agent 部署不受影响，多 agent 用户 opt-in
- **无外部依赖**：仅用 stdlib (`os`, `json`)，不引入 squad_config_sync 等定制逻辑
- **防御性解析**：非法 JSON / 缺失 `id` 字段 → skip，不抛异常

## 验证

Staging 环境测试通过：

```
$ python3 -c "
import asyncio, websockets, json, os
async def test():
    ws = await websockets.connect(f'ws://127.0.0.1:{ws_port}/?token={token}')
    for _ in range(3):
        evt = json.loads(await ws.recv())
        print(evt['event'])

#1 → ready
#2 → peers_update    ✅
#3 → (timeout, no more events)
```

`peers_update` 在 WS 握手后作为第 2 个事件推送，紧跟 `ready`。

prs.title: feat(memory): compress long tool results before LLM consolidation
prs.body:
## Summary

When archiving idle sessions, individual tool results (file reads, shell outputs)
can be 10k+ characters, dominating the archive LLM's input and drowning out
actual conversation logic.

This adds `Consolidator._compress_tool_results()` — a static truncation pass
that runs before `_format_messages()` in `archive()`. Tool results exceeding
2000 chars are truncated to a 2000-char preview with a `…(compressed N chars)`
marker.

Since both `AutoCompact._archive()` and `maybe_consolidate_by_tokens()` call
`archive()`, one change covers all consolidation paths.

## Before / After

Tested with DeepSeek on a realistic 7-turn debugging session (16 messages,
5 large tool results):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Archive input | 27,505 chars | 6,516 chars |
| Prompt tokens | 7,119 | 1,910 |
| Total tokens | 7,147 | 1,948 |
| **Savings** | — | **73%** |
| Summary quality | 1 fact extracted | 2 facts extracted |

Without compression, the input was 90% config boilerplate and log lines —
the LLM was overwhelmed. With compression, it correctly identified both key
facts from the conversation.

## Test plan

- [x] Standalone comparison script included: `tests/agent/test_tool_result_compression.py`

prs.title: feat(agent): add before_process hook for message preprocessing
prs.body:
## Summary

- Add `before_process` async callback to the agent hook system, fired before `extract_documents` in the agent loop
- Extend `AgentHookContext` with `media` and `media_text` fields for hook-based media preprocessing
- Wire `before_process` through `CompositeHook` to support multiple hooks

## Motivation

The current hook system provides `before_iteration` / `after_iteration` callbacks that operate within the agent loop, but there is no hook point for preprocessing raw media content **before** the loop processes it. This means any media transformation (e.g. converting images to text) would require modifying core loop logic.

This PR adds a lightweight `before_process` entry point that enables custom hooks to intercept and transform media content without touching the core agent loop.

No behavior change when no hooks are registered.

## Future Use Cases

This hook is a foundation for several planned features:

- **Vision processor**: Convert images to text descriptions via a vision model, allowing non-multimodal models to handle image input
- **Audio transcription**: Transcribe audio files to text via ASR, expanding the agent's supported input formats
- **Custom document parsing**: Allow users to replace or extend the built-in `extract_documents` behavior for special file formats

## Test Plan

- [x] Verify existing tests pass: `pytest tests/`
- [x] Confirm no regression in agents without custom hooks (default `_extra_hooks=[]`)
- [x] Manual test: register a dummy hook with `before_process` and verify it is called before `extract_documents`

prs.title: feat(my): persist focus key to session metadata for auto-injection
prs.body:
Hi @chengyongru , i have  implemented the refined approach exactly as you proposed for #3292 . 

  ## Summary                                                                                                                                                            
   
  Reuses the existing `my` tool with a session-persistent `focus` key — no new tool, no new prompt, no compactor changes, no reminder mechanism. The agent decides when 
  to set or overwrite focus based on its own judgment.      

  ## Changes (the three touchpoints)

  **1. `nanobot/agent/tools/self.py`**
  - `_modify()` intercepts `key == "focus"` and routes to a new `_modify_focus()` helper that writes to `session.metadata["_focus"]` instead of `_runtime_vars`.
  - Empty/`None` value clears the focus; non-string values rejected.
  - `set_context()` now also receives `session_key` so the tool can resolve the live session.

  **2. `nanobot/agent/context.py`**
  - `_build_runtime_context()` accepts a `focus` kwarg and appends `Current Focus: {focus}` to the runtime metadata block when present — same injection pattern as
  `session_summary`.

  **3. `nanobot/agent/loop.py`**
  - `_set_tool_context()` passes `session_key=effective_key` to the `my` tool.
  - Both `build_messages` call sites in `_process_message` now pass `focus=session.metadata.get("_focus")`.

  ## Behavior verified

  -  Survives compaction — re-injected every turn, independent of conversation history.
  -  Survives restarts — persisted in `session.metadata` like `_last_summary`.
  -  Overwrites naturally — `my(set, key="focus", value="next task")` just replaces the prior value.
  -  Empty value clears.
  -  Does **not** spill into `_runtime_vars` (would defeat the point).

  ## Tests

  9 new tests, all passing alongside the existing 158 in the related suites:

  - `tests/agent/tools/test_self_tool.py::TestFocusKey` — write to `session.metadata`, overwrite, clear-on-empty, non-string rejection, missing-session-key error, no
  scratchpad spill.
  - `tests/agent/tools/test_self_tool.py::TestSetContext::test_set_context_stores_session_key`
  - `tests/agent/test_context_prompt_cache.py::test_runtime_context_includes_focus_when_provided`
  - `tests/agent/test_context_prompt_cache.py::test_runtime_context_omits_focus_when_absent`

prs.title: fix(security): harden public-deploy footguns + browser-CSRF on /v1/*
prs.body:
## Problem

When operators front nanobot with a public tunnel or reverse proxy (cloudflared, ngrok, nginx), three configurations silently turn dangerous; a fourth even on default loopback lets any website drive the local agent. nanobot is built around a single-user, single-machine deployment model — these surfaces were meant for same-host use, but nothing in the code stopped them from being silently exposed.

- **`/webui/bootstrap`** mints a token that authorizes the WebSocket handshake plus the `/api/sessions` read/delete REST surface (the delete route really unlinks the session JSONL). The localhost gate trusts only the TCP peer, so a tunnel running on the same host (peer = 127.0.0.1) defeats it.
- **`nanobot serve`** has no auth at all on `/v1/*`. Pointing `--host 0.0.0.0` (or fronting it with a proxy) exposes `/v1/chat/completions` to the world. The CLI only printed a `console.print` warning.
- **WebSocket token-issue route** issues tokens to anyone when `tokenIssuePath` is set without `tokenIssueSecret`. Logged a warning and proceeded.
- **Default `serve` on 127.0.0.1 is reachable from any browser tab.** A `no-cors` fetch with `Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8` is browser-simple (no preflight) and was reaching `agent.process_direct(...)` with attacker-controlled `session_id`/message.

## Fix

### WebUI bootstrap (`nanobot/channels/websocket.py`)

- Refuse when the channel's bind host is not a loopback address. A non-loopback bind is an explicit public posture; the implicit token mint is unsafe there.
- Reject requests carrying standard proxy-hop headers (`X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Real-IP`, `Forwarded`) even when the TCP peer is loopback — catches the common tunnel-on-same-host shape.
- New `webuiBootstrapDisabled: bool = false` config so operators behind a proxy that strips/omits the headers can hard-disable the route.
- Recognize the full IPv4 `127.0.0.0/8` loopback range plus IPv6 `::1` via `ipaddress.is_loopback`, not just three literals.

### WebSocket channel startup

Refuse to start when bind is non-loopback **and** either:
- `tokenIssuePath` is set without `tokenIssueSecret`, **or**
- there is no token gate at all (`websocketRequiresToken: false` with no static `token`).

Heuristics are easy to defeat with a custom proxy. A hard error at startup is harder to ignore than a console warning at request time.

### OpenAI-compatible API auth (`nanobot/api/server.py`, `nanobot/cli/commands.py`)

- New `api.authToken` config + `--auth-token` CLI flag.
- Aiohttp middleware enforces `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on `/v1/*` when configured; `/health` stays open for liveness probes.
- CLI refuses to start when bind is non-loopback and no auth token is set.

### Browser-CSRF protection on `/v1/*` (loopback included)

Even when `authToken` is unset, the browser-localhost vector is closed. CSRF middleware on `POST /v1/*`:
- **Rejects any `Origin` not in `api.allowedOrigins`** (403). Empty allowlist means "no browsers"; non-browser clients (curl, openai-python, LiteLLM) don't send `Origin` and pass.
- **Requires Content-Type `application/json` or `multipart/form-data`** (415). Closes the `text/plain` simple-request path that bypasses preflight.
- `/health` and `GET /v1/models` stay exempt (no side effects).
- New `--allowed-origin` flag and `api.allowedOrigins` config for explicit cross-origin allowlisting (e.g. WebUI deployments).

This addresses @Hinotoi-agent's review feedback (browser-localhost variant); the reviewer's PoC is reproduced as a regression test (`test_v1_blocks_text_plain_csrf_via_origin`) and now returns 403 without reaching the agent.

### Backwards compatibility

- All defaults preserve current local-only behavior. No `auth_token` = no Bearer middleware = no behavior change for non-browser clients.
- `webuiBootstrapDisabled` defaults to `false`.
- `allowedOrigins` defaults to `[]`. Browser clients with an `Origin` header now require allowlisting; curl/openai-python/LiteLLM are unaffected.
- The startup refusals only fire on non-loopback binds, so existing local installs are unaffected.

## Tests

```
$ uv run pytest tests/channels/test_websocket_http_routes.py \
    tests/channels/test_websocket_channel.py::test_websocket_requires_token_without_issue_path \
    tests/channels/test_websocket_channel.py::test_http_route_issues_token_then_websocket_requires_it \
    tests/test_api_auth.py tests/cli/test_commands.py -q
```

Coverage:
- `test_bootstrap_rejects_x_forwarded_for` / `test_bootstrap_rejects_forwarded_header` — bootstrap → 403 with proxy-hop headers
- `test_start_refuses_public_token_issue_without_secret` / `test_start_refuses_public_bind_without_token_gate` — channel raises at start
- `test_v1_requires_bearer_when_auth_token_set` / `test_v1_models_requires_bearer` / `test_health_is_exempt_from_auth` / `test_no_auth_token_keeps_v1_open` — Bearer middleware
- `test_v1_blocks_text_plain_csrf_via_origin` / `test_v1_allows_origin_in_allowlist` / `test_v1_allows_no_origin_request` / `test_v1_models_skips_csrf` — browser-CSRF middleware
- `test_serve_refuses_non_loopback_without_auth_token` / `test_serve_passes_auth_token_to_create_app` / `test_serve_reads_auth_token_from_config` — CLI wiring

End-to-end smoke (run locally):

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| loopback bind, plain `GET /webui/bootstrap` | 200 + token | ✅ |
| loopback bind, `X-Forwarded-For` header | 403 | ✅ |
| loopback bind, `Forwarded:` header | 403 | ✅ |
| non-loopback bind, bootstrap | 403 | ✅ |
| non-loopback + no secret + no static token | refuses to start (`ValueError`) | ✅ |
| `webuiBootstrapDisabled: true` | 403 | ✅ |
| `127.0.0.5` (non-`.1` loopback) recognized | true | ✅ |
| loopback `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `Origin: https://evil.example`, `text/plain` | 403 | ✅ |
| loopback `POST /v1/chat/completions` from curl (no Origin, application/json) | 200 | ✅ |
| `--allowed-origin https://evil.example` then same browser request | 200 | ✅ |

## Docs

- `docs/deployment.md`: new "Exposing nanobot publicly" section with the explicit recommendation, the WS-only public profile, and the rationale for fail-loud over heuristics; new "Browser-localhost CSRF" subsection covering `allowedOrigins`.
- `docs/websocket.md`: documents `webuiBootstrapDisabled` and the refuse-to-start guards under Authentication.

## Targeting

Per `CONTRIBUTING.md`: this PR adds new config fields (`api.authToken`, `api.allowedOrigins`, `webuiBootstrapDisabled`) and changes startup behavior for non-loopback binds, so it targets `nightly`. No behavior change for default local installs except that browser clients with an `Origin` header now need allowlisting.

## Commits

- `fix(security): harden public-deploy footguns on WebUI bootstrap and API serve`
- `fix(security): block browser-CSRF on /v1/* even on loopback`

prs.title: feat(tools): reduce context-window token usage - compact schemas & lazy MCP load (Stages 2C + 2A)
prs.body:
This PR bundles two independent token-efficiency features. Each can be reviewed commit-by-commit; they share no coupling beyond the config schema.

## Commit 1 — Compact Tool Schemas (Stage 2C)

Strips verbose fields from tool schemas before passing them to the LLM, reducing per-turn context token consumption.

When enabled, `get_definitions()` post-processes each schema:
- **Parameter `description` and `default` fields** are stripped
- **Long enum lists** (> 5 values) are collapsed to just the parameter type
- **Top-level descriptions** are truncated to a configurable character limit

```json
{ "tools": { "compactSchemas": true, "compactSchemasMaxDescLength": 80 } }
```

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `tools.compactSchemas` | `false` | Strip verbose fields from tool schemas |
| `tools.compactSchemasMaxDescLength` | `80` | Max chars for top-level descriptions (0 = no truncation) |

Tests: `tests/tools/test_tool_registry_compact.py` (13 tests)

## Commit 2 — MCP Lazy Load (Stage 2A)

Defers MCP server connections until a server is actually needed by the agent, eliminating schema tokens for servers never used in a session.

**How it works:**
1. At startup, one thin proxy tool (`mcp_<server>__proxy`) is registered per MCP server instead of all its real tools
2. On first call the proxy connects, registers the real tools/resources/prompts, removes itself, and returns the list of newly available tool names
3. If the connection fails the proxy stays registered so the agent can retry
4. Concurrent calls are serialised via `asyncio.Lock` — connect fires exactly once

`connect_single_mcp_server()` is extracted from an inner closure to a module-level function so the proxy can reuse the same transport logic without duplication.

```json
{ "tools": { "mcpLazyLoad": true } }
```

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `tools.mcpLazyLoad` | `false` | Register one proxy per MCP server at startup; connect on demand |

Tests: `tests/tools/test_mcp_lazy_load.py` (12 tests)

## Design decisions

- **Proxy name format** `mcp_<server>__proxy` — double underscore distinguishes proxies from real tools (which use `mcp_<server>_<tool>`)
- **Failure behaviour** — proxy stays registered and returns a string starting with `"Error"` so it is never served from the tool result cache (Stage 2B)
- **Full schemas preserved internally** — `_cached_definitions` always stores originals; compact output is derived at return time so the flag can safely be toggled mid-session
