issues.title: Automation runs are hit-or-miss: unattended runs execute as plain interactive chat turns

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Epic issue tracking a larger initiative

issues.body:
## Problem

Automation runs are hit-or-miss: the same stored prompt sometimes succeeds and sometimes produces nothing useful, especially on small models (DeepSeek V4 Flash). Audit of the trigger → run pipeline (2026-07-30) shows this is structural, not model noise: **a trigger fire is executed as a completely ordinary interactive chat turn** — same system prompt, full tool surface, fresh empty thread — with no signal that the run is unattended, no scoping, and no outcome checking.

## Root causes (verified in code)

1. **No unattended-mode prompt.** The base system prompt (`crates/ironclaw_reborn_composition/assets/prompts/default-system.md`) instructs the model to *ask the user* when unsure — but no user is present. Small models routinely end automation runs with a clarifying question, which terminates as `Completed`/`Ok`. The antidote text already exists (`assets/prompts/benchmarking-mode.md`: "no human on the other end … never end a turn with a question") but is gated on the process-wide `BENCHMARKING_MODE` env var, not on `TurnOriginKind::ScheduledTrigger` (`crates/ironclaw_reborn_composition/src/root/default_system_prompt.rs:100-112`).
2. **Failed runs are silent.** `triggered_notification_for_state` only produces output for `Completed` / `BlockedApproval` / `BlockedAuth`; `Failed`, `Cancelled`, `RecoveryRequired` fall through to `Ok(None)` → `Skipped` (`crates/ironclaw_product/src/run_delivery/triggered.rs:703`). The user can't distinguish "failed" from "never fired".
3. **Full interactive tool surface.** The `scheduled_trigger` run profile is the interactive profile minus exactly 4 trigger-mutator capabilities (`crates/ironclaw_runner/src/planned_driver_factory.rs:279`, `crates/ironclaw_runner/src/runtime.rs:888`). No per-automation tool allowlist or skill pinning — tool-choice errors are the dominant small-model failure mode.
4. **Zero structure in the automation record.** `TriggerRecord` stores a raw prompt string plus schedule/delivery (`crates/ironclaw_triggers/src/lib.rs:326`); `builtin.trigger_create` takes 4 fields (`crates/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/trigger_management.rs:417`). No goal, success criteria, tool scope, output shape, or model pin.
5. **No task-level retry.** `retry_disposition()` has zero production callers (`crates/ironclaw_runner/src/retry_disposition.rs:106`); the pre-submit trigger retry lane is unbounded with no backoff (`crates/ironclaw_triggers/src/in_memory.rs:404-441`).
6. **Completion nudge misses the common failure.** `reply_trailed_off` only matches empty-or-ends-with-`:` (`crates/ironclaw_agent_loop/src/executor/loop_exit.rs:34`) — a reply ending in a question is never nudged.
7. **Approval gates park unattended runs.** `ScheduledLoopRun` collapses into the `loop_run` lane (`crates/ironclaw_host_api/src/capability.rs:134`); a gated tool call parks the fire and DMs the creator mid-run.
8. **No cross-run continuity.** Every fire gets a fresh thread keyed on `(tenant, trigger, fire_slot)` — no "last run's output" context.

## Benchmark: Hermes agent (NousResearch/hermes-agent) cron lane

Hermes automations are also raw prompt + fresh session, with **no task retry and no success evaluator** (parity with us). Their reliability comes from elsewhere:

- Hard-coded cron preamble: "running as a scheduled cron job, no user present, cannot ask questions, final response auto-delivered, reply `[SILENT]` to suppress delivery".
- Per-job **toolset allowlist**; `cronjob`/`messaging`/`clarify` force-disabled for cron runs.
- Per-job **model/provider pin**, attached skills, prior-job output chaining (`context_from`, 8 KB cap).
- **Operator-authored pre-run scripts** as the determinism seam (script fetches data deterministically; the model only summarizes); `no_agent=true` skips the LLM entirely; a `wakeAgent:false` gate skips the run.
- **Blueprints**: typed-slot prompt templates for common automations; docs mandate self-contained prompts and running a job once manually before trusting the schedule.
- **Failures always deliver**, summarized to one line.

Design philosophy worth copying: don't make the model deterministic — move the deterministic work out of the model, shrink the blast radius, make every outcome visible.

## Fix ladder

**P0 — highest leverage, small diffs**
- [x] Origin-conditional unattended preamble keyed on `TurnOriginKind::ScheduledTrigger` (adapt benchmarking-mode text; add a `[SILENT]`-style suppression sentinel and "your final reply is the delivered output").
- [x] Deliver failures: add `Failed`/`RecoveryRequired` arms at `triggered.rs:703` with a one-line failure summary.

**P1 — structure the automation record**
- [ ] Per-automation tool allowlist + pinned skills on `TriggerRecord` (+ libSQL/Postgres migrations, `trigger_create` schema).
- [ ] Force structured, self-contained prompts at creation time via `TRIGGER_CREATE_DESCRIPTION`/schema: goal, steps, success criteria, output format, nothing-to-report condition. Plan once at creation (strong model + user present), execute the frozen plan every fire.
- [ ] Run-once-now verification as part of the creation flow before arming the schedule.
- [ ] Per-automation model pin (route hard automations to a stronger model, cheap digests to Flash).

**P2 — hardening**
- [ ] Wire `retry_disposition()` into the turn scheduler; bound the pre-submit retry lane with backoff.
- [ ] Widen the completion-nudge heuristic to catch question-ending replies; treat empty final replies as failure, not Ok.
- [ ] Creation-time approval preflight: verify required grants when the automation is created, not at 3am mid-run.
- [ ] Optional `context_from`-style chaining: inject the previous run's output (capped) for recurring automations.

**Deliberately not copied from Hermes:** their lack of success evaluation. A cheap "does the output satisfy the stored success criteria" check on top of P1's structured record is a differentiator they don't have.

## Related

- #6369 (heartbeat/proactive loop not ported)
- #5505 (scheduled_trigger deny-map — the existing profile seam)
- Contract drift: `docs/reborn/contracts/triggers.md` §3.4 documents `completion_policy`, which no longer exists in code.

issues.title: Cache: place explicit Anthropic cache_control breakpoints (rig adapter + OAuth transport)

labels.name: scope: llm
labels.description: LLM integration

labels.name: reborn
labels.description: IronClaw Reborn architecture and landing work

labels.name: p0
labels.description: Vanta recognized label for security vulnerabilities

labels.name: performance
labels.description: Runtime performance / hot-path optimization

issues.body:
Part of the pi-harness adoption program (P0 #1) — see `docs/research/pi-agent-deep-dive.md` §7.3.

**Current behavior**
- The rig adapter injects a single top-level `cache_control` into the request root and relies on Anthropic *automatic* caching: `crates/ironclaw_llm/src/rig_adapter.rs:1086-1095`.
- The OAuth/subscription transport sends **no cache markers at all** — `AnthropicRequest` has no `cache_control` field and only reads back cache counters: `crates/ironclaw_llm/src/anthropic_oauth.rs:485-490`.
- Measured consequence: prompt-cache hit rate collapses 82% → 29% past ~200 model calls (~3.5× input cost) — recorded in `crates/ironclaw_runner/src/model_gateway/prompt_cache_activity.rs` header.

**Proposed change**
Place explicit `cache_control` breakpoints at the three stable boundaries, on both the API-key and OAuth paths:
1. system prompt block(s)
2. last tool definition only
3. last content block of the last user message

Reference implementation: pi's Anthropic adapter (`pi-mono/packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts:977-999, 1256-1281, 1320`), including short (5m) vs long (1h) retention and the 2× write premium on 1h TTL.

**Acceptance**
- Both Anthropic transports emit the three breakpoints; retention configurable (existing `ANTHROPIC_CACHE_RETENTION`).
- `prompt_cache_activity` shows sustained cache reads across a long run (integration-tier assertion at the gateway seam).

Depends on prefix stability (nudges/timestamp/tool-array issues) to actually pay off.

issues.title: Reveal long conversation titles on hover in the left navigation
issues.body:
## Steps

1. Open the WebUI with enough conversation history to display the left navigation.
2. Create or open a conversation whose generated title is wider than the available sidebar row.
3. View the conversation title in the left navigation.
4. Hover over the truncated title and try to read the complete text.

## Current Behavior

Long conversation titles are rendered with an ellipsis in the left navigation. Hovering the title does not reveal or scroll the hidden text.

Users cannot read the complete conversation title without opening the conversation and inferring its subject from the message history. Similar titles can become difficult to distinguish when their unique text appears after the truncated portion.

## Expected Behavior

Make overflowing conversation titles scroll horizontally while hovered.

The title should:

- Keep the current truncated, stationary presentation when it is not hovered.
- Start a smooth horizontal marquee when the rendered title exceeds its available width.
- Keep titles that fit within the row stationary.
- Reveal the complete title and loop seamlessly while hover remains active.
- Recalculate overflow when the title or sidebar dimensions change.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by disabling the animation.
- Preserve conversation selection, active-state styling, status indicators, pinning, deletion, and other row interactions.
- Keep other truncated labels unchanged.

Conversation naming, persistence, sidebar grouping, and thread activity metadata should remain with the existing WebUI flow.

issues.title: Epic: Storybook + an AI-first Design System (theming, assets, interactions, IA)

labels.name: module:M1-webui-product
labels.description: Reborn WebUI beta module M1: browser-facing WebUI/WebChat product surface

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Epic issue tracking a larger initiative

issues.body:
## 📐 Proposal, plan & review

This Epic is backed by a full proposal package (PR #7257), framed on the target crate-architecture docs (PR #6918) and the APDD governance kit:

| Doc | Role |
|---|---|
| [README](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/blob/docs/design-system-proposal/docs/reborn/design-system/README.md) | North-star overview |
| [PROPOSAL](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/blob/docs/design-system-proposal/docs/reborn/design-system/PROPOSAL.md) | Case, alternatives, and §7 dependencies with implementation proposals |
| [PLAN](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/blob/docs/design-system-proposal/docs/reborn/design-system/PLAN.md) | The five phases as waves — milestones, ⚠ ordering, next PRs |
| [CHECKLIST](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/blob/docs/design-system-proposal/docs/reborn/design-system/CHECKLIST.md) | Definition of done — WS1–WS7 |
| [explorer.html](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/blob/docs/design-system-proposal/docs/reborn/design-system/explorer.html) | Self-contained interactive review page (schematics + phase/dependency maps) |

**Interactive review:** open [explorer.html](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/blob/docs/design-system-proposal/docs/reborn/design-system/explorer.html) or [render it via html-preview](https://html-preview.github.io/?url=https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/blob/docs/design-system-proposal/docs/reborn/design-system/explorer.html) (self-contained, theme-aware, no build). Also published as a [claude.ai artifact](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/371a2622-054c-404a-8992-f110e1fa3d5a) (private by default — share from its page for teammates).

---

## Problem

IronClaw's WebUI (`crates/ironclaw_webui/frontend`) has grown a real component
surface — a `design-system/` primitives layer, `components/`/`layout/`
composites, and design tokens in `styles/app.css` — but there is no shared,
**governed design system**: no living catalog, no written guidelines for how
primitives/tokens/interactions are built and evolved, and the current
look-and-feel and interaction model predate IronClaw's shift to an
**AI/agentic-first** product.

This Epic makes the design system a first-class, governed part of the codebase
and evolves the WebUI's theming, visual assets, interactions, and information
architecture toward an agent-first UX — where streaming agent output,
tool/capability transparency, approvals/gates, trust signals, and
proactive/background execution are the primary experience, not bolt-ons.

The first piece already landed — Storybook integration with a catalogued design
system (~33 stories across Primitives / Components / Composites / Icons /
Tokens) — which becomes Phase 1 and the foundation the rest is built and
reviewed on.

## Vision — AI/Agentic-first UX

The reskin and interaction work are anchored to IronClaw's product identity
(secure personal AI assistant; tooling that scales; trustworthy validations;
multi-channel accessibility with transparent background execution). Agent-first
means the UI commands communication while promoting content over chrome:

- **Agent presence & activity** — streaming output, live status, what the agent
  is doing right now.
- **Tool/capability transparency** — what tools/skills exist, what they touched,
  with redaction-safe summaries.
- **Approvals & gates** — inline auth/permission/approval flows accessible when
  needed and a click away when not.
- **Trust signals** — attestation/TEE, zero-exposure secrets, security state
  surfaced honestly.
- **Proactive/background execution** — jobs/missions/automations visible and
  actionable.
- **Multi-channel parity** — the web surface reflects the same agent reachable
  from Slack/Telegram/CLI.

## Design decision — build on what exists, govern it

- Do **not** rebuild the component layer or fork a parallel/third-party design
  system. Formalize and evolve the existing one: `design-system/` primitives,
  `components/`/`layout/` composites, and the `--v2-*` tokens in
  `styles/app.css`.
- Storybook (already integrated) is the **catalog + review surface + regression
  harness** (story tests in headless Chromium) for every visual/interaction
  change in Phases 3–4.
- A checked-in **`DESIGN.md`** is the governance doc: design principles, token
  taxonomy/naming, primitive/composite/component boundaries, story-authoring
  rules, theming contract, accessibility bar, and the agentic-UX principles the
  reskin must uphold. It builds on `src/design-system/README.md`.
- Theming stays token-driven (`data-theme` + `--v2-*` CSS variables). The reskin
  changes token **values** and assets, not the architecture.

## Implementation placement

- Catalog / stories / decorators: `crates/ironclaw_webui/frontend/.storybook/`,
  `src/**/*.stories.tsx`, `src/test-support/storybook-decorators.tsx`
- Primitives / composites: `src/design-system/`, `src/design-system/primitives.tsx`
- Shared components / shell: `src/components/`, `src/layout/`
- Tokens / theming / assets: `src/styles/app.css`, served `public/` assets
- Governance: `DESIGN.md` (new; frontend root), building on `src/design-system/README.md`
- Routing / IA: `src/app/routes.ts`, `src/pages/`, `src/layout/gateway-layout.tsx`

## Scope — phased

### Phase 1 — Storybook integration ✅ (landed; PR incoming)

- Storybook 10 (`@storybook/react-vite`, pnpm) wired to the real `app.css` +
  light/dark `data-theme` toolbar.
- ~33 stories organized into **Primitives / Components / Composites / Icons /
  Tokens** via explicit `meta.title` + `storySort`.
- Shared `withRouter` / `withQueryClient` decorators; react-query cache seeding
  for network-backed components.
- Vitest split: node `pnpm test` stays browser-free; `pnpm test:storybook` runs
  the story suite in headless Chromium.
- `@storybook/addon-mcp` available so agents can query the catalog.
- Verified green: 106 story tests, 1021 node tests, typecheck, build-storybook.

### Phase 2 — `DESIGN.md` governance & guidelines

- Author `DESIGN.md`: agentic-first design principles, token taxonomy + naming,
  primitive/composite/component boundaries, story-authoring rules, theming /
  `data-theme` contract, accessibility bar, contribution workflow.
- Codify the AI/agentic-UX principles that Phases 3–4 must satisfy.
- Optional: lightweight enforcement (extend `scripts/check-source-conventions`).

### Phase 3 — Theme update & UI reskin (theming + visual assets)

- New/updated **token values** in `app.css` for light + dark; refreshed
  color / type / space / radius / motion scales.
- Visual assets: logo, iconography, imagery aligned to the new look-and-feel.
- Reskin primitives/composites against the new tokens; validate every change in
  Storybook (stories + `CssCheck` + a11y).

### Phase 4 — Interaction & component updates (agentic-first)

- Evolve interactions for agent-first UX: streaming/activity presentation,
  tool/capability transparency, approvals/gates, background/proactive execution
  surfacing, notification/command affordances.
- New/updated components as needed; each shipped with stories + play coverage.

### Phase 5 — Information Architecture

- Revisit navigation / routes / page structure (`app/routes.ts`, `pages/`,
  sidebar / `gateway-layout`) so the IA foregrounds agentic workflows (threads,
  activity, projects, approvals) and multi-channel parity.

## Acceptance criteria / Definition of done

- A governed design system exists: `DESIGN.md` + the Storybook catalog are the
  source of truth, and new UI is built through them.
- Every primitive/composite/component with meaningful states has a story; visual
  and interaction changes are reviewed in Storybook and covered by story tests.
- The WebUI's theming, assets, interactions, and IA reflect the agentic-first
  principles in `DESIGN.md`.
- Light + dark parity and the accessibility bar hold across the reskin.
- `pnpm test` (node) and `pnpm test:storybook` (Chromium) are green;
  `build-storybook` succeeds.

## Non-goals

- Rebuilding the component layer or adopting a parallel/third-party design-system
  framework.
- Backend / product-surface changes beyond what the UI needs (WebUI-frontend
  scoped).
- Changing the token **architecture** (`data-theme` + `--v2-*`); Phase 3 changes
  values/assets, not the mechanism.
- A wholesale rename/move of the `src/` folder structure (the existing layout is
  kept — see the design-system README).

## Phasing / tracking

Phases are tracked as a checklist here; each becomes its own issue as it starts.

- [x] Phase 1 — Storybook integration (PR #7039)
- [x] Phase 2 — DESIGN.md governance & guidelines (#7042, PR #7043)
- [ ] Phase 3 — Theme update & UI reskin
- [ ] Phase 4 — Interaction & component updates
- [ ] Phase 5 — Information Architecture

issues.title: Memory: target-alias resolution is contract — move it to the domain layer

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Problem

Memory target aliases are contract vocabulary, but they are resolved in only one provider. The shared write-tool prompt (`crates/extensions/packages/memory-native/prompts/memory-native/write.md`, reused verbatim by the mem0 manifest) teaches every model that durable facts go to `target: "memory"` and daily notes to `target: "daily_log"`. What that string *means* is currently a per-provider accident:

- **native** resolves aliases to canonical paths (`resolve_target`: `"memory"` → `MEMORY.md`, `"daily_log"` → `daily/<date>.md`) before storage.
- **mem0** stores `metadata.target` verbatim (`"memory"`) and its `read` filters by exact string match against the requested path.

So the same logical document has different identities per provider. This was latent while only the model round-tripped its own strings within one provider; it became a live fault with the host-composed always-on lane in #7365: the host reads the canonical path `MEMORY.md` via `MemoryService::read_document`, which under a mem0 binding can never match a fact stored as `"memory"` — the lane runs but is permanently empty.

Discovered during the #7365 rework (see the PR's Review Notes). Keeping the earlier `read_curated` lifecycle hook would have hidden this (the lane simply didn't run under mem0), not fixed it — the tool-path divergence and cross-provider document-identity mismatch exist regardless.

## Fix

Promote target-alias resolution to the domain contract layer so every provider resolves identically:

- Move/expose the alias table in `ironclaw_memory` (the domain crate already owns the `MEMORY.md` name in its protected-paths list) and route every provider's write/read path resolution through it — providers must not reimplement or skip it.
- mem0: resolve aliases before storing `metadata.target` and before read filtering.
- Migration/compat: existing mem0 rows tagged `"memory"` must remain readable — either a read-time alias-set match (`path ∈ {canonical, legacy alias}`) or a one-time metadata migration; decide with the mem0-gated test in hand.
- Conformance: extend the shared memory-service contract suite so a provider that stores an alias unresolved fails the suite (this is exactly the class of divergence the pluggable-provider direction needs to catch mechanically).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A fact written with `target: "memory"` under a mem0 binding is returned by `read_document("MEMORY.md")` and therefore surfaces in the always-on prompt lane (mem0-gated test).
- [ ] Native behavior unchanged (existing suites).
- [ ] Shared conformance case pinning alias resolution for any document-store provider.
- [ ] Pre-existing mem0 rows with legacy `"memory"` targets remain reachable.

## Related

- #7365 — where the divergence surfaced (host-composed always-on lane).
- #7185 — parent recall complaint; #5260 — memory epic (pluggable-provider direction makes contract-level resolution mandatory, not optional).

issues.title: fix(disclosure): bridge tools hardcoded Exclusive serialize discovery batches and discard batch tails

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: scope: tool
labels.description: Tool infrastructure

labels.name: reborn
labels.description: IronClaw Reborn architecture and landing work

issues.body:
## Problem

The three disclosure bridge tools (`tool_search`, `tool_describe`, `tool_call`) are hardcoded `ConcurrencyHint::Exclusive` (`crates/loop/ironclaw_loop_host/src/tool_disclosure.rs:836,849`), despite `tool_search`/`tool_describe` being side-effect-free metadata lookups.

Consequences:

- `DefaultBatchPolicyStrategy` goes `Sequential` if **any** call in the batch is `Exclusive` (`crates/loop/ironclaw_agent_loop/src/strategies/batch.rs:41-50`).
- Sequential arms `stop_on_first_suspension` (`executor/capabilities.rs:239`), which **discards every call after the first one that parks** — the model must re-issue the tail in another round trip.
- This bites hardest during the discovery phase, exactly where parallel probing (search + several describes in one response) helps most. A production trace showed seven sequential single-name `tool_describe` calls in one run (per #7374's description).

Real capabilities get correct hints (`read_file`/`glob`/`grep`/`list_dir` are `SafeForParallel` via `concurrency_hint_from_effects`, `capability_port.rs:3154-3166`); the defect is isolated to the bridge descriptors.

## Proposed fix

Set `tool_search` and `tool_describe` to `SafeForParallel`. `tool_call` should derive its hint from the *target* capability's effects where resolvable pre-dispatch, defaulting to `Exclusive` when unknown.

## Notes

Verified on `pi-agent-architecture-rev` (0f646ed0de); re-verify against main. Interacts with #7416 (opt-in parallel batches): #7416 parallelizes batches already classified safe — without this fix, any discovery call in the batch keeps it serial, so #7416 never applies to the discovery phase. Regression test: a batch of `tool_search` + 3 `tool_describe` must classify `Parallel` and survive one member erroring without discarding siblings.

issues.title: fix(disclosure): tool_search marks tools disclosed without returning schemas, disarming describe-first; oneOf required collapses to empty

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: scope: tool
labels.description: Tool infrastructure

labels.name: reborn
labels.description: IronClaw Reborn architecture and landing work

issues.body:
## Problem

`tool_search` disarms the describe-first safety net it's supposed to feed.

The describe-first mechanism exists to prevent blind-call spirals: a schema-undisclosed tool called with mis-shaped args is **not dispatched**; the port returns the schema with "call again with the required arguments" (`crates/loop/ironclaw_loop_host/src/tool_disclosure_port.rs:1102-1131`, predicate `should_describe_first` at `:869-895`, one-shot per tool).

But `invoke_tool_search` inserts every search result into `disclosed_names` (`tool_disclosure_port.rs:1030`) while returning only `name`/`capability_id`/`description`/`required` — **no parameter schema** (`:1032-1037`). `should_describe_first` then returns false for anything "disclosed" (`:873-874`). Net effect: after a search, a blind call with bad args gets a bare `invalid_input` **with no schema to recover from** — the exact spiral describe-first exists to prevent.

Compounding: `collect_required_params` passes `contributes_required = false` into `oneOf`/`anyOf` branches (`tool_disclosure.rs:194-199`), so for `oneOf`-shaped tools the `required` array comes back **empty**. `trigger_create` was force-pinned to core for exactly this reason (comment at `tool_disclosure.rs:53-55`); every other `oneOf` tool in the deferred set has no escape hatch.

## Proposed fix

Either (a) **return the full parameter schema from `tool_search` results** — collapses the search→describe→call ritual from 3 round trips to 2 and legitimately justifies marking results disclosed; or (b) stop inserting search results into `disclosed_names` so describe-first stays armed. (a) is strictly better: it fixes the spiral *and* removes a round trip.

Also fix `collect_required_params` to surface `oneOf` alternatives (e.g. `required: ["one of: schedule.cron | schedule.interval"]` or return the branch schemas).

## Notes

Verified on `pi-agent-architecture-rev` (0f646ed0de); re-verify against main. Complements #7374 (bulk describe) — with (a), bulk describe becomes needed only for >8-candidate exploration. Watch response-size interaction with the disclosure caps (`DisclosureCaps { max_tokens: 12_000 }`) — cap the number of full schemas returned per search (e.g. top 5).

issues.title: GitHub MCP extension startup gives confusing endpoint verification prompt instead of connecting

labels.name: bug_bash_P2

issues.body:
**Instance:** Railway (ironclaw-qa-testing-libsql.up.railway.app)

## Description

When starting the GitHub MCP extension, instead of connecting cleanly, the system reports the extension is "already registered and installed" but then raises concerns about endpoint verification. It mentions multiple installs exist (`mcp-xxx-github` and `mcp-xxx-github-v2`) and states the install step doesn't allow fetching or verifying the exact endpoint URL behind the extension. It then asks the user to either confirm the endpoint or re-register/point it explicitly, and asks about auth type — instead of just connecting to GitHub.

The user should not need to deal with internal MCP identifiers, endpoint URLs, or auth type configuration. The extension should either connect successfully or give a clear, actionable error.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attempt to start/activate the GitHub MCP extension
2. Observe the response

## Expected

The GitHub MCP extension should connect and become usable, or provide a clear error message if something is misconfigured.

## Actual

The extension reports as "registered and installed" with tools available, but then presents a confusing prompt about endpoint verification, multiple install variants, and asks the user to confirm endpoints and auth types — information the user should not need to provide manually.

issues.title: Epic: Make Reborn durable state profile-agnostic and migrate legacy profile roots

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: risk: high
labels.description: Safety, secrets, auth, or critical infrastructure

labels.name: scope: workspace
labels.description: Persistent memory / workspace

labels.name: reborn
labels.description: IronClaw Reborn architecture and landing work

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Epic issue tracking a larger initiative

issues.body:
## Problem

Reborn storage is currently indexed by deployment profile. A profile change can therefore make an existing deployment appear empty while leaving conversation history, encrypted secrets, extensions, skills, prompts, settings, and workspaces stranded in a different profile directory. This splits authoritative state and makes rollback, redeployment, and profile transitions unsafe.

## Goal

Make durable storage profile-agnostic and root it directly at `IRONCLAW_REBORN_HOME`. Profiles should select runtime policy and process backend, not physical storage directories.

The canonical layout must separate:

- authoritative application state;
- host-managed system extensions, prompts, and skills;
- persistent workspaces owned by tenant and user;
- Docker/Railway runtime bookkeeping;
- disposable cache and temporary data.

## Security invariants

- Workspace identity and ownership are tenant plus user, never profile name.
- A sandbox receives only its selected tenant/user workspace leaf as `/workspace`.
- The full Reborn home, database, secrets master key, sibling workspaces, and provider credentials must never enter a sandbox, including transiently.
- Profile transitions are restart-only, operator-controlled, and admitted against a persisted security envelope so a sandboxed multi-user deployment cannot silently become an unrestricted host-shell deployment.

## Migration and cutover

Startup adoption must be bounded, idempotent, and fail closed:

- a valid canonical layout starts normally;
- a genuinely fresh home initializes the canonical layout;
- exactly one supported legacy profile root may be adopted automatically during an explicit deployment cutover, after old replicas are stopped, with locking, revalidation, verification, interruption-safe resume, and the canonical manifest committed last;
- multiple populated legacy roots, conflicting canonical data, unsupported layouts, or workspace-ownership ambiguity refuse startup and require manual recovery—never automatic merging.

Rollback and interruption behavior must preserve the legacy source or a recoverable snapshot until canonical verification succeeds.

## Acceptance criteria

- No deployment-ID or profile-name layer exists in canonical durable paths.
- Existing durable state survives supported redeployments and profile changes without splitting or loss.
- Tenant/user workspace ownership is preserved and sandbox mounts are leaf-only.
- Safe single-root legacy adoption is covered by startup, interruption/resume, ambiguity, and rollback tests.
- Ambiguous or unsafe layouts fail before mutation with actionable recovery instructions.
- Railway, Docker, and local deployment cutover instructions document how to stop old replicas, authorize one migration startup, verify it, and remove the temporary cutover authorization.

Implementation in progress: nearai/ironclaw#7456

issues.title: Fix default NEAR AI connection and model probes to use the authenticated runtime session
issues.body:
## Summary

Opening the built-in NEAR AI provider dialog with its default configuration causes both actions to fail:

- `POST /api/webchat/v2/llm/test-connection`
- `POST /api/webchat/v2/llm/list-models`

The failures occur when the API key field is left blank and the default `https://cloud-api.near.ai` endpoint is used.

Manually supplying an explicit API key works with both the production and staging endpoints, including:

- `https://cloud-api.near.ai`
- `https://cloud-stg-api.near.ai/v1`

The default probe path does not deterministically prefer the authenticated NEAR AI runtime session. A stored API key or a newly created session manager can take precedence, so the transient provider may not use the active NEAR account session.

## Expected behavior

- With no inline API key, the default/persisted NEAR AI endpoint should use the authenticated runtime session.
- An explicitly supplied API key should remain the highest-priority credential and work with custom endpoints.
- Runtime session credentials must not be forwarded to an overridden endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- “Test connection” succeeds with the default configuration after NEAR account authentication.
- “Fetch models” succeeds with the default configuration after NEAR account authentication.
- The runtime session takes precedence over any stale stored NEAR AI API key.
- An explicit API key continues to work with production and staging endpoints.
- An overridden endpoint without an explicit API key does not receive the runtime session token.
- Regression tests cover both probe APIs and the endpoint credential boundary.

prs.title: feat(webui): operator surface for the IronHub agent link
prs.body:
## Summary

- An operator can only obtain the IronHub register URL and install the hub-minted shared key through the CLI today, so a deployment cannot complete an agent link from the WebUI at all. This adds that surface to the Extensions page.
- The panel shows the register URL to paste into IronHub, reports whether a key is stored and whether the register gateway is actually running on one, accepts a key, and removes a stored key.
- `IronhubLinkAdminService` is declared in `ironclaw_product_contracts` and implemented in `ironclaw_extension_manager::ironhub`, next to `RebornIronhubLinkService` and `IronhubSharedKey`. No new dependency edges: that crate already depends on `ironclaw_secrets` and `ironclaw_product_contracts`, and already stores operator-set deployment credentials through the same substrate in `admin_configuration.rs`.
- The key is written to the encrypted standalone secret store under a fixed handle, never to plaintext state. `IRONHUB_AGENT_SHARED_KEY` keeps its existing precedence, so nothing about the current env-based deployment path changes.
- One ratchet raise: `ironclaw_product_contracts` 15909 to 15970, for the port and its wire DTOs. Declaration only. `scripts/ci/composition-budget.toml` is unchanged.

## Change Type

- [x] New feature
- [x] Security

## Linked Issue

Related #5409. That PR carried the deep-link gateway and its WebUI half onto Reborn and was closed unmerged; the backend landed separately afterwards, the operator-facing half did not.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo build`
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `ironclaw_product_contracts`, `ironclaw_extension_manager`, `ironclaw_composition`, `ironclaw_assistant`, `ironclaw_webui`, `ironclaw`, `ironclaw_architecture_tests` (124 suites, 3714 tests), plus the frontend suite (140 files, 1244 tests)
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` if database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed
- [ ] Manual testing
- [ ] `review-pr` / `pr-shepherd --fix`

Opened as a draft deliberately. The runs above were green on `5ce21472b`; this branch has since been rebased onto `307521f15` and the local results have not been reproduced on the new base. Clippy was run per-package over the seven touched crates with `--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` rather than the workspace form in the checklist. CI is the verification of record here, which is why this is a draft rather than a review request.

Also run locally on the pre-rebase base: `scripts/ci/check-guidance.py`, `check-target-tree.py`, `check-include-str-paths.sh`, `check-hermetic-env.sh`, `check_no_panics.py --base --head`, `check-composition-budget.sh`, and `scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh`, all clean.

No manual testing against a running deployment. That gap is real and called out under Review Follow-Through.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: an operator opens Extensions, copies the register URL into IronHub, pastes the key IronHub generated back into the agent, restarts, and the register gateway accepts hub traffic. A non-operator never sees the panel.

Risk areas:
- [x] Browser
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: `ironhub/link_admin.rs` covers unconfigured state, stored-but-not-active, env-key-active-without-stored, accept-then-stored, short-key rejected before it reaches the store, whitespace trimmed before storage, status never carrying key material, clear removes a stored key, clear on an absent key is not an error, and clear leaving a running gateway active. `ironhub/shared_key_store.rs` covers put/read round trip, repeatable read, rotation, and delete. `webui_v2_descriptors_contract.rs` and `webui_v2_operator_route_predicate_contract.rs` pin both routes and their operator gating. `ironhub_link_serve.rs` pins the register-URL join.
- Reborn integration: not applicable. The behavior is a product-surface command and view plus their transport, and the existing composition test `every_webui_v2_descriptor_is_mounted_on_composed_app` already drives the composed app that mounts them.
- Recorded fixture: not applicable, no model behavior.
- Browser E2E: not applicable. The panel is covered by a VM-harness component test asserting the 403-hides-panel, error, restart-notice, remove-affordance-visibility, and no-key-material-rendered cases.
- Backend or runtime: not applicable, no database or runtime-lane behavior.
- Live canary: not applicable.

What the tests prove: a key that fails validation never reaches the store; the status projection carries no key material; both routes are stripped from deployments without an operator surface and re-checked in the handler; clearing a stored key does not claim to have stopped a gateway that is still running on the key it booted with.

Commands run: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p <each of the seven crates> --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p <same seven> --no-fail-fast`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, `bash scripts/ci/check-composition-budget.sh`, `bash scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh`.

## Security Impact

This change stores and reads a shared HMAC secret, and adds two operator-only routes.

- Storage is the encrypted standalone secret store through `SecretStorePort` under the fixed handle `ironhub_agent_shared_key`, scoped `ResourceScope::system()`. It is never written to `/system/settings/...` or any plaintext state root.
- Precedence is unchanged: `IRONHUB_AGENT_SHARED_KEY` wins, the stored key is the fallback, and neither present still leaves the register gateway off. The default-off gate and the test that pins it are untouched.
- Both routes are gated three ways: `is_webui_v2_operator_webui_config_route_id` strips and pre-gates them, `mount_operator_routes` conditionally mounts them, and each handler re-checks `operator_webui_config` and fails closed with 403. The view id is also in `product_view_requires_operator_config`.
- The key never travels outward. `RebornIronhubLinkResponse` carries a boolean, not the value, and there is a test asserting no key material appears in its `Debug`. `RebornIronhubLinkSetKeyRequest` has a hand-written `Debug` that redacts the field, and the port takes a `secrecy::SecretString` from the assistant boundary inward.
- Validation happens before storage: a key shorter than the 32-character minimum is rejected and never written.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: none introduced. `IronhubSharedKey` is unchanged and still constructed only through its validating constructor.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope: not applicable, nothing here is model-visible.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose: not applicable, no new hashing. The existing HMAC-SHA256 verification path is untouched.
- [x] New/changed status/exit/policy/runtime/error variants: none. `IronhubLinkError` is unchanged and its existing projection onto `ProductSurfaceError` is reused. Verified with `rg "IronhubLinkError" crates`.
- [x] Security `serde(default)` fields fail closed: none added. `RebornIronhubLinkSetKeyRequest` is `deny_unknown_fields` with a required field.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters bounded: not applicable, no new collections. The set-key route carries the standard 4 KiB body limit and per-caller rate limit.
- [x] Operator-visible errors have stable class semantics: reuses `map_ironhub_link_error`, which projects onto the existing sanitized `ProductSurfaceError` codes.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe the trust boundary: no process or sandbox surface involved.

## Database Impact

None. No migrations, no schema change. The secret store is the existing encrypted store; no new mount or table.

## Blast Radius

Five crates. `ironclaw_product_contracts` is the widest, but the change there is declaration only, additive, and touches no existing type. `ironclaw_extension_manager` gains the implementation and a `secrecy` dependency. `ironclaw_composition` gains construction and wiring only, and its mass and dispatch budgets are unchanged from main (41663 LOC, 831 `Arc<dyn>`). `ironclaw_assistant` gains a view, two commands, and a fail-closed default. `ironclaw_webui` gains two operator-gated routes.

The realistic failure mode is a deployment with no public base URL configured, where the panel reports no register URL rather than guessing one. Existing env-configured deployments are unaffected: the boot resolution prefers the env var and the register gateway's default-off behavior is unchanged.

## Rollback Plan

Revert the single commit. Nothing persists across the revert except a secret-store entry under `ironhub_agent_shared_key`, which is inert once the code reading it is gone, and which the pre-existing `IRONHUB_AGENT_SHARED_KEY` path does not consult.

## Review Follow-Through

Two things I would like a decision on rather than assume.

The admin surface is a separate port instead of two more methods on `IronhubLinkService`. That service is `Option`-gated and is `None` until a key exists, while the whole point of this surface is setting the key before the gateway comes up, so folding them together breaks the bootstrap ordering. If you would rather it hang off the existing service with a different gating shape, I will rework it.

The contracts ratchet raise is the one number needing sign-off: `("ironclaw_product_contracts", 15_909)` to `15_970`. It is the port, the view and two command descriptors, and two wire DTOs, with the implementation living outside contracts.

Not done: no manual verification against a running deployment. I have not started a server, completed a link against IronHub staging, and confirmed the handshake end to end. The route and gating behavior is covered by contract tests, but the full round trip is unproven.

---

**Review track**: C (security/runtime)

prs.title: fix(reborn): make durable storage profile-agnostic
prs.body:
## Summary

- Root every Reborn profile directly at `IRONCLAW_REBORN_HOME` with profile-agnostic `state/`, `system/`, `workspaces/`, `runtime/`, `logs/`, `cache/`, and `tmp/` namespaces.
- Persist a typed security envelope so restart-only profile transitions cannot weaken tenancy or workspace isolation.
- Bind sandboxes to one typed tenant/user workspace leaf as `/workspace`; the Reborn home, database, master key, provider credentials, system content, and sibling workspaces remain host-only.
- Preserve conversations, encrypted secrets, extension installations, settings, prompts, system/user skills, and tenant/user ownership across adoption and restart.
- Automatically adopt exactly one supported legacy root during startup only when the deployment supplies `IRONCLAW_REBORN_STORAGE_CUTOVER=legacy-layout-v1` after every old replica has stopped.
- Fail before mutation when cutover authority is absent or legacy state is ambiguous, unsupported, tampered, incompatible, or carries an external workspace import. The explicit `ironclaw storage adopt` command remains the recovery and workspace-ownership path.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [x] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

- Epic: #7467

## User behavior

Startup now follows this bounded decision:

```text
valid canonical layout -> start
fresh home -> initialize canonical layout and start
one supported legacy root or compatible journal
  + exact deployment cutover authority -> snapshot, adopt, verify, commit layout.toml, start
  + no authority -> fail before listener or storage mutation
ambiguous or unsafe state -> fail closed with manual recovery instructions
```

The cutover environment value is a deployment attestation, not a process probe. Operators must stop all old binaries before setting it; old releases do not participate in the new locks. Remove it after `layout.toml` is ready.

## Test Strategy

Risk areas:

- [x] Side effects
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security and permissions
- [x] External PostgreSQL ordering
- [x] Cross-process concurrency
- [x] Cross-component behavior
- [x] Browser/model behavior

The tests prove:

- A real `ironclaw serve` process refuses one released `local-dev/` root without cutover authority, does not bind, and leaves the complete home unchanged.
- The same real startup automatically adopts with the exact authority and cold-reopens preserved threads, encrypted secrets, extensions, settings, prompts, skills, and tenant/user ownership.
- Every persisted journal phase resumes automatically and publishes `layout.toml` last.
- Source, snapshot, staging, canonical, workspace, and symlink shapes are revalidated under the cutover lock before PostgreSQL verification.
- Invalid, multiple, and unreleased roots fail before an intentionally invalid PostgreSQL verifier can run.
- Two new processes serialize on one persistent advisory-lock inode; workspace-bearing journals remain manual.
- Incompatible profile transitions and sandbox mounts fail closed.
- WebUI browse paths remain relative to the composition-scoped tenant/user workspace leaf, avoiding double scoping.
- Hosted PostgreSQL profiles refuse CLI secret commands that would otherwise create a shadow local libSQL store.
- Session-only encrypted state fails cutover closed when no safe master-key verifier exists.

## Validation

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p ironclaw runtime::storage_layout::tests
cargo test -p ironclaw runtime::tests::automatic_startup_rejects_unsafe_legacy_shapes_before_postgres_verification
cargo test -p ironclaw --test storage_adoption
cargo test -p ironclaw_secrets
cargo test -p ironclaw_webui --test webui_v2_handlers_contract
cargo test -p ironclaw_config --test profile_contract
cargo test -p ironclaw_composition --test profile_acceptance
cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --test reborn_dependency_boundaries
cargo clippy -p ironclaw --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
bash scripts/ci/check-composition-budget.sh
python3 scripts/ci/docs_publication_boundary.py
python3 scripts/ci/test_reborn_pr_test_plan.py
bash scripts/test-reset-extension-state.sh
python3 -m unittest tests/test_smoke_release_binary.py
git diff --check
```

Focused validation passed on exact HEAD `27b475d2bc924f7a13faa565e123a7512f051f5f` after merging current `origin/main`. The complete changed-crate clippy and contract suites also passed on the review-fix commit; CI is rerunning them on the merged head.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Only the selected tenant/user workspace leaf is mounted as `/workspace`.
- [x] Reborn home, databases, master key, credentials, system content, and sibling workspaces remain host-only.
- [x] Profile transitions are restart-only, operator-controlled, typed, and fail closed.
- [x] Automatic adoption accepts one supported legacy root only and never merges populated roots.
- [x] Existing encrypted records are authenticated before filesystem source mutation or manifest commit.

## Blast Radius

Touches CLI startup/adoption, configuration-owned layout types, composition filesystem assembly, sandbox workspace admission, secret verification, WebUI workspace browsing, integration harnesses, and deployment documentation. No persistence schema changes. Rollback requires stopping processes and restoring the retained snapshot or operator backup before running an old binary.

## Security Impact

This tightens storage and sandbox boundaries. Automatic migration requires an exact versioned cutover authority, holds a cross-process lock through external-store verification and the journaled state machine, revalidates immediately before mutation, and commits `layout.toml` last. Credentials never enter a sandbox, including transiently. Multiple roots are never selected or merged automatically.

## Database Impact

No database schema is added. Embedded libSQL files move as one recognized unit into canonical `state/`. PostgreSQL remains external; startup performs source/journal/security admission and obtains cutover exclusion before opening or migrating the configured store. Existing encrypted secret/account records are verified with the configured master key before filesystem source mutation. A session-only encrypted store fails cutover closed because its invocation-bound AAD cannot be reconstructed without exposing encrypted identity metadata.

## Rollback Plan

Stop all IronClaw processes. Keep the operator backup and retained `runtime/layout-adoption/snapshot/` tree through the rollback window. Compatible profile rollback reuses the canonical home. Old-binary rollback requires restoring the original legacy root or full pre-adoption backup; never run old and new binaries against diverging copies. External workspace sources and migration evidence are not automatically deleted.

## Review Follow-Through

The automatic-cutover increment received repeated Terra security, concurrency, testing, and thermo-maintainability reviews. Findings around old-binary exclusion, pre-PostgreSQL journal-shape admission, advisory-lock inode reuse, fresh-home manifest races, WebUI double scoping, hosted secret-store backend drift, session-only key verification, unowned workspace content, and dangling symlinks were fixed and regression-tested.

---

**Review track**: C

prs.title: feat(channels): unified channel model — one ChannelAdapter for inbound, replies, and notifications
prs.body:
# Unified channel model: one ChannelAdapter per channel for inbound, replies, and notifications

Implements `docs/internal/design/2026-08-10-unified-channel-model.md` end-to-end (§12 items 1–11 + §13 enforcement). Every channel — web-app, Slack, Telegram — is now ONE `ChannelAdapter` implementing inbound + reply + notifications; the only per-channel variation is the declared entrypoint and capabilities in its manifest; nothing channel-specific for inbound/outbound/notifications lives outside `crates/extensions/packages/*` (§0), enforced by a new architecture gate.

## 1. Inbound unification (§12 1–4)

- `ChannelInboundSurfaceRequest` / `ProductInboundEnvelope` generalized: trust is an enum (`VerifiedInbound { evidence } | SessionCaller { caller }`), binding is an enum (`ExternalRef | OwnedThread { thread_id }`). Sealed evidence minting is untouched (T1 webui middleware, T2 extension-host verifier; ratchet unchanged).
- Browser + OpenAI-compat submissions re-plumbed through the ONE webhook inbound core (`admit_channel_inbound` → `submit_inbound_inner` → durable `IdempotencyLedger` → `InboundTurnService`). The duplicate `RebornServices::submit_turn` tail (`AcceptedWebUiMessage`, `replay_webui_send_message`, …) is deleted; the command constant keeps its wire contract byte-for-byte (the 278-test `reborn_services_contract` suite passes unchanged).
- `SubmissionLane { Webhook, Session }` keeps lane differences as data on the one pipeline: persisted binding-id schemes are byte-identical to the old webui scheme (with legacy fallback), idempotency key shapes preserved, `client_action_id` replay, caller-owns-thread, and no-thread-auto-creation all pinned by tests.
- Generic session-inbound route: `POST /api/webchat/v2/channels/{extension_id}/messages`. The frontend learns the deployment's session channel from `GET /session` (`session_channel_extension_id`, exactly-one rule, fail-closed) — no channel name in the frontend.

## 2. Reply unification (§12 5–7)

- `ChannelReplyMode { Streaming, Batched }` declared in the manifest (`[channel] reply_mode`). Web-app declares `streaming` (its reply sink IS the existing SSE/projection stream); Slack/Telegram declare `batched`.
- The delivery coordinator's streaming gate skips batched delivery only for CONVERSATION traffic; a notification-routed send (RunNotification intent + non-live-source origin) flows regardless of reply mode. This distinction is load-bearing: the blocked-fire browser-push journey caught the intent-only version dropping gate-prompt notifications, now pinned at the contract tier (`streaming_channel_delivers_a_notification_routed_gate_prompt`) and by the journey.
- Gate reads use a lightweight `channel_reply_mode` port method so the coordinator's one-generation-pinned resolution contract is preserved (its pinning test is untouched).
- `max_message_chars` is optional and load-bearing for the batched sink only.

## 3. Notification generalization (§12 8–10)

- **Send facade (§7a):** `ChannelAdapter::deliver_notification` (default delegates to `deliver`) is the channel's notification send; the coordinator dispatches to it by route classification. `notify` / `notify_user` facade in `run_delivery/notifications.rs`; the triggered-run driver delegates to it (no rebuild of the canary-guarded path).
- **Setup surface (§7b):** generic `GET/POST /api/webchat/v2/channels/{extension_id}/notifications{,/enable,/disable}` replaces the deleted `/web-push/{status,subscriptions,subscriptions/remove}`. Adapter methods `notification_setup_status` / `enable_notifications` / `disable_notifications` take channel-opaque payloads; `AdapterChannelNotificationSetupService` dispatches by `extension_id` over the same `ChannelDeliveryResolver` delivery uses (unknown extension → 404 fail-closed; no-setup channels report `enabled: true`; payload/detail byte bounds enforced before adapter work).
- The web-push subscription store, VAPID advertisement, and endpoint validation moved behind the web-app adapter (slot runtime installed by composition after canonical VAPID read-back). Enrollment storage scope is byte-identical to the retired product service.
- Frontend: generic `getNotificationSetupStatus/enable/disable` keyed by `extensionId`; the notification-channels panel's device row matches `row.channel === getSessionChannelExtensionId()` — the channel-opaque status `detail` is interpreted only by the session channel's own client module (`device-push.ts`). `webPush.*` i18n keys → `devicePush.*` across all 11 locales.
- Picker readiness is generic: selectability derives from the channel's setup status (enrolled-browser count in the opaque detail), not a channel name.

## 4. Rename web-push → web-app (§12 11)

Product identity renamed: extension id / channel name / catalog target id `web-app`, package dir `crates/extensions/packages/web-app` (crate `ironclaw_web_app_extension`), domain crate `crates/domains/ironclaw_web_app`, all `WEB_PUSH_*` → `WEB_APP_*`, `WebPush*` types → `WebApp*`. PROPOSAL §5 tree updated (checked by `check-target-tree.py`, 66/66 OK).

**Persisted coordinates deliberately keep pre-rename bytes** (each commented in place, pinned by the new gate's allowlist):
- secret-store credential handle value `web_push_vapid` (renaming = VAPID rotation = every existing browser subscription breaks cryptographically);
- enrollment document path `/web-push/subscriptions.json` + composition's `/web-push` per-user mount alias (alias resolves to a physical subpath — renaming orphans enrollments);
- binding-ref prefix: mints `web-app/v1/`, decodes legacy `web-push/v1/` forever (regression test added).

**Documented residue (no migration):** stored notification-channel selections carrying the old `web-push` target id render as `Unavailable` after deploy and stop delivering until re-selected in the picker (one checkbox). Population is ~QA-only (the channel shipped 2026-08-09). A read-time alias was deliberately not added (repo rule: renamed persisted identities get migrations, never runtime aliases; a migration for a one-checkbox QA fix is not warranted — flagging for your ruling if you disagree).

- The install-catalog hide for the host's own surface is no longer an id match: `is_builtin_host_surface` now consults the `SessionChannelDirectory` (manifest-derived `authenticated_session` fact); absent directory fails OPEN (catalog visibility).

## 5. Enforcement (§13)

New gate `reborn_web_push_vocabulary_retired.rs` (retired-taxonomy shape): `web-push` / `web_push` / `WebPush` / `webPush` / `WEB_PUSH` pinned at **zero occurrences** across `crates/` (frontend sources included), `tests/integration/`, and `skills/`, with an exact-term, shrink-only, reality-pinned allowlist covering only the five persisted-compat files above. A second assertion pins the session + notification-setup routes as `{extension_id}`-parameterized in the descriptor source. The specificity gate's `web-app` carve-out doc records the rename.

## Test strategy

- **Unit/contract:** trust/binding enum serde-compat; session-lane module (10 tests) incl. byte-identical binding-id schemes + replay; reply-mode manifest validation; 5 setup-dispatch tests (fail-closed unknown channel, no-setup mutation rejection, verbatim scope/payload pass-through, payload bound before adapter work, detail bound/non-JSON refusal); streaming-gate trio incl. the notification-routed gate-prompt regression pin; legacy ref-prefix decode.
- **Integration (production composition):** `webui_v2_product_api::browser_channel_notification_setup_round_trip_through_production_facade` (VAPID advertisement, enroll/refresh outcomes, endpoint redaction + digest correlation, undeclared-host rejection, notification-channel wire, disable read-back, unknown-channel 404); `delivery_user_journeys::blocked_fire_pushes_web_app_notice_to_enrolled_browser` (real encrypted push with host-injected VAPID while the run parks on its gate); the 278-test reborn_services suite unchanged.
- **Architecture:** full `ironclaw_architecture_tests` suite incl. the new retirement gate; `check-target-tree.py` OK; `docs_publication_boundary.py` OK.
- **Frontend:** 139 files / 1241 tests green; bundle budgets via build.
- **E2E:** journey case/coverage data renamed consistently (Rust + Python sides); e2e venv not provisioned locally — CI runs it.

## Compatibility / rollback

- Wire: session send + setup routes are NEW paths; the old `/web-push/*` routes are deleted in the same PR that repoints the only client (the bundled SPA). OpenAI-compat and webhook wire contracts unchanged.
- Persisted: all storage coordinates stable (see §4); binding-id schemes byte-identical; idempotency ledger key shapes preserved. Rollback = revert the PR; no data migration in either direction. The one forward-only residue is the notification-channel selection re-tick noted above.
- Trust: no seam weakened — evidence mint ratchets, body limits, rate limits, and fail-closed paths preserved; new routes carry the same policy classes as their predecessors (8 KiB setup bodies, per-caller rate limits).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: feat: automation suggestion cards V1 backend (#7038)
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements the automation suggestion cards V1 backend (#7038): a narrow,
single-purpose "suggestion generation" loop the model runs to produce a
handful of home-screen automation suggestion cards, exposed via
`GET /api/webchat/v2/suggestions` and `POST /api/webchat/v2/suggestions/generate`.

- New `crates/domains/ironclaw_suggestions` crate: `SuggestionCard`,
  `SuggestionsDoc`, and a CAS-based `SuggestionsStore` over `RootFilesystem`
  — shared between the kernel-layer `render_suggestions` tool and the
  product-layer service (kernel cannot depend on products, mirrors
  `ironclaw_triggers`'s identical position).
- `builtin.render_suggestions`: the forced structured-output first-party
  tool the generation run must call to finish.
- `suggestion_generation` run profile with a strict capability allow-list
  (`extension_search` + `memory.read` + `memory.search` +
  `render_suggestions` — everything else, including `spawn_subagent` and
  trigger CRUD, excluded by omission).
- `RebornSuggestionsProductService`: CAS-claims a generation job, submits a
  hidden single-message turn, derives `generation.state` at read time
  (never persisted).
- The suggestion-generation thread (like an automation-trigger thread) is
  excluded from thread listing but its transcript stays durably readable —
  generalized the existing automation-trigger-only hidden-thread predicate.

## The user journey this enables

This PR is backend only — the interface is a separate PR — but the whole point
of the contract is one experience. Here is that experience end to end, and what
in this diff makes each moment possible.

**Maya opens IronClaw for the first time this week.** The home screen has no
suggestions yet, so it offers to find some. Nothing was precomputed in the
background and no job was waiting for her: generation only happens when someone
asks. *(`GET /api/webchat/v2/suggestions` on an account that has never
generated returns `state: "none"` with an empty `cards` array — an absent
document derives the same view as an empty one, so first-run needs no seeding
and no migration.)*

**She clicks "Get suggestions."** The screen acknowledges immediately and
starts filling in — this takes seconds, not milliseconds, because a model is
actually reasoning about her setup. *(`POST .../suggestions/generate` claims a
job and returns right away rather than holding the request open for the model
run. The UI polls the GET while `state` is `running`.)*

**Impatient, she clicks it twice more.** Nothing bad happens. She doesn't get
three sets of cards, three model runs, or three charges against her budget —
the second and third clicks quietly join the run already going. *(The claim is
a compare-and-swap on the stored document: the first caller wins, and every
subsequent caller gets back the winner's `job_id` instead of starting a rival
run. This is the behavior the concurrent-claim test pins, and it only failed
under real contention — which is why the suite runs unfiltered.)*

**Behind the screen, the assistant is doing real work.** It looks at which
extensions Maya has installed and which are actually connected for *her*, and
searches what it remembers about how she works, then decides what would
genuinely help. It cannot send an email, post to Slack, create a routine, or
spawn another agent while it does this — not because it was asked not to, but
because those tools are not on the table. *(The `suggestion_generation` run
profile narrows the capability surface to exactly four tools:
`extension_search`, `memory.search`, `memory.read`, `render_suggestions`.
Everything else is excluded by omission, and globally disabled capabilities
still apply on top. Proven by widening the list in a test and watching a
forbidden tool's output reach the transcript.)*

**None of this shows up as a conversation.** Maya's chat sidebar looks exactly
as she left it — no mysterious "Suggestion generation" thread appeared next to
her real conversations. *(The generation turn does run in a genuine thread, so
it gets transcripts, budgets, scheduler limits, and error handling for free —
but the thread is tagged `suggestion_generation` and filtered out of the
listing, the same mechanism automation-trigger threads already used. The
transcript stays durably readable for debugging; it is hidden, not discarded.)*

**Four cards appear.** "Triage my inbox." "Summarize today's Slack mentions."
Each one is a specific thing, not a description of a capability. *(The run can
only finish by calling `render_suggestions` with a schema-validated card list —
a model that replies with prose describing cards instead is recorded as a
failed generation, not rendered as garbage. Malformed output becomes a retry,
not a broken screen.)*

**One card says "Triage my inbox — connect Gmail first."** Maya hasn't
connected Gmail. The card doesn't pretend otherwise, and it doesn't look like
an error — it's the first genuinely concrete reason she's had to connect it.
*(`requires_connection` is computed from real per-user connection state at
generation time, not guessed by the model: the catalog search is credential-
aware and scoped to the calling user. The prompt forbids inventing extensions
or connections it didn't observe.)*

**She clicks "Summarize today's Slack mentions."** A normal chat thread opens,
with a first message already written in her voice — the kind of thing she'd
have typed herself. She can read it before anything happens, follow up, or
walk away. Nothing was sent, changed, or scheduled on her behalf. *(The card
carries `suggested_prompt`, the exact text that gets submitted, and the click
uses the ordinary create-thread + send-message path. There is no separate
execution engine, so the resulting conversation is honest history rather than a
hidden process.)*

**A week later she comes back.** Her cards from last time are there
immediately, no waiting — and a refresh gets a new set reflecting what has
changed since. *(Results are persisted per user, so a revisit renders instantly
from the last successful run. Regeneration replaces the set; each run also
leaves its own transcript behind, so nothing the model produced is destroyed.)*

**When something goes wrong, she can tell.** If a generation run dies — crash,
model failure, a run that ended without producing cards — the screen says so
and offers to try again, still showing the previous cards rather than going
blank. *(Generation state is never stored, only derived per request from what
actually happened, so a crashed run reads as `failed` on its own with no stuck
"running" spinner to clear. A finalizer clears the claim the moment a run
terminates, so the next attempt starts clean.)*

**What deliberately does not happen yet:** accepting a card never runs anything
in the background, nothing tracks completion, there is no "do all of these,"
and cards are not objects Maya has to dismiss or manage. Those depend on the
background-job design still in progress. Everything above is proposals and
ordinary conversations — which is exactly what the UI should convey.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/integration/suggestion_cards.rs` — 23 tests: happy path, dedupe
      + concurrent-claim CAS, strict-output enforcement (prose reply +
      invalid-cards retry), hidden-thread listing + automation-trigger
      regression + transcript readability, capability lockdown, card-click
      round-trip, dead-run derivation.
- [x] Break-it-to-prove-it verified for the three security/correctness-load-
      bearing tests: capability allow-list denial, hidden-thread predicate,
      and CAS claim (the last required a purpose-built `RaceBarrierFilesystem`
      test double, since real concurrent execution against `InMemoryBackend`
      never reliably landed the race — see `ironclaw_suggestions/src/tests.rs`).
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`
      (per-crate and workspace) — zero warnings.
- [x] `cargo test` / `cargo test --features integration` — green across every
      touched crate.
- [x] Architecture tests (`ironclaw_architecture_tests`) — full suite green,
      including the layer-matrix and WS5 transport-boundary rules this PR's
      new crate and DTO shapes had to satisfy.

## Code review

Ran the multi-agent `code-review` skill (8 reviewers) at low effort. Two
real regressions found and fixed in this PR (both from the transport-
boundary fix): `suggestions.generate`'s dispatch arm was skipping the
`product_command_input` no-input-validation idiom every sibling command
uses, and the webui handler was sending `Value::Null` where an empty-struct
`Deserialize` impl requires `{}`.

Two known follow-ups intentionally left for a separate PR (neither blocks
merge — both are confidence 50-74 candidates per the review's own scale,
not confirmed defects):
- `render_suggestions`' hook resolves which job to record cards against by
  re-reading whichever `active_job` is *currently* active rather than
  carrying the acting run's own `job_id` through the tool call. Under a
  narrow race (a superseded run's tool call lands after a new claim), a
  stale run's cards could overwrite a newer claim's slot. The CAS store's
  own stale-job guard exists to prevent exactly this but never sees it
  because the hook never tells it which job is calling. Fix requires
  threading `job_id` through `RenderSuggestionsHook`/`FirstPartyCapabilityRequest`.
- `SuggestionsStore` takes a raw `Arc<dyn RootFilesystem>` and hand-composes
  tenant/user scoping into its own path strings, where sibling stores
  (`ironclaw_web_push`, `ironclaw_threads`) take a pre-scoped
  `Arc<ScopedFilesystem<F>>`.

## Post-merge concurrency fix

A rebase onto `main` surfaced a real production bug the merge itself didn't
cause but exposed under full-suite CPU load:
`concurrent_generate_calls_converge_on_one_claim` failed 4/5 unfiltered runs
(never in isolation). Root cause: `generate_suggestions_with_thread_id`'s
crash-recovery pre-check can't distinguish "this run crashed" from "this run
just completed normally without calling `render_suggestions`" — both report
the same `RunLiveness::Terminal`. Under real scheduling variance, a second
concurrent caller can observe a winning racer's claim *after* that racer's
(fast, scripted) turn already went terminal, independently decide the claim
is dead, and mint a second, different `job_id` via two separate non-atomic
CAS writes — violating the spec §4 / decision D1 dedupe guarantee.

First fix, `MIN_CLAIM_AGE_BEFORE_RECLAIM` (3s): a claim younger than this is
treated as still-forming regardless of what the coordinator reports, so
every racer in a concurrent burst converges on the same first claim; a claim
past that age remains recoverable exactly as before. Break-it-to-prove-it:
zeroing the grace period reproduces the original failure 4/5 runs; restored,
25 consecutive unfiltered full-suite runs are clean, including runs under
genuine CPU contention.

**Follow-up review correctly flagged that timer as a mitigation, not a
fix**: it doesn't resolve the actual conflation (`RunLiveness::Terminal`
reads identically for "crashed" and "finished without calling
`render_suggestions`") — it just makes the ambiguous window unreachable for
3s, which a busy-enough box could still exceed. Root cause: spec §6's "turn
finalizer" (clear `active_job` the moment a run's OWN terminal transition
fires, so a terminal claim is never ambiguous) was never wired.

**Built it.** `SuggestionGenerationFinalizerSink`
(`ironclaw_composition::suggestions`) rides the existing `TurnEventSink` fan-out
(the same shared seam `TraceCaptureTurnEventSink`/`SkillLearningTurnEventSink`
already use in `runtime.rs`) — no new trait, no new registration surface —
and clears `active_job` on every terminal transition of the run it's
actually waiting on (`ActiveJob.run_id` match; `record_failure`'s existing
stale-job guard makes it a no-op for every other event). With this wired,
`MIN_CLAIM_AGE_BEFORE_RECLAIM` is reduced to a genuine short lease (500ms)
covering only the residual gap between a run's status becoming visible and
the sink actually firing (they're not the same atomic event) — its doc
comment now states that plainly and names the failure mode if the finalizer
is ever removed or fails silently. Re-verified with the same unfiltered
repeat-run protocol: 20 consecutive clean runs at 500ms, plus 3 runs under
real CPU contention (three full copies of the test binary running
concurrently). New finalizer unit tests break-it-to-prove-it verified on
their own run_id-matching guard.
