prs.title: fix(safety): redact model-bound secrets without rejecting turns
prs.body:
## Summary

- Replace credential-content rejection in prompt contracts with deterministic redaction, so one false positive can no longer block prompt construction, attachment recovery, or unrelated threads.
- Add a source-independent final model-input redaction pass shared by plain, tool-capable, streaming, and repair provider calls.
- Preserve surrounding context and raw durable data while replacing detected values with `[REDACTED_SECRET]`.
- Keep prompt-injection handling separate: untrusted memory remains enveloped and an injection-bearing snippet is omitted without rejecting the turn.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [x] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

None.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_safety --no-fail-fast` (308 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_contracts --no-fail-fast`
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_turns --test agent_loop_host_contract --no-fail-fast` (87 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_host_runtime --test memory_prompt_context --no-fail-fast` (18 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --test llm_gateway --no-fail-fast` (92 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --lib provider_bound_redaction_covers_stop_sequences --no-fail-fast`
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --no-fail-fast`
- [x] `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_golden_payload --no-fail-fast` (21 passed)
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration`: Not applicable; no database-backed behavior changed.
- [x] Manual testing: exact-head Railway preview validated a neutral JSON attachment through upload, agent recovery, and refresh persistence.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: Given recovered text containing security vocabulary, host paths, credential-shaped values, or prompt-injection markers, when IronClaw reconstructs and dispatches a model request, benign context remains usable, detected credential values are placeholders, injection-bearing memory snippets are isolated, and the turn continues.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior
- [x] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit/contract: known credential formats, labeled weak values, Basic/Bearer authorization, UTF-8 boundaries, idempotency, benign near misses, large-input regex budget, structural prompt limits, and provider stop sequences.
- Caller contract: credential-bearing runtime, skill, instruction, and capability content no longer aborts prompt construction.
- Backend/runtime: production memory admission keeps security prose and paths, redacts credential values, drops injection-bearing snippets, and preserves model-content budgets.
- Provider boundary: recording providers prove secrets are absent from every message role, textual reasoning/content parts, tool descriptions, JSON schema strings/keys, prior tool arguments, and provider-generated repair prompts.
- Reborn integration: the production-wired durable file-tool path proves structured credential values are absent from persisted tool-result references and every captured model request while benign fields survive.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable; no model-selection behavior or nondeterministic output is asserted.
- Browser E2E: exact-head Railway preview upload and neutral recovery flow passed, including persistence after refresh.
- Live canary: exact-head Railway preview used a fresh synthetic credential value; the marker, source path, message, and benign secretary field survived, while the password rendered as `[REDACTED_SECRET]` and the canary was absent.

What the tests prove: detected secrets do not reach provider-visible prompt content, while false positives no longer reject a whole turn or remove unrelated context. Prompt-injection containment remains independent of secret handling.

## Security Impact

The model-input boundary now scans immediately before provider dispatch, after all prompt assembly and before prompt-cache hashing. It covers plain/tool/streaming/repair paths; message content across roles; text content parts; plain reasoning and summaries; tool-call argument string keys/values and parse errors; tool descriptions and JSON schema strings/keys; and stop sequences. It logs only aggregate redaction counts, never detected values.

Opaque protocol material that requires exact replay—encrypted/redacted reasoning payloads, signatures, tool-call IDs/names, route/model identifiers, and provider metadata—is not treated as prompt text. Managed credentials remain host-side and continue to use mediated injection rather than prompt construction.

This guarantees redaction for formats recognized by the existing leak detector plus labeled weak values such as `password: letmein`; it is not a cryptographic proof that arbitrary unlabeled prose cannot contain a secret. The strongest invariant remains: secrets known to IronClaw must stay in the secret store and never be assembled into model input. The final scan is defense in depth for untrusted text and accidental leakage.

Warn-only high-entropy hex findings remain visible unless they are credential-labeled, so ordinary SHA-256 fingerprints do not mutate prompts or prompt-cache identity.

Prompt injection is intentionally not conflated with secret detection. Existing trust envelopes and injection checks still isolate offending untrusted snippets. SkillSpector-style skill trust scanning and NeMo Guardrails-style broader input/output policy remain follow-up layers rather than dependencies of this recovery hotfix.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: the new public safety transform represents model-visible redaction results without exposing findings.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts through existing structural validation and trust envelopes, then receives source-independent redaction at provider dispatch.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose; prompt-cache hashing now observes the redacted system prompt.
- [x] New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: none.
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields: none changed.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters: no durability or concurrency semantics changed.
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors: credential content no longer creates a policy-denied turn; structural errors are unchanged.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names: no trust-boundary names changed.

## Database Impact

None. Raw stored LLM/thread/memory data is retained; redaction applies to the transient model-facing view.

## Blast Radius

Prompt construction contracts, production memory admission, and all loop-host provider request shapes. A regression could leak a recognized secret, corrupt opaque replay data, or reintroduce thread-wide rejection. Caller-level provider captures, memory integration tests, structural contract tests, all-features clippy, and architecture ratchets cover those directions.

## Compatibility and Rollback

No wire or storage migration. Removing the unused `base64` dependency from `ironclaw_loop_contracts` shrinks the contract layer. Roll back by reverting this PR; stored data requires no repair. During rollback, the prior credential denylist behavior—and its false-positive thread failures—would return.

## Follow-up

- Evaluate SkillSpector in the skill install/update trust pipeline, not on every runtime text field.
- Prototype NeMo Guardrails or an equivalent classifier as an observable, shadow-mode prompt-injection layer before considering enforcement.
- Add canary metrics for redaction frequency and snippet-level injection omission without logging source text.

---

**Review track**: C (security/runtime/DB/CI)



## Prior exact-head Railway QA (269c0206f)

The first live attempt exposed a second path: after direct and JSON-encoded results were redacted, the agent retried through `shell` with `od -c`. Its character-separated output (`p a s s w o r d`) bypassed label matching even though the model could reconstruct the value. The final fix decodes only offset-prefixed character dumps for detection and replaces the encoded field when the reconstructed text contains a credential assignment. A benign `Secretary of the Treasury` dump remains unchanged.

Validation on `269c0206f8bf26ac233cd62a4e92cab9e19bba5b`:

- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_safety --no-fail-fast` (308 passed)
- [x] Provider-boundary character-dump regression in `llm_gateway`
- [x] Clippy for `ironclaw_safety` and the `llm_gateway` test target with `-D warnings`
- [x] `reborn_dependency_boundaries` (41 passed)
- [x] Repository pre-commit safety hook
- [x] Railway deploy check and CodeRabbit
- [x] Neutral browser QA with a fresh synthetic canary; benign values survived, password was `[REDACTED_SECRET]`, canary absent
- [x] Refresh/replay preserved the same redacted transcript

No real credential was used. The synthetic QA task and local fixture were deleted after verification.


## Final exact-head Railway QA (362966a24)

- [x] Commit-scoped Railway deployment succeeded for `362966a2417eaa2babb7d28cbabaa9da7595d7a4`.
- [x] Neutral browser upload exercised the real JSON attachment and model/tool recovery path using only: `Read the attached JSON and report every field and its value.`
- [x] Marker, source path, benign message, and secretary value survived; `password` rendered as `[REDACTED_SECRET]`; the exact synthetic canary and distinctive tail were absent.
- [x] A full refresh restored the completed durable task with the same safe result and no running/interrupted state.
- [x] Temporary Railway task, local fixture, credential variable, and browser tabs were cleaned up.
- [x] Canonical evidence: https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/pull/7509#issuecomment-5260115839

Final review regressions on this head cover propagation of sensitive schema context through nested composition/applicator keywords, credential redaction in URL fragments while benign state remains visible, and the corrected memory-path expectation. CodeRabbit reported no new actionable comments.

prs.title: fix(processes): lease expiry recovers safe runs instead of failing them; isolate the journal heartbeat pool
prs.body:
## Summary

- Isolate process-journal heartbeats from data-plane PostgreSQL traffic and increase the default application pool capacity.
- Recover expired runs only at replay-safe checkpoints, with a lease-TTL grace window and bounded reclaim budget.
- Fence stale executors at supervisor, heartbeat, and transcript seams; derive the CLI heartbeat limit from the runner's lease constant.
- Update recovery contracts, targeted regression coverage, and Reborn CI scope classification.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [x] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

None

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo build` — covered by the stricter all-target, all-feature clippy build.
- [x] Relevant tests pass: recovery matrix, scheduler/supervisor fencing, CLI heartbeat validation, composition boundary and PostgreSQL process-journal seam, and panic-call scanner.
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` — not applicable; selected database/runtime coverage is in the root Reborn integration suite and composition seam tests.
- [x] Manual testing: reproduced the affected state transitions and exercised the PostgreSQL journal read-back seam.
- [x] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `review-pr` or `pr-shepherd --fix` was run before requesting review: review comments and CI failures were audited directly, with focused and full lint gates run locally.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: a run whose worker loses its lease can resume from a replay-safe checkpoint instead of surfacing `lease_expired`; stale workers must not overlap a replacement or persist later output.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [x] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: recovery transition matrix, checkpoint-kind compatibility, heartbeat-budget bounds, definitive lease-loss cancellation, composition export snapshot, and CLI config rejection.
- Reborn integration: `tests/integration/lease_wedge.rs` covers safe resume, fail-closed side-effect checkpoints, completed output, and stale-worker transcript exclusion.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable; no provider/model response fixture changed.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable; no browser or WebUI behavior changed.
- Backend or runtime: composition PostgreSQL journal-pool read-back and production-wired transcript-fence seam.
- Live canary: Not applicable; no external provider behavior changed.

What the tests prove: safe checkpoints recover only after grace and within budget; unsafe/unknown checkpoints fail closed; replacement executors do not overlap locally; heartbeat configuration fits within lease timing; changed production code passes the panic scanner.

Commands run:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_turn_runner run_lease_fence_tests --lib`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --test reborn_composition_boundaries composition_public_pub_use_surface_matches_snapshot`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw --test smoke run_rejects_runner_heartbeat_interval_past_the_lease_ttl_bound`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_composition --test service_factory production_postgres_process_journal_pool_writes_rows_the_data_plane_reads` (Docker-aware test returned success; local environment did not exercise a container-backed leg)
- `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 scripts/check_no_panics.py --base origin/main --head HEAD`
- `cargo test --workspace --lib` (two unrelated `ironclaw_host_runtime` tests returned `NetworkDenied`; 476 neighboring tests in that crate passed)

## Security Impact

No permission, secret, sandbox, or network-policy changes. The runtime change strengthens lease ownership checks and preserves fail-closed recovery for checkpoints that may have performed an external side effect.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: existing process-journal and host-API types retain their current construction boundaries.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive: unchanged.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose; trust/binding/authenticity uses SHA-256/BLAKE3 or separate authenticity check: unchanged; no hashes added.
- [x] New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: downstream match sites audited. Command/output: targeted `rg` audit plus all-feature clippy; checkpoint-kind compatibility is pinned by tests.
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields fail closed or have migration tests: old or unknown checkpoint kinds resolve to the fail-closed recovery branch.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters have bounds and overflow-safe arithmetic: reclaim and heartbeat failure budgets are bounded.
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors have stable class semantics (`Transient`, `Permanent`, `Misconfigured`, `PolicyDenied` or equivalent): stale/unverifiable leases remain explicit failures; invalid CLI timing is a configuration error.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe trust boundary: unchanged.

## Database Impact

No migration or schema change. PostgreSQL deployments use a dedicated small pool for process-journal traffic; libSQL/in-memory behavior is unchanged. The new optional snapshot field is backward-compatible and unknown values fail closed.

## Blast Radius

Process recovery, turn-runner heartbeat/supervisor behavior, transcript persistence fencing, PostgreSQL pool sizing, CLI runner configuration, and Reborn CI test-scope selection. Primary risks are delayed terminalization of truly wedged model calls and connection-budget increases of two PostgreSQL connections per instance.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this PR. No data migration is required; older binaries ignore the added snapshot field and newer readers treat a missing/unknown kind conservatively. Restore the prior PostgreSQL connection budget when rolling back.

## Review Follow-Through

Review feedback on the lease-derived heartbeat bound, missing-journal polling, host-API imports, CI panic annotations, and grace-window documentation is addressed in `c2156a0d6c`. One valid reviewer concern remains open: the current transcript check is immediately before persistence but is not atomic with the separate process-journal lease authority. A complete fix needs a coordinated fencing epoch/transaction or an equivalent recovery-time ownership protocol across the process and thread stores; this PR does not claim that stronger guarantee.

---

**Review track**: C (runtime, persistence, and CI)

prs.title: feat(memory): memory-save guidance + always-on MEMORY.md prompt lane (#7185)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **The bug (#7185):** a fact the user states in conversation A is not recalled in conversation B. Two causes, both fixed here. (1) Nothing ever told the model that persistent memory exists or when a stated preference is worth saving, so it usually never called `ironclaw.memory.write` at all. (2) Even when something *was* saved, the proactive-recall lanes were **full-text search over the current turn's user message** — so recall only happened when conversation B's opening message happened to share vocabulary with the stored fact. Open a new chat on an unrelated topic and the memory is invisible.
- **Guidance is shipped by the memory extension, not the host.** The memory-save doctrine lives in `memory-native/prompts/memory-guidance.md` and is declared by that package's manifest as one new optional field, `[memory].guidance_doc`. Composition appends whatever the **bound** provider declares and writes none of it. This is the Hermes pattern: the text names that provider's own tools and describes that provider's own recall behavior, so a search-first backend can say something different from one that serves a standing document, without either editing host code. mem0 deliberately declares none — absent means nothing is appended, never a fallback to another provider's wording.
- **Curated recall is native-internal policy.** `NativeMemoryService::read_long_term` now serves its standing `MEMORY.md` at the head of its own long-term lane, ahead of the full-text hits and independent of the turn's query. A fact saved in A reaches B regardless of vocabulary overlap.
- **Zero new trait or lifecycle surface.** `MemoryService` is byte-identical to `main` — no `read_document`, no `read_curated`, no new lifecycle hook, no new wire token. The host's prompt-context service is byte-identical to `main` too: still two lanes, and it knows no document paths. The entire diff to shared contracts is one optional manifest field.
- **Write-quality doctrine:** the guidance encodes how to phrase a memory — declarative facts about the user rather than imperatives to self (an imperative is re-read as a standing directive every later turn), a staleness skip-list (task progress, session outcomes, PR numbers, commit SHAs), priority framing, and the non-append rewrite mode for an explicit forget request.
- **Approval gating deliberately unchanged** — see **Review notes (a)**. Two tests pin the actual posture instead of leaving it implicit.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Part of #7185 (memory not recalled across conversations). Also part of #7275 (proactive prompt recall — this is the non-FTS half that scenario could not cover) and part of #5260 (memory recall quality). Closes nothing on its own: #7185 also has UI/settings and recall-quality follow-ups outside this diff. Retrieval quality inside the lane (BM25 ranking) is explicitly the next PR, not this one.

## Layers touched

Every layer in the diff, in dependency order:

| Layer | File(s) | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Extension contracts | `crates/contracts/ironclaw_extension_contracts/src/memory.rs` | **The only shared-contract change in the PR:** one optional `[memory].guidance_doc` field on `MemoryDescriptor`, typed as the existing validated `CapabilityProfileSchemaRef` (the same newtype `prompt_doc_ref` uses), `#[serde(default)]`, absent ⇒ no guidance. The lifecycle vocabulary is unchanged. |
| memory-native package | `prompts/memory-guidance.md` (new), `manifest.toml`, `src/service.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `AGENTS.md` | Ships the guidance asset and declares it; exports `MEMORY_GUIDANCE_DOC_REF` + `MEMORY_GUIDANCE` so the host resolves it through this package's **public API** rather than compiling its asset tree in (see Review notes (c)). `read_long_term` gains the curated prefix, with the splitter, budget, line joining, and truncation marker as provider-internal policy. Append-mode writes terminate each entry with exactly one newline — without it two guided saves persist as one run-on line. |
| mem0 package | `manifest.toml` | Declares no `guidance_doc`, with the reason in a manifest comment (search-first recall, no standing document). No Rust change; `read_long_term` untouched. |
| Host runtime | `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/memory_native_extension.rs` | `memory_guidance_text(&MemoryDescriptor)` maps a declared ref onto the owning package's exported text. Fail-quiet: an unclaimed ref appends nothing rather than failing a boot. |
| Composition (prompt assembly) | `src/root/default_system_prompt.rs`, `src/runtime.rs`, `src/memory_provider_factory.rs` | `SystemPromptProtocols.memory_guidance: Option<String>` carries provider **content**, not a host flag. Appended only when a provider is actually bound *and* it declares guidance. The three positional `bool`s on `try_new` became a named struct. |
| Composition (gate pinning) | `src/capability_authorization/tests.rs` | Helper generalized to take an `ApprovalSettingsProvider`; two new tests pin `ironclaw.memory.write` under default settings (Allow) and with auto-approve off (RequireApproval). Test-only. |
| Integration | `tests/integration/group_memory/scenario_always_on_memory_recall_libsql.rs`, `main.rs`, `tests/CLAUDE.md` | New always-on scenario (real composition + libSQL). |
| Unchanged, deliberately | `crates/domains/ironclaw_memory/src/service.rs`, `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/memory_context.rs`, `crates/loop/ironclaw_loop_host/**` | Byte-identical to `main`. The trait gained nothing, the host lane count did not change, and the loop tier owns no memory prompt text. |

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt`
- [x] `cargo clippy` over every touched crate, `--all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — zero warnings
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-features --all-targets`
- [x] Relevant tests pass — see Test Strategy
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` — **not run**: no Postgres/Docker-gated behavior changed. The persistence-adjacent path is exercised over real libSQL in the Reborn integration tier instead. Docker availability was not checked.
- [x] Manual testing: not applicable beyond the automated tiers — the recall path is only observable through the assembled model prompt, which the integration scenario asserts directly.

## Test Strategy

**User behavior:** A user mentions a durable preference in one conversation ("by the way, I race a kayak named quokka every autumn"). Later, in a brand-new conversation opened on a completely unrelated topic ("can you help me draft a thank-you note?"), the assistant already knows it — without the user repeating it and without the assistant running a memory search. Another user on the same deployment never sees that fact.

**Risk areas:**
- [x] Model behavior (provider-shipped guidance appended whenever memory is bound changes what the model does every turn)
- [ ] Browser
- [x] Side effect (memory writes)
- [x] Persistence (reads the standing `MEMORY.md` every run)
- [x] Security or permissions (untrusted content entering the prompt; approval-gate posture; cross-scope isolation)
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior (contracts → provider → host → composition)

**Tests added or updated:**
- **Unit or contract:**
  - `ironclaw_extension_contracts`: `guidance_doc` is absent unless declared and implies no lifecycle; a path escaping the package fails the parse.
  - `ironclaw_host_runtime` `memory_native_extension` (+3): the native bundle's declared ref resolves to real text that opens with a heading and names the tool it tells the model to call; a provider declaring none resolves to `None` (never a fallback to native's); an unrecognized ref is fail-quiet.
  - `ironclaw_memory_native` `memory_service_contract` (+6): an unrelated query still returns the standing document **first**; a query's own search hit is still admitted behind it; an absent document degrades the lane to search-only rather than failing; consecutive guided appends stay separate facts; another user's standing document never reaches this lane; an oversized document is capped at its own budget and the last chunk is marked `(truncated)`.
  - `ironclaw_composition` `default_system_prompt`: the bound provider's guidance is in the resolved prompt for a freshly seeded install **and** for a user-edited `SYSTEM.md` that predates it, is never written into the user's file, and is absent with no provider bound. The tests use their own fixture text, not any real provider's asset — the rule under test is composition's, not one provider's wording.
  - `ironclaw_composition` `runtime` (caller tier): a standalone runtime with a bound provider really does inject the guidance. The unit tests prove the gate is honored once set; this proves it tracks the real binding.
  - `ironclaw_composition` `capability_authorization` (+2): `ironclaw.memory.write` → Allow under default settings; → RequireApproval with auto-approve off. Both drive the real manifest-projected descriptor through the real authorizer.
- **Reborn integration:** `scenario_always_on_memory_recall_libsql.rs` — real composition, real libSQL, real runner. Conversation A's scripted model saves with `append: true` on a user message that never asks it to remember anything; conversation B opens with a message sharing **no content word** with the fact and makes **no memory tool call**; the fact must appear in B's system prompt. A second user's `MEMORY.md` written to the same composite must not. **This scenario is unchanged across the rework** and is the behavior-neutrality proof: the curated read moved from a host-composed third lane into the provider's own `read_long_term` without touching a line of it.
- **Recorded fixture / Browser E2E / Live canary:** Not applicable — no provider request shape, WebUI surface, or credentialed surface changed. **Not run.**
- **Backend or runtime:** Not applicable as a separate feature-gated leg: no schema, migration, or backend-specific behavior changed. **Postgres legs not run** (Docker availability not checked).

**What the tests prove:** that recall works *for the stated reason*. The integration scenario is constructed so that no full-text retrieval can satisfy it — zero vocabulary overlap and no tool call — so only the standing-document prefix can put the fact in the prompt. The provider-tier suite proves the prefix is bounded, scoped, and degrades to search-only when absent. The contract and host tests prove guidance is provider-owned in both directions: declared ⇒ served, undeclared ⇒ nothing, unknown ⇒ nothing.

## Security Impact

This puts **more** stored content in front of the model on **every** turn, so the prompt-safety envelope is the load-bearing part. The curated prefix reuses the existing host-owned pipeline unchanged, and adds nothing that bypasses it — the host cannot tell a curated chunk from a search hit, which is the point:

- **Scope:** the provider resolves the document under the invocation's own scope, and the host's existing `ExpectedScope` filter still drops any snippet whose scope does not match the request. Another user's `MEMORY.md` is unreachable, covered by a provider-tier test and by the integration scenario's negative control on one shared libSQL composite.
- **Untrusted content:** every chunk goes through the unmodified `wrap_untrusted_with_limit(EnvelopeSource::Memory, EnvelopeTrust::Untrusted, …)` envelope and the `LoopSafeSummary` prompt denylist, exactly as a search snippet does. Chunking is what makes this hold — see Review notes (b). The host remains the sole constructor of admitted loop-context snippets.
- **Privacy:** the memory-disabled context profile short-circuits **before the document read**, not only before the search, so a disabled profile issues no curated read at all.
- **Bounds:** the prefix is capped at 4 snippets of ≤400 raw bytes inside the caller's `max_snippets`, with `saturating_*` arithmetic throughout, and the splitter stops at `budget + 1` chunks so a large user-controlled document is never fully materialized just to be discarded.
- **Permissions:** no capability's gate, effects, `default_permission`, or `origin_gate_matrix` changed. `UNGATED_LOOP_RUN_CAPABILITIES` and `builtin_capability_policy.toml` are untouched. See Review notes (a).

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] **Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: who can construct them?** No new trust-bearing type. `MemoryServiceContextSnippet` (already provider-constructible, already treated as untrusted) is the only DTO crossing the seam, and it crossed it before this PR.
- [x] **Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive.** Yes, unchanged — see Review notes (b).
- [x] **Hashes declare purpose.** No new hashing.
- [x] **New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: downstream match sites audited.** None. No new enum variant, no new trait method, no new lifecycle token.
- [x] **Security/durability `serde(default)` fields fail closed or have migration tests.** One new `serde(default)` field, `[memory].guidance_doc`. It is fail-**quiet** by design rather than fail-closed, and that is the honest posture: it carries no authority, gates nothing, and its absence means "append no guidance". A ref that is not a valid relative asset path fails the manifest parse; a valid ref no bundled provider claims appends nothing. Both directions are tested.
- [x] **Queues/maps/buffers/counters have bounds and overflow-safe arithmetic.** `MAX_CURATED_SNIPPETS`, `CURATED_CHUNK_RAW_BYTES`, `saturating_add`/`saturating_sub`, and a splitter that is linear in the document and stops at the budget. The truncation marker reserves its own room rather than growing a chunk past its cap.
- [x] **Driver/operator-visible errors have stable class semantics.** No new error variant. An absent or unreadable standing document degrades the lane to search-only with a `debug!` — memory is best-effort and never fails a turn.
- [x] **Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe trust boundary.** `memory_guidance_text` returns static bundled text and nothing else; no name implies more trust than is held.

## Database Impact

**None.** No migration, no schema change, no new table or column. The curated prefix is a read of an existing memory document through the existing repository path, so PostgreSQL- and libSQL-backed deployments behave identically; the integration scenario runs over real libSQL.

## Blast Radius

- **Every turn's system prompt** grows by the ~11-line guidance plus the user's own standing facts, whenever a memory provider is bound. This is the intended change and the main thing to weigh: it costs prompt budget on every request, and it changes model behavior (the model is now told to save durable facts unprompted).
- **The long-term lane's composition shifts**: up to 4 of the caller's snippet allowance now goes to the standing document ahead of full-text hits, so a low-ranked search hit can be displaced. Bounded by design and asserted by `native_long_term_lane_keeps_search_hits_behind_the_standing_document`.
- **Memory providers**: native serves the prefix and ships guidance. mem0 is untouched — no prefix, no guidance, no behavior change of any kind. A third-party provider is likewise unaffected unless it opts in.
- **What could break**: a `MEMORY.md` whose lines trip the prompt denylist has *those lines* dropped rather than the whole document — chunking makes this strictly better than a single wide snippet, but it does mean partial content.
- Not touched: the `MemoryService` trait, the host prompt-context service, the loop tier, transports, projections, events, approvals runtime behavior, WebUI, migrations, CI.

## Rollback Plan

`git revert` the feature commits. There are **no schema changes, no migrations, and no persisted format changes**, so revert is complete and immediate: the provider stops prepending the standing document, the guidance stops being appended, and recall returns to full-text-only. Documents already written to `MEMORY.md` remain valid and keep working through the ordinary `ironclaw.memory.read`/`search` tools. Removing `guidance_doc` from the native manifest is a one-line partial rollback that drops the prompt guidance while leaving retrieval intact.

## Review notes

### (a) Approval gating is deliberately unchanged

The issue's framing suggests saving a memory should not raise an approval prompt. I investigated the seam and concluded the right move is to change nothing and pin the behavior instead. The reasoning, so a reviewer can disagree with it explicitly:

- **An argument-aware gate does not exist.** The authorization seam is `TrustAwareCapabilityDispatchAuthorizer::authorize_dispatch_with_trust(context, descriptor, estimate, trust_decision)`, and `ProfileApprovalGatePolicy::{capability_exempt_from_approval, origin_gate_requirement}` only ever see the `CapabilityDescriptor`. The invocation input never reaches the gate. So "ungated when the resolved target is `memory`, gated otherwise" is **not expressible** without a new argument-aware authorization stage — a cross-cutting change to the authorization contract, well beyond this PR.
- **On the default path there is no prompt to remove.** `AUTO_APPROVE_DEFAULT_ENABLED = true`, so for a never-configured user `ironclaw.memory.write` is allowed at the global-auto-approve step before the effect gate is reached. Pinned by `standalone_memory_write_is_auto_approved_under_default_settings`.
- **The gate only fires for users who deliberately turned auto-approve off** — and for them, being asked before an arbitrary-path write is the behavior they chose. Pinned by `standalone_memory_write_still_gates_when_auto_approve_is_off`.
- **Therefore the obvious alternative fails the "fail toward less exposure" test.** A separate always-ungated `ironclaw.memory.save` would only change behavior for exactly the population that opted into being asked, while adding a permanent sixth model-facing memory tool for zero default-path benefit.

**Deferred, not rejected:** if we do want unprompted saving for auto-approve-off users, the clean shape is a narrowly scoped append-only `ironclaw.memory.save` restricted to curated targets, ungated + exempt, with `ironclaw.memory.write` left exactly as it is. That is a security-reviewed follow-up, and I would rather it be reviewed on its own merits than smuggled in here.

### (b) Why the standing document is chunked instead of served as one wide snippet

The natural implementation is "read `MEMORY.md`, return it as one 2 KiB snippet." That would be a security regression, worth stating plainly because the code looks more complicated than it needs to be:

A `LoopContextSnippet`'s model-visible text is validated through `LoopSafeSummary` → `SafeSummary`, which is capped at **512 bytes** *and* is where the prompt denylist runs (path delimiters, credential markers, secret-like tokens, control characters). A wider snippet would mean the denylist only ever inspects the head of the document — a secret on line 40 of `MEMORY.md` would sail into the prompt unchecked.

So the provider splits the document on **line boundaries** into ≤400-byte chunks, each of which goes through the *unmodified* host sanitize + envelope + denylist path. Consequences worth noting:

- Every byte the model sees passed the same check a search snippet passes.
- A line carrying a denylisted secret is dropped **on its own**; the surrounding facts still reach the model.
- Lines within a chunk are joined with `"; "`, not `\n`: raw newlines are control characters and are stripped during sanitization, which would silently run two facts together. The same reasoning is why append-mode writes now terminate each entry with exactly one newline.
- The truncation marker is `" (truncated)"` — plain words, because `[`, `]`, and other delimiters are rejected by the safe-summary rule — and it reserves its own room rather than pushing a chunk past its cap.

### (c) Why guidance is extension-shipped, and why the host reads it through a public API

Two decisions here, both deliberate:

**Provider-owned rather than loop-owned.** An earlier revision put this text in `ironclaw_loop_host` beside the other system-prompt assets. That was wrong: the text names concrete `ironclaw.memory.*` tools and describes one provider's recall behavior. mem0's recall is search-first and it serves no standing document, so native's "save it to `memory`, it comes back every turn" advice would be actively misleading under a mem0 binding — and under the loop-owned shape there was no way to say so short of host code branching on provider identity. Declaring the doc in the manifest that already declares the tools puts the wording next to the thing it describes and makes "no guidance" a first-class, honest answer.

**Resolved through `ironclaw_memory_native`'s public API, not `include_str!`.** The first cut compiled the asset in from the host crate, matching the existing inline-schema precedent — and `reborn_cross_crate_include_scan` correctly rejected it. §11.2.7 is shrink-only: a new reach-in compiles another crate's tree into this one and bypasses the dependency graph the boundary gates police. So the package exports `MEMORY_GUIDANCE_DOC_REF` and `MEMORY_GUIDANCE` and the host matches the declared ref against them. The inventory stays at 16, and the ref and the text now live in one file, so a rename cannot silently desynchronize the manifest from the asset.

### (d) mem0 and the target-alias divergence (#7505)

The earlier host-composed lane called `read_document("MEMORY.md")` against **any** bound provider, which surfaced a pre-existing inconsistency: the shared write prompt teaches the model `target: "memory"`, which native canonicalizes to `MEMORY.md` while mem0 stores verbatim.

**This rework removes lane code from that question entirely.** The curated prefix is now native-internal, so mem0's `read_long_term` is untouched and issues no extra read. The divergence remains a real tool-path/contract issue — cross-provider document identity is still inconsistent on the `ironclaw.memory.read`/`write` path — and stays tracked as **#7505**. It is no longer on this PR's critical path in either direction.

## Review Follow-Through

- **Reviewer judgment wanted on (a)**: the decision not to touch gating is the one place I chose against the obvious reading of the issue.
- **The budget split is now provider-internal policy, not a host guarantee.** Under the previous shape the host reserved half the aggregate byte budget for the curated lane and no provider could exceed it. Now the native provider decides how much of its own `max_snippets` allowance the standing document takes. That is the right ownership — a provider knows what its lane should contain — but it does mean a future provider could return an unbalanced lane, and the host's only remaining backstop is the aggregate byte budget it already enforced. Flagging it explicitly rather than leaving it implied.
- **Known gaps, stated rather than hidden**: Postgres-gated suites and the browser E2E suite were not run (no Docker check performed; no WebUI or backend-specific behavior changed). `MEMORY.md` hygiene (dedup, aging out stale facts) and retrieval ranking (BM25) are not addressed here and are the next steps on #7185.

---

**Review track**: C (security/runtime — untrusted content entering the prompt on every turn, plus the approval-gate posture)

## Summary

- add a strict release-only `IRONCLAW_REBORN_ENABLE_RAILWAY_SANDBOX_SHELL` alias for `hosted-single-tenant-volume`
- preserve base-volume storage paths while reusing the existing Railway user-sandbox runtime and process binding
- expose Railway-only shell guidance, including that sandbox `/workspace` is separate from the IronClaw user workspace
- keep local Docker and other user-sandbox consumers on generic guidance only

## Change Type

- [x] Local multi-agent code review ran; both findings were fixed and re-reviewed

User behavior: Operators can retain `hosted-single-tenant-volume` durable paths while explicitly enabling the existing Railway sandbox shell.

Risk areas:

- `cargo test`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw --bin ironclaw`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_host_runtime --test first_party_builtin_tools`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_extension_support`

Shell is enabled only by an explicit operator variable and reuses the existing fail-closed Railway `UserSandbox` binding. ## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive: added guidance is trusted static host content

- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters have bounds and overflow-safe arithmetic: N/A, none changed
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors have stable class semantics: existing strict environment and Railway binding errors are preserved

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

CLI runtime-profile resolution, local storage-root selection, builtin shell descriptions, and composition wiring for supplemental guidance. The base-volume default remains processless when the override is unset or false.

## Rollback Plan

Unset the variable or set `IRONCLAW_REBORN_ENABLE_RAILWAY_SANDBOX_SHELL=false`. No persisted profile or schema migration is introduced.

## Review Follow-Through

Local eight-lane review found no production bug or security issue. Its two test-coverage findings were fixed and scoped re-review confirmed both addressed. The repository-wide composition budget remains pre-existing debt and was not changed or waived here.

prs.title: feat(slack): bind the remaining eight core standard messaging ops
prs.body:
## Summary

Slack bound **8 of the 16** core standard messaging operations. The other eight were a named fast-follow the framework design spec deferred (§13 *"Deliberately not built"* — `New Slack ops / scopes (edit, delete, reactions, open_dm, resolve_user) | keeps this the framework PR | immediate fast-follow after merge`). This lands them, so Slack now covers the full core vocabulary.

Note the deferral row named five; the real gap was eight — `get_message` and `list_members` were unaccounted for, and both needed no new scope.

| Op | Slack API | New scope |
|---|---|---|
| `edit_message` | `chat.update` | — (`chat:write`) |
| `delete_message` | `chat.delete` | — (`chat:write`) |
| `get_message` | `conversations.history` + `.replies` | — |
| `list_members` | `conversations.members` | — |
| `resolve_user` | `users.list` + local filter | — |
| `add_reaction` | `reactions.add` | `reactions:write` |
| `remove_reaction` | `reactions.remove` + `.get` | `reactions:read`, `reactions:write` |
| `open_dm` | `conversations.open` | `im:write` |

## Layers in this diff

- **Manifest** — 8 new `standard_op`-bound `[[tools]]`, appended after the v2-era eight so the projection-parity gate's positional comparison still holds.
- **WASM guest** — vendor mechanics + types + dispatch; artifact rebuilt, `wasm-src-digests.toml` re-recorded (only Slack's digest moved).
- **Package embeds** — 8 prompt addenda registered in `extension_support::packages::slack`.
- **Gates** — the v2→v3 parity suite and the catalog scope pin (see below).
- **Docs** — `standard-operations.md`, `crates/extensions/AGENTS.md`, package README.

## Three behaviours worth reviewing

**`get_message` has no Slack endpoint.** It reads the conversation at the exact `ts` and falls back to the thread when the message is a threaded reply, accepting only an exact match. `conversations.history`'s `latest` is a *range* bound, so a near miss would otherwise return the neighbouring message as though it were the one asked for — that returns `messaging.unknown_message` instead.

**`remove_reaction`'s optional `emoji` is implemented, not rejected.** The canonical schema leaves it optional because some vendors can clear "my reaction" without naming it; Slack's endpoint *requires* a name. The omit-emoji variant therefore reads the message's reactions and removes each one the connected account added. That is why `reactions:read` joins the grant, and why that variant returns no `emoji` — exactly the case the output schema leaves optional. The identity lookup there is fatal rather than best-effort: without knowing who "we" are, the filter could remove someone else's reaction.

**`already_reacted` / `no_reaction` are treated as success.** Slack returns them only for a message it resolved, so the requested end state holds; an error would push the model into retrying a no-op. It also makes the removal loop converge on retry after a partial failure (Slack has no batch reaction removal, so a mid-loop failure leaves earlier removals applied).

## Compatibility

**The scope widening breaks existing connections.** There is no scope-upgrade re-consent flow, so an account connected before this change holds a token without `reactions:read` / `reactions:write` / `im:write`. Slack answers those three tools with `missing_scope`, mapped to `messaging.permission_denied` — a model-visible denial, deliberately **not** an `AuthRequired` re-auth gate, since re-running OAuth would request the same manifest scopes and change nothing. Widening an existing grant means disconnecting and reconnecting Slack; the other 13 tools are unaffected.

**Rollback:** reverting restores the 8-tool surface and the narrower grant. Already-widened user tokens keep unused scopes, which is inert.

## Two pins evolved, not relaxed

The v2→v3 parity gate would have frozen the manifest forever, and updating the frozen v2 fixture would have falsified the historical baseline. Instead the v2-era eight still project **identically and positionally**, while additions are declared in a `PackageAdditions` struct — capability ids *and* the exact scope delta, with the ceiling asserted to only ever grow (a disappearing scope fails too). The catalog scope pin moved from `assert!(matches!(..))` to `assert_eq!` so a future drift prints *which* scope moved rather than a bare "assertion failed".

## Test Strategy

- **Unit/contract (guest):** 24 tests — canonical input serde for all 8 ops, output shapes (incl. `deleted: true`, omitted-vs-null optionals), the reaction authorship filter, exact-ts matching, the idempotent-success arms (including that each endpoint accepts only *its own* end-state code), directory matching and bot/deactivated skipping, the error taxonomy, and capability-id dispatch across all 16.
- **Crate/composition:** manifest projection asserts all 16 bind exactly the core set, ids are `slack.<op_name>`, both schema refs are host-synthesized, writes declare `external_write`, each ships an addendum, and every tool runs on the user token.
- **Sabotage-verified:** the authorship filter, exact-ts matching, and both evolved gate assertions each fail when inverted.
- **Architecture:** `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests` green.
- **Not applicable — integration tier:** the guest's HTTP path is unreachable in-process; no production wiring outside the manifest changed.

**Known gap:** the I/O orchestration *inside* each operation — which calls run, in what order, and that a failed `auth.test` aborts the omit-emoji removal — is unreachable without introducing a host seam in the WASM guest. Flagging rather than hiding it.

## Pre-existing failure, not from this change

`ironclaw_composition --lib runtime::tests::multi_tool_call_response_survives_surface_change_mid_register` fails under the full suite and passes in isolation. Verified pre-existing: stashing this branch's changes reproduces the identical `528 passed; 1 failed` on a clean tree. The test installs **github**, not slack.

prs.title: fix(threads): restore listability for unprojected thread index rows
prs.body:
## Verified bug

A `thread_index` row can exist durably while carrying no ordered-projection metadata. The sidebar reads the `thread_activity_v2` ordered projection, and that projection only emits a row when the stored entry holds the listing keys — so such a thread is **absent from `list_threads` while its thread record, index record and every message are intact**.

Observed on staging (`ai-infra-nearai-staging-01`), read-only inspection of live volumes:

| Box | Image | Thread records | Listed by API |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `quick-fox-razuh` | `1.1.1-rc.1` | 5 | **4** |
| `calm-cod-basip` | `1.1.0-rc.1-stg` | 2 | **1** |

On `quick-fox-razuh` the missing thread has 13 messages and a valid index record; its `indexed` column is `{}` where its four siblings carry `{scope_key, activity_sort, thread_id}`. The projection table holds exactly 4 rows. `GET /api/webchat/v2/threads` returns 200 with the thread simply absent — no error, no empty state.

This is the first failure mode listed in #7178 ("Thread headers still exist, but the 1.1 ordered sidebar projection cannot find them").

## Root cause

Two layers, only the second of which this PR closes.

**How a row gets damaged (not fixed here).** The damaged staging rows carry no `projection_schema_version` field at all, so they were written by a binary predating it — on a volume whose `thread-index-v2.complete` marker had already been written minutes earlier by a newer one (15:22:35 marker, 15:27:14 damaged row, 15:54:54 restart onto `1.1.1-rc.1`). Their `kind` is intact while only the indexed sidecar is empty, which is what a record-plane write from an older projection shape looks like. Mixed binaries against one volume is the suspected origin. **This PR does not close that.**

**Why the damage is permanent (fixed here).** Once a scope has its completion marker, `ensure_thread_index_query` short-circuits and no repair pass runs again — so a row damaged after that point stays invisible for the life of the volume, across every restart and upgrade. Confirmed on `calm-cod-basip`, where the broken row has already survived later container starts untouched.

## Fix

Reconcile the scope behind the existing declaration gate: compare the durable index directory against the projected rows, and repair only when they disagree.

Repair uses the shared bounded `cas_update` loop with an explicit `CasApply::force_write` operation. The new operation bypasses only decoded-body equality so sidecar-only damage is physically rewritten, while preserving capability checks, version preconditions, bounded retries, backoff, and timeout. A selective precheck keeps already-correct rows read-only.

A healthy scope costs one bounded directory listing plus one capped query. When the counts disagree, repair selectively reads each bounded candidate row and conditionally rewrites only rows with stale projection keys; this damaged-scope path remains sequential and capped at `Page::MAX_LIMIT`. A scope holding more index rows than `Page::MAX_LIMIT` is skipped rather than walked page by page, because this runs inside a live listing request and an unbounded scan would put a latency spike proportional to scope size on the first request after a restart. Those scopes keep today’s behavior; no full repair path exists for marker-complete scopes above the cap. That limitation is explicit in this PR and requires a separate pagewise/background repair design rather than unbounded work on the live listing path.

Reconcile failure is non-fatal: before this pass a scope with its marker written did no further I/O here and could not fail, so propagating a transient storage error would break a listing that previously succeeded.

The repair lives in a child module beside the index query, matching how `startup_migration` and `transcript_migration` own their projections, and keeping `thread_index.rs` under the file-size gate (1122 → 999 lines at the current head).

## Regression tests

The recovery regressions drive `list_threads_for_scope` through a **fresh service** (a process restart) after damaging a row, exercising the real production chain rather than calling the repair directly.

- `filesystem_list_threads_recovers_index_row_without_projection_keys` — the exact staging shape: no projection metadata, body predating `projection_schema_version`.
- `filesystem_list_threads_recovers_current_version_index_row_without_projection_keys` — strips only the projection metadata, so the body still compares equal to a rebuild. **This one fails against a merge-based repair**, pinning the `cas_update` no-op hazard.

- `filesystem_list_threads_degrades_to_projected_rows_when_reconcile_fails` — proves non-fatal degradation and retry on the next request.
- `filesystem_list_threads_retries_reconcile_projection_repair_after_cas_race` — injects one version mismatch and proves bounded CAS retry repairs the row.
- `filesystem_list_threads_reconciles_unrelated_scopes_independently` — proves one scope’s blocked reconcile does not stall another scope.
- `filesystem_list_threads_skips_reconcile_for_oversized_scope` — pins the `Page::MAX_LIMIT + 1` boundary.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p ironclaw_filesystem                                 # all unit and contract suites passed\ncargo test -p ironclaw_threads                                    # 247 passed, 0 failed\ncargo clippy -p ironclaw_filesystem -p ironclaw_threads --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings  # clean\nbash scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh                                 # passed
```

Red-before/green-after evidence covers the original recovery failure, forced sidecar rewrite after a version mismatch, and unrelated-scope progress under a blocked reconcile.

## Coverage limits and known gaps

- **Containment, not a root-cause fix.** If a stale binary is still writing to these volumes, a row damaged *after* reconcile runs for a given process stays invisible until the next restart — better MTTR, same class of bug.
- The reconcile re-runs if a scope is evicted from the 128-entry reconciled-scope cache, so a process working more than 128 concurrent scopes may pay the check again as scopes cycle; this cache is a best-effort optimization with nondeterministic eviction.
- Scopes above `Page::MAX_LIMIT` rows are deliberately not reconciled (largest observed on the fleet is 820).
- Tests run against `InMemoryBackend`, consistent with the rest of this contract suite.
- `main` has no `projection_schema_version` at all — that mechanism exists only on the release branches, so this is not a straight cherry-pick forward.

Refs #7178

prs.title: feat(telegram): linked-device — device-link auth, session custody, standard-op tools
prs.body:
Implements [#7443](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/pull/7443)'s design. **Branched off the docs PR**, so review that one first — this PR assumes its decisions.

A user links their personal Telegram account as a real MTProto linked device (visible and revocable in Telegram's Settings → Devices), and the agent reads their conversations and acts as them through the standard messaging operations. **Reads are live; no message content is persisted.**

## Draft, deliberately

Everything below is verified locally. But the design's own checklist is largely unticked, and I would rather you see an accurate account than a green-looking PR that hides stubs. **Read "What is not done" before reviewing depth-first.**

## What is verified green locally

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | **zero warnings** |
| `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` | clean |
| `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests` | **all 25 gate binaries pass** |
| `ironclaw_auth` | 312 pass (incl. `module_charter` 4/4) |
| `ironclaw_extension_host` | 430 pass |
| `ironclaw_host_api` | 281 pass |
| `ironclaw_extension_contracts` | 131 pass |
| `ironclaw_telegram_extension` | 188 pass |

166 files, +19,132/−636.

## The decisions worth reviewing

**The schema is a `.v2` graduation, not an edit.** `send_message.output.v1.json` is byte-identical — verify that first, because the standard's immutability rule forbids an in-place change and an earlier design revision got this wrong. Resolution is now version-aware so existing Slack and acme bindings keep resolving `.v1` forever.

**`id == 0` returns `Completed` with `sent_unverified`, never a failure.** grammers returns a zero id when it cannot correlate a send that *did happen*. Mapping that to a failure is what makes a model retry — and the retry double-sends, as the user, to a human. `Dropped`/`Io` on a write is a genuinely different state (outcome unknown) and maps to `vendor_error` instead.

**`NoRetries` plus an explicit wrapper.** grammers' default `AutoSleep` re-sends once on an I/O error, and no custom policy can prevent it — `RetryContext` cannot see whether a request is a write.

**The `=0.10.0` pin is a security control.** 0.10.0 never persists server-pushed DC addresses, which is the only reason address validation in `IronclawSession` covers 100% of dials. A routine bump silently weakens it.

**Two gate decisions I made that a reviewer should confirm:**
- Vendor names stripped from generic crates (four were in comments; one was the word "notion" in "no notion of", matching the Notion vendor).
- Cross-crate include ratchet **16 → 17**, recorded deliberately in that file. The telegram package gained prompt docs when it gained tools, using the same `include_bytes!` shape Slack already uses. Not a new class of reach-in, and not repointable while the layer matrix forbids `runtimes → products`. **This is the one place I widened a shrink-only ratchet — push back if you disagree.**

## Follow-up: three defects found by driving the real flow (2026-08-11)

A local stack with real MTProto credentials surfaced three bugs that every
test tier passed. Each sits at a seam between two things individually tested.

1. **Blank ids for ids the caller does not have.** The chat auth-gate card
   reads scope from a gate model with no `threadId` and a null `invocationId`,
   so it posted `thread_id: ""`. The host parses each into a validated newtype
   that rejects a blank, so `start` returned `400 invalid_request`. Absent
   optional ids are now omitted at one API choke point. Required fields are
   deliberately not filtered — a blank `provider` must be rejected, not vanish.
2. **`start` minted an invocation and never returned it.** `scope_matches` is
   exact equality over the whole scope, and poll/input/cancel re-derive that
   scope from the browser. A card opened outside a run (the Extensions modal —
   no run, no gate) has no invocation to carry in, so the host minted one and
   stored the flow under it, with no way for the browser to learn it: the flow
   could be **started and never advanced**. `DeviceLinkFlowResponse` now echoes
   `invocation_id`, as `ManualTokenSetupResponse` already does.
3. **A still-valid QR reported as "nothing to show".** Telegram returns the
   same token bytes on every poll within a token's window; `paint_token`
   mapped unchanged bytes to `AwaitingVendor` ("nothing to show"), so the card
   blanked the code one poll after painting it. It now always returns
   `Display`. Consequent dead code removed (`poll_interval` + constants, the
   write-only `AwaitingScan { token }`); pacing comes from the host's 3s
   `DEVICE_LINK_POLL_INTERVAL_MILLIS`, the cadence the module header documents.

**Compatibility:** `invocation_id` is a new required field on a response DTO no
released client consumes; the frontend changes are additive at the request
boundary and widen what the host accepts nowhere.

**Not in this PR:** the local launcher (in dotfiles, not this repo) wipes
`telegram_api_id` on every run, because admin configuration is a *replace* and
the launcher omits that non-secret handle. Fixed locally; anyone else running
the local stack will hit it.

## What is NOT done

- **Live-Telegram verification is partial.** `start → poll → cancel` now runs
  against real MTProto — the code is exported, re-exported, and still shown on
  the second poll. **Nobody has scanned it**, so acceptance, DC migration, 2FA,
  and the credential mint on completion are unexercised at every tier. Closing
  this needs a real account and a human, which no PR provisions.
- **A failed linked session still reconnects before `link_revision` changes.**
  The pool's revision key and the custody gate exist and are wired, but nothing
  records a session-level *failure*, so there is no behavior to assert.
- **`error_code: "internal"` collapses distinct causes.** "MTProto not
  configured", "half-configured", and a real vendor failure render the same
  message with nothing logged. This cost two diagnostic round trips during
  manual testing and is the next thing I would fix.
- **§6.4 read-content obligations not implemented** — #7397 landed the pattern
  to reuse; this PR does not yet use it.
- **`sent_unverified` conformance coverage** for both output branches is
  incomplete.
- **Remaining PROPOSAL §14.2–14.4 security conditions** beyond the supply-chain
  pin (which is armed, below) have not been re-verified in this pass.

## Test Strategy

- **Unit/contract:** touched crates green — `ironclaw_telegram_extension` 201,
  `ironclaw_webui` all suites, 1,271 frontend vitest. Both new guards were
  sabotage-checked (reverting each fix fails its test).
- **Integration:** `reborn_group_device_link` **15/15**, including
  `scenario_handshake_mints_and_serves`, which drives the production
  `DeviceLinkFlowDriver` start → poll → submit → completed and asserts the
  minted account's §4.5 ownership pin (`ExtensionOwned`, `owner_extension`,
  empty grants), that custody actually persisted, and that a linked tool call
  resolves to that account.
- **Architecture:** full suite green, including the telegram gates and
  `reborn_linked_device_supply_chain_pin` (version + checksum + resolved
  feature sets, proxy feature off).
- **Lint:** clippy clean on both touched crates with `-D warnings`.
- **E2E / live:** partial — see the first bullet above.

prs.title: fix(memory): resolve target aliases in the domain contract layer (#7505)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **The bug:** the two bundled providers declare the same conventional `ironclaw.memory.write` / `.read` tools and reuse the same prompt/schema, but only native resolved the prompt's target aliases. mem0 stored `target: "memory"` verbatim, so a canonical `MEMORY.md` read could never find it.
- **Ownership:** add the optional conventional document-tool target vocabulary to `ironclaw_memory`, beside the capability IDs, request DTOs, and wire helpers that already define those shared tools. This is **not** a requirement on every `MemoryService` provider: providers may expose different tools or none, exactly as `service.rs` documents.
- **Providers:** native deletes its private alias table and uses the shared resolver. mem0 resolves aliases before storing `metadata.target`, reports the canonical path, and matches legacy alias tags on reads so pre-existing `"memory"` rows remain reachable at `MEMORY.md`.
- **Conformance:** lifecycle conformance remains independent and keeps its original `(factory, seed)` shape. A new, separate opt-in `memory_document_tool_contract!` is wired only by providers whose manifests declare the conventional write/read pair with the shared prompt/schema. Both bundled providers opt in; a future lifecycle-only or custom-tool provider does not.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

Fixes #7505

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_memory -p ironclaw_memory_native -p ironclaw_memory_mem0 --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

- [ ] Manual testing — not applicable beyond the automated provider seams
- [ ] `review-pr` / `pr-shepherd --fix` — not run

## Test Strategy

**User behavior:** a fact saved through mem0's conventional write tool with `target: "memory"` is readable at `MEMORY.md`; pre-existing mem0 rows tagged with legacy `"memory"` remain readable.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior — mem0 now reports the canonical path in its write response; prompt wording is unchanged
- [ ] Browser
- [x] Side effect — new mem0 rows store the canonical target tag
- [x] Persistence — legacy alias tags remain readable; no migration/deletion
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider — mem0 adapter mapping
- [x] Cross-component behavior — optional domain tool vocabulary → native/mem0 adapters → opt-in conformance

Tests added or updated:
- **Unit or contract:**
  - `ironclaw_memory` target vocabulary: fixed aliases, timezone-aware `daily_log`, invalid timezone, pass-through paths, legacy alias identity.
  - New opt-in `memory_document_tool_contract!`: write `target: "memory"`, read `MEMORY.md`, require the fact. The existing lifecycle macros no longer know about or require document tools.
  - Native and mem0 explicitly opt in because both manifests declare `ironclaw.memory.write` + `.read` with the shared prompt/schema.
  - mem0 unit tests pin canonical stored/write-response path, shared `daily_log` timezone behavior, and legacy `"memory"` + canonical `MEMORY.md` read compatibility.

- **Backend or runtime:** mem0 provider contract uses the stateful fake server; composition `memory_mem0_swap` remains green.

**What the tests prove:** the exact divergence is fixed for providers opting into the shared document-tool vocabulary, without asserting that every memory provider ships those tools or aliases.

prs.title: fix(loop): compact context on window eviction
prs.body:
## Summary

- Convert bounded recent-window eviction into a typed forced-compaction signal instead of silently losing durable model context.
- Preserve complete assistant/tool-result exchanges at the 128-message boundary, keep the latest later user/steering instruction raw, and permit finalized tool-result cut points only in the dedicated window-eviction mode.
- Add caller-path coverage proving a 130-tool run persists a summary and still presents the original task to the model.
- This is stacked on #7503, which pins the accepted task before this PR makes the remaining eviction path lossless.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Closes #7484

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo build`
- [x] Relevant tests pass: loop contracts, agent-loop, loop-host, architecture boundary, and 130-tool production-wired regression listed below
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` if database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed (the root `integration` feature is empty — the flag is per-crate)
- [ ] Manual testing: not applicable; behavior is exercised through the production-wired integration harness
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `review-pr` or `pr-shepherd --fix` was run before requesting review

## Test Strategy

User behavior: A task can run past the 128-message recent-window limit without silently losing the original accepted task or the evicted tool history; durable summaries replace the omitted prefix.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: window-eviction triggering, safe user/tool-result cut selection, latest-steering preservation, deferred retry suppression, complete exchange eviction, active-task strategy handling, and host cut-point validation.
- Reborn integration: `long_tool_run_keeps_the_original_task_after_raw_history_exceeds_window_limit` drives 130 tool calls through the production loop/host path and asserts durable summary persistence plus original-task presence in the final model request.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no provider wire contract or replay fixture changed.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no browser-visible behavior changed.
- Backend or runtime: Host and executor contract suites exercise the real compaction boundary; no optional database backend behavior changed.
- Live canary: Not applicable: no external deployment or provider is required to reproduce this deterministic context-window path.

What the tests prove: Eviction reports an exact stable watermark, latest steering remains outside the compacted prefix, the canonical loop compacts at a validated user or finalized tool-result boundary, repeated unchanged deferrals do not spin, summaries persist, and the model retains the task after raw durable history exceeds 128 messages.

Commands run:

- `cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_model_recovery long_tool_run_keeps_the_original_task_after_raw_history_exceeds_window_limit -- --exact --nocapture`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_contracts -p ironclaw_agent_loop -p ironclaw_loop_host -p ironclaw_turn_runner --all-targets` (all affected suites pass; one unrelated pre-existing `ironclaw_turn_runner::trace_capture::tests::capture_skips_when_policy_missing_or_disabled` failure reproduced unchanged on the base)
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --test reborn_dependency_boundaries reborn_contracts_crates_carry_a_checked_size_ceiling -- --exact`
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_loop_contracts -p ironclaw_agent_loop -p ironclaw_loop_host -p ironclaw_turn_runner --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `python3 scripts/ci/docs_publication_boundary.py`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

## Security Impact

None. This changes context-retention and compaction policy without changing permissions, network access, secrets, file access, tool authorization, or sandbox policy.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: `LoopContextWindowTruncation` remains host-produced; the loop only consumes the typed durable watermark. The new enum variants are neutral contract vocabulary.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive. No new prompt content path is introduced; compaction still reads the existing normalized transcript.

- Add caller, backend, and production-wired coverage, including a 130-tool-call run whose final model request still contains the original task.

This PR builds on merged #7502 because the token-budget pinning path uses the unified estimator introduced there. It is the first of two #7484 PRs; the follow-up will consume the omission watermark to compact on eviction. prs.title: feat(llm): explicit Anthropic cache_control breakpoints on both transports
prs.body:
Closes #6984 — P0 #1 of the pi-harness adoption program (`docs/research/pi-agent-deep-dive.md` §7.3, PR #6991).

## Summary

Both Anthropic transports now place explicit `cache_control` breakpoints instead of relying on automatic caching alone (rig/API-key path) or emitting nothing (OAuth path — previously **no cache markers at all**, so subscription-auth users got zero prompt caching).

**OAuth transport** (`anthropic_oauth.rs`): new `apply_cache_breakpoints` marks the three pi-style boundaries — system prompt block, last tool definition, last content block of the last message (including the tool_result tail common in agent loops) — each carrying the retention TTL. Retention `none` preserves the legacy wire shape exactly (plain-string system, no markers).

**API-key transport** (`rig_adapter.rs` + `create_anthropic_from_registry`):
- keeps the request-level automatic-caching marker (moving breakpoint for the growing conversation),
- adds an explicit marker on the **last tool** so the tool prefix stays cached when later content churns — rig's typed `ToolDefinition` can't carry `cache_control`, so the last tool moves into rig's raw `additional_params.tools` (appended after typed tools, order preserved, Anthropic-native `input_schema` shape),
- `short` retention additionally enables rig's typed system/last-message breakpoints (`CompletionModel::prompt_caching`).

`long` retention deliberately does **not** enable rig's typed breakpoints: they're always plain 5m ephemeral, and per Anthropic's rules a 5m block marker beside a 1h automatic marker on the last block is a 400 (TTL conflict), and 1h entries must precede 5m entries. All markers within a request therefore share one TTL. Verified against the current prompt-caching docs (request-level + block-level compatibility, 4-breakpoint budget, longer-TTL-first ordering).

Unsupported models (claude-2 era) downgrade to `none` on both paths via `supports_prompt_cache`.

## Tests (written first, red → green)

- **Wire-level capture tests** in both files: a loopback server captures the exact request JSON; six tests pin the breakpoint layout for short/long/none on each transport (system block marker, last-tool-only marker with order preservation, last-message block marker incl. tool_result, TTL values, and the no-caching legacy shape).
- **Seam tests** on `build_rig_request` for the tool move (marker + `input_schema` key + typed-tools untouched when caching is off).
- Full `ironclaw_llm` suite: 893 passed; crate clippy `-D warnings` clean.

Note on the issue's second acceptance item (sustained cache reads visible in `prompt_cache_activity`): cache-read counts come from the live API and can't be asserted hermetically; this PR pins the emitting side. The realized hit rate also depends on the rest of the P0 program (#6985 prefix stability, #6986 tool-array stability, #6987 regression test).

## Spec

`crates/ironclaw_llm/CLAUDE.md` gains an "Anthropic Prompt Caching" section documenting the layout and the TTL-ordering constraint.

prs.title: docs(reborn): Runtime-Swappable Components design document
prs.body:
## What

Adds `docs/reborn/design-documents/` — a home for architecture design documents in [GitLab's format](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/architecture/design-documents/) — and lands the first one, **Runtime-Swappable Components**, at `status: proposed`.

Docs-only. No code or behavior changes.

## Why

The question came out of a discussion on what should eventually be hot-swappable in IronClaw: what is installable, configurable, or replaceable at runtime rather than compiled into the host. It matters now because IronHub and collections/bundles are landing, and we should settle the product model before "extension" grows to mean several different things.

The document is backed by six code surveys of `crates/`; the evidence appendix (full swap matrix with `file:line` anchors) is linked from the review notes below rather than committed, since it is a point-in-time survey.

## The proposal in one paragraph

Make personas, prompts, skills, channels, loop profiles, and their composition installable and scope-selectable at runtime by generalizing three mechanisms that already work — the shared download-and-verify pipeline tools use today, the extension host's generational snapshot pattern, and the per-run resolution cadence — plus a typed scope resolver (service → tenant → user → thread) with exactly two combination rules: preference values take the nearest scope, authority values only narrow. The kernel, sandbox lanes, mount containment, safety layer, and registry verification never become swappable.

## Positions worth arguing with

These are the load-bearing calls; the Alternative Solutions section carries the rejected options and why.

- **Extension stays the only installable product object**, growing by *surface kind* (a new `[identity]` surface for personas, beside `[tool]` / `[channel]` / `[memory]`) — not by new object kinds.
- **Skills keep their own entry kind** rather than becoming a surface. The test proposed: does installing this create a binding the system must remember, or content the system must index? Skills are indexed content, their trust is decided per file, and they are the self-improvement substrate — package-level trust would defeat the per-file promotion gate.
- **Bundles/collections are `HarnessManifest`** (#3036), a composition object of references with at most one bound per thread — this is also the per-thread persona story.
- **Agent-authored artifacts enter at a non-trusted tier** and are promoted by human approval. This closes a live gap: learned skills currently auto-install at Trusted with full prompt-body exposure.
- **Third-party loop drivers are deferred** (a Non-Goal here); loop *profiles* as scoped data deliver most of the value with no new trust surface.

## Defects surfaced while researching (independent of this proposal)

- A `[channel]` manifest with no compiled adapter activates successfully on a placeholder bridge and fails only at the first inbound message — fails open at activation, closed at first use.
- The WASM prepared-component cache is keyed by module path and never invalidated, so a reinstalled extension executes stale code until restart.

Happy to file both separately if reviewers agree they are real.

## Review notes

- `coaches` and `dris` in the frontmatter are `@TBD` — please claim them.
- Security review holds blocking authority over the trust-promotion and channel-credential designs; other sections are consultative.
- Per GitLab's workflow this is meant to merge early and iterate — a merged document is a working draft, not an approved plan. Comments on the open questions (persona trust floor, model-cost custody, static-OAuth custody) are the most useful thing at this stage.
