prs.title: fix(webui): bound SSE reconnect storms
prs.body:
## Summary

- Keep `event-source-plus` for fetch, framing, cancellation, and `Last-Event-ID`, while making one IronClaw coordinator own reconnect timing across HTTP errors, stream endings, activity stalls, visibility changes, and network recovery.
- Apply jittered 1/2/4/8/16/30-second backoff, honor server `Retry-After`, and start the stability interval with a valid frame, and reset after that stream remains open for 15 seconds—even if quiet.
- Add `Retry-After` to request-volume and concurrent-stream 429 responses so the browser has an authoritative recovery deadline.
- Correct the stream-budget rationale and lock the real packaged-client behavior, retry budget, coalescing, reload, and server response contracts with regressions.
- Merge current `main` and raise the measured initial `/chat` gzip budget from 217.0 KB to 219.0 KB, retaining about 1.3 KB of explicit headroom after the merged main changes and retry coordinator landed together.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [x] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

None — reproduced from the QA Railway deployment report where one caller reached repeated `429 Too Many Requests` responses on the WebChat event stream.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings` — Not run workspace-wide; scoped owning-crate gate passed: `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_webui --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- [ ] `cargo build` — Not run separately; `cargo test -p ironclaw_webui --all-features` compiled the owning crate and `corepack pnpm build` produced the production SPA bundle.
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `cargo test -p ironclaw_webui --all-features`; `corepack pnpm test` (139 files, 1,244 tests).
- [ ] `cargo test --features integration` — Not applicable: no database-backed behavior or Reborn turn/runtime orchestration changed.
- [ ] Manual testing — Not applicable: deterministic hook tests drive all retry clocks and packaged transport callbacks; the production bundle was built and budget-checked.
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `review-pr` or `pr-shepherd --fix` was run before requesting review — Not run; final diff, production-file panic patterns, formatting, lint, typecheck, tests, and bundle were reviewed directly.

Additional gates: `corepack pnpm lint`, `corepack pnpm build`, bundle budgets, `git diff --check`.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: During a persistent WebChat stream failure, one tab performs at most seven opens per minute, multiple reconnect signals remain one retry chain, and a server 429 pauses until its advertised recovery deadline instead of feeding a reconnect storm.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [x] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: Extended `frontend/src/pages/chat/lib/useSSE.test.ts`, the real rate-limit router contract, and the SSE handler caller contract.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: no turn, runner, agent-loop, capability, or persistence behavior changed.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no model choice or request shape changed.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: retry timing and competing lifecycle signals are deterministic transport-hook behavior; the source-backed hook harness exercises the mounted hook and the actual `event-source-plus` package without browser/network timing flakiness.
- Backend or runtime: Not applicable: no database or execution-runtime behavior changed.
- Live canary: Not applicable: no provider dependency or model drift risk.

What the tests prove:

- One continuously failing tab cannot exhaust the 30-open-per-minute route budget.
- Watchdog, online, visibility, replay, response-error, and end-of-stream recovery converge on one timer.
- `Retry-After` overrides local backoff.
- HTTP 200 alone does not reset retry state; a valid frame starts the stability interval, and 15 seconds on the same open stream resets it even if no second frame arrives.
- Aborting from IronClaw's error hook prevents `event-source-plus@0.1.15` from starting its internal 2ms retry chain.
- Middleware and concurrent-stream 429 responses carry bounded retry hints.

Commands run:

- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/pages/chat/lib/useSSE.test.ts`
- `corepack pnpm test`
- `corepack pnpm lint`
- `corepack pnpm build`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_webui --all-features`
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_webui --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_webui -- -D warnings`
- `bash scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh`
- `git diff --check`

## Security Impact

The existing authenticated per-caller request-volume limit and three-stream concurrency cap remain unchanged. Responses now reveal only the bounded wait until an already-declared limit resets; they expose no caller identity, token, cursor, or internal capacity. The client continues sending the bearer in the `Authorization` header.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

N/A: browser transport lifecycle and HTTP recovery metadata only. No public trust-bearing types, prompt inputs, hashes, status/error variants, serialization defaults, runtime lanes, sandbox boundaries, permissions, or authority construction changed. Existing counters remain bounded and use overflow-safe arithmetic.

## Database Impact

None. No schema, migration, persistence format, PostgreSQL, or libSQL behavior changed.

## Blast Radius

WebChat SSE reconnect lifecycle and WebUI rate-limit responses. WebSocket transport behavior is unchanged except that its shared concurrency-cap rejection now also carries `Retry-After: 1`. The numerical rate and concurrency limits are unchanged.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this PR. There is no schema, persisted-state, configuration, or server/client version migration to reverse; the prior retry behavior returns immediately.

## Review Follow-Through

Reviewer judgment requested on the 15-second stability threshold. It intentionally aligns with the server's keep-alive cadence so the immediate admission frame cannot reset backoff while the next keep-alive proves sustained liveness.

The integration tier now uses parallel-safe file reads; deterministic timing overlap remains at the executor unit tier to avoid timing-sensitive integration tests.

prs.title: fix(safety): redact model-bound secrets without rejecting turns
prs.body:
## Summary

- Replace credential-content rejection in prompt contracts with deterministic redaction, so one false positive can no longer block prompt construction, attachment recovery, or unrelated threads.
- Add a source-independent final model-input redaction pass shared by plain, tool-capable, streaming, and repair provider calls.
- Preserve surrounding context and raw durable data while replacing detected values with `[REDACTED_SECRET]`.
- Keep prompt-injection handling separate: untrusted memory remains enveloped and an injection-bearing snippet is omitted without rejecting the turn.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [x] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

None.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_safety --no-fail-fast` (299 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_contracts --no-fail-fast`
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_turns --test agent_loop_host_contract --no-fail-fast` (87 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_host_runtime --test memory_prompt_context --no-fail-fast` (18 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --test llm_gateway --no-fail-fast` (88 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --lib provider_bound_redaction_covers_stop_sequences --no-fail-fast`
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --no-fail-fast`
- [x] `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_golden_payload --no-fail-fast` (21 passed)
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration`: Not applicable; no database-backed behavior changed.
- [ ] Manual testing: Not applicable; the behavior is deterministic and asserted at the provider and production-memory seams.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: Given recovered text containing security vocabulary, host paths, credential-shaped values, or prompt-injection markers, when IronClaw reconstructs and dispatches a model request, benign context remains usable, detected credential values are placeholders, injection-bearing memory snippets are isolated, and the turn continues.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit/contract: known credential formats, labeled weak values, Basic/Bearer authorization, UTF-8 boundaries, idempotency, benign near misses, large-input regex budget, structural prompt limits, and provider stop sequences.
- Caller contract: credential-bearing runtime, skill, instruction, and capability content no longer aborts prompt construction.
- Backend/runtime: production memory admission keeps security prose and paths, redacts credential values, drops injection-bearing snippets, and preserves model-content budgets.
- Provider boundary: recording providers prove secrets are absent from every message role, textual reasoning/content parts, tool descriptions, JSON schema strings/keys, prior tool arguments, and provider-generated repair prompts.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable; the production memory adapter and model gateway are exercised directly through their caller-facing integration binaries.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable; no model-selection behavior or nondeterministic output is asserted.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable; no browser behavior changed.
- Live canary: Not applicable; provider dispatch is captured before network I/O.

What the tests prove: detected secrets do not reach provider-visible prompt content, while false positives no longer reject a whole turn or remove unrelated context. Prompt-injection containment remains independent of secret handling.

## Security Impact

The model-input boundary now scans immediately before provider dispatch, after all prompt assembly and before prompt-cache hashing. It covers plain/tool/streaming/repair paths; message content across roles; text content parts; plain reasoning and summaries; tool-call argument string keys/values and parse errors; tool descriptions and JSON schema strings/keys; and stop sequences. It logs only aggregate redaction counts, never detected values.

Opaque protocol material that requires exact replay—encrypted/redacted reasoning payloads, signatures, tool-call IDs/names, route/model identifiers, and provider metadata—is not treated as prompt text. Managed credentials remain host-side and continue to use mediated injection rather than prompt construction.

This guarantees redaction for formats recognized by the existing leak detector plus labeled weak values such as `password: letmein`; it is not a cryptographic proof that arbitrary unlabeled prose cannot contain a secret. The strongest invariant remains: secrets known to IronClaw must stay in the secret store and never be assembled into model input. The final scan is defense in depth for untrusted text and accidental leakage.

Warn-only high-entropy hex findings remain visible unless they are credential-labeled, so ordinary SHA-256 fingerprints do not mutate prompts or prompt-cache identity.

Prompt injection is intentionally not conflated with secret detection. Existing trust envelopes and injection checks still isolate offending untrusted snippets. SkillSpector-style skill trust scanning and NeMo Guardrails-style broader input/output policy remain follow-up layers rather than dependencies of this recovery hotfix.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: the new public safety transform represents model-visible redaction results without exposing findings.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts through existing structural validation and trust envelopes, then receives source-independent redaction at provider dispatch.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose; prompt-cache hashing now observes the redacted system prompt.
- [x] New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: none.
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields: none changed.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters: no durability or concurrency semantics changed.
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors: credential content no longer creates a policy-denied turn; structural errors are unchanged.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names: no trust-boundary names changed.

## Database Impact

None. Raw stored LLM/thread/memory data is retained; redaction applies to the transient model-facing view.

## Blast Radius

Prompt construction contracts, production memory admission, and all loop-host provider request shapes. A regression could leak a recognized secret, corrupt opaque replay data, or reintroduce thread-wide rejection. Caller-level provider captures, memory integration tests, structural contract tests, all-features clippy, and architecture ratchets cover those directions.

## Compatibility and Rollback

No wire or storage migration. Removing the unused `base64` dependency from `ironclaw_loop_contracts` shrinks the contract layer. Roll back by reverting this PR; stored data requires no repair. During rollback, the prior credential denylist behavior—and its false-positive thread failures—would return.

## Follow-up

- Evaluate SkillSpector in the skill install/update trust pipeline, not on every runtime text field.
- Prototype NeMo Guardrails or an equivalent classifier as an observable, shadow-mode prompt-injection layer before considering enforcement.
- Add canary metrics for redaction frequency and snippet-level injection omission without logging source text.

---

**Review track**: C (security/runtime/DB/CI)

prs.title: fix(threads): restore listability for unprojected thread index rows
prs.body:
## Summary

- Port #7470's thread-index projection self-heal to the `release/2026-08-11` family layout.
- Reconcile marker-complete scopes once per process, repairing durable thread-index rows whose ordered-projection sidecar is missing or incomplete.
- Use the shared bounded CAS loop with an explicit forced write so sidecar-only damage is repaired even when the decoded record body is unchanged.
- Keep reconciliation bounded and non-fatal: healthy scopes pay one bounded directory listing plus one capped projection query, and scopes above `Page::MAX_LIMIT` are skipped.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Related #7178

Port of #7470 to `release/2026-08-11`.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo build`
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `cargo test -p ironclaw_filesystem`; `cargo test -p ironclaw_threads`
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` if database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed (the root `integration` feature is empty — the flag is per-crate)
- [ ] Manual testing: Not run; the regression is covered through the filesystem service contract.
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `review-pr` or `pr-shepherd --fix` was run before requesting review

Additional lint evidence: `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_filesystem -p ironclaw_threads --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passed.

`bash scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh` remains blocked by the target branch's existing composition-budget baseline: composition source is 1,654 LOC above the effective absolute ceiling and `Arc<dyn>` dispatch is one site above the effective ceiling. This PR changes no composition files.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: A thread whose durable index row loses some or all ordered-projection keys becomes visible in the sidebar again after the next process restart/listing request.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: filesystem CAS force-write regressions and filesystem thread-service recovery, retry, isolation, concurrency, partial-key, and oversized-scope contract tests.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: the owning filesystem service contract exercises the production caller and in-memory backend; existing PostgreSQL and libSQL filesystem/CAS contract suites also passed.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no provider or serialized transport fixture changed.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no frontend behavior changed; the backend listing result is asserted directly.
- Backend or runtime: `cargo test -p ironclaw_filesystem` includes in-memory, libSQL, and PostgreSQL filesystem/CAS contracts; `cargo test -p ironclaw_threads` includes libSQL/PostgreSQL release-pair migration contracts.
- Live canary: Not run for this port; #7470 documents the staging evidence for the original failure.

What the tests prove: sidecar-only damage is physically rewritten despite equal decoded bodies; incomplete projection keys are repaired; optional writes cannot suppress the first required repair; CAS races retry; failures degrade non-fatally and retry; unrelated scopes progress independently; oversized scopes remain bounded.

Commands run:

```text
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p ironclaw_filesystem
cargo test -p ironclaw_threads
cargo clippy -p ironclaw_filesystem -p ironclaw_threads --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
git diff --check
bash scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh  # blocked by unrelated target-branch composition baseline
```

## Security Impact

None. This does not change permissions, network calls, secrets, sandbox policy, or capability execution. It rewrites only an already-authorized thread-index record within the caller's existing scoped filesystem mount.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: no new public trust-bearing types.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive. N/A: no prompt path changed.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose; trust/binding/authenticity uses SHA-256/BLAKE3 or separate authenticity check. N/A: no hashing changed.
- [x] New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: downstream match sites audited. Command/output: N/A; no variants changed.
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields fail closed or have migration tests. N/A: this target-specific port does not add a persisted field.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters have bounds and overflow-safe arithmetic. Scope caches are capped at 128; repair is capped at `Page::MAX_LIMIT`; lock entries are weak and pruned.
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors have stable class semantics (`Transient`, `Permanent`, `Misconfigured`, `PolicyDenied` or equivalent). No new operator-visible error class; reconcile failure degrades to existing projected rows and remains retryable.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe trust boundary. N/A: no runtime lane changed.

## Database Impact

No schema migration. Existing index entries may be rewritten through their current backend using version-checked CAS. The target branch's existing `thread-index-v1.complete` marker path and body are preserved; this port intentionally does not import `release/1.1.1`'s separate `projection_schema_version` mechanism.

## Blast Radius

Touches the shared filesystem CAS helper and filesystem-backed thread listing. A regression could cause unnecessary index-row rewrites, delay the first listing after restart, or leave a damaged row hidden. Work is selective, version-checked, bounded, and once per scope per process after success. Scopes larger than `Page::MAX_LIMIT` retain current behavior and are not repaired.

## Rollback Plan

Revert commit `97d912525`. There is no schema change or new durable marker. Any successfully repaired index sidecars remain valid under the previous binary.

## Review Follow-Through

Please focus on the target-specific adaptation around the existing `thread-index-v1` marker and the removal of the source branch's projection-version dependency. The known follow-up remains a background/pagewise repair path for scopes above `Page::MAX_LIMIT`.

---

**Review track**: C (persistence/runtime behavior)

Updates `aws-lc-rs` from 1.17.0 to 1.18.0
Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.18.0

AWS-LC-FIPS module updated to 4.x

This release switches aws-lc-fips-sys (used via the fips feature) from the AWS-LC-FIPS 3.x branch to AWS-LC-FIPS 4.0.

  • If your project requires FIPS compliance, please consult your local FIPS compliance experts before upgrading. The FIPS v3 module shipped in aws-lc-rs v1.17.x is FIPS 140-3 validated ([Certificate #5314](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/certificate/5314) static, [Certificate #5298](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/certificate/5298) dynamic). The 4.x module has completed validation testing by an accredited lab and has been submitted to NIST for certification. Refer to the CMVP Modules In Progress List for its current status, and to FIPS.md for security policies and supported operating environments.
  • Consumers who need to remain on the FIPS 3.x module should pin aws-lc-rs to <1.18.0. See the Cargo Book on Specifying Dependencies.
AWS-LC-FIPS module aws-lc-rs
2.0.x <1.12.0
3.0.x <1.18.0
4.x latest

What's Changed

  • Switch aws-lc-fips-sys to AWS-LC's "FIPS 4.0" branch by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1185
    • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.13.16 -> v0.14.0. Please see the call-out above.
  • The ML-DSA signature APIs are now stable 🎉 by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1188 and aws/aws-lc-rs#1189
    • PqdsaKeyPair, PqdsaPublicKey, PqdsaPrivateKey, PqdsaSigningAlgorithm, PqdsaVerificationAlgorithm, and the ML_DSA_44 / ML_DSA_65 / ML_DSA_87 algorithms (and their _SIGNING counterparts) now live in aws_lc_rs::signature. ML-DSA no longer requires the unstable feature, and is now available under fips -- the FIPS 4.0 module provides ML-DSA, which is what had kept these APIs unstable. See our updated API documentation.
    • Please migrate any use of aws_lc_rs::unstable::signature to aws_lc_rs::signature. The unstable::signature module remains as deprecated aliases and will be removed in a future release.
    • PqdsaKeyPair::to_pkcs8 has been renamed to to_pkcs8v1, since elsewhere in the module an unqualified to_pkcs8 means PKCS#8 v2. A deprecated to_pkcs8 alias remains available under the unstable feature.
    • Existing unstable consumers continue to compile, with deprecation warnings. Two cases need a source change: builds using #![deny(warnings)], and code that glob-imports both signature::* and unstable::signature::*, which now needs an explicit import to disambiguate.
    • Behavior change: PqdsaVerificationAlgorithm::parsed_verify_digest_sig now always returns Unspecified. Digest-then-verify is not an operation defined by FIPS 204 -- pure ML-DSA signs the message itself, and the pre-hash variant (HashML-DSA) uses a distinct domain separator that this API does not implement.
  • Add out-of-place AEAD sealing by @​iainmcgin in aws/aws-lc-rs#1183
    • Adds seal_separate_out_of_place to LessSafeKey and TlsRecordSealingKey. Every sealing entry point was previously in-place, so a caller whose plaintext was borrowed or shared had to copy it into a scratch buffer purely to make it mutable. This mirrors the existing open_separate_gather, so the sealing and opening directions now match.
  • Add rsa::KeyPair::from_components for constructing RSA key pairs from raw components by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1175
    • Adds rsa::KeyPairComponents and rsa::KeyPair::from_components, matching ring 0.17, so a signing key can be built from formats such as JWK without first encoding the components as DER. Unlike ring, d and the CRT parameters are validated at construction using RSA_check_key, so keys with inconsistent or placeholder values that ring accepts may be rejected. Unnecessary generic bounds were also removed from PublicKeyComponents.
  • Automatically optimize aws-lc for size when opt-level is "s" or "z" by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1159
    • The builder now enables AWS-LC's size-optimized configuration (OPENSSL_SMALL, and no AVX-512 assembly on x86_64) whenever Cargo is already building for size. In CI, a small binary exercising SHA-256, AES-256-GCM, and ECDSA P-256 is 36-50% smaller at opt-level=z than at opt-level=3: 50% on x86_64 Linux, 48% on aarch64 macOS, 39% on x86_64 Windows, 36% on aarch64 Linux. Your own savings depend on how much of AWS-LC your binary retains.
    • No algorithms are removed and outputs are unchanged; the trade-off is slower elliptic-curve performance. Set AWS_LC_SYS_SMALL=1/=0 to force it on or off independently of opt-level.
    • FIPS builds do not opt in automatically: aws-lc-fips-sys requires an explicit AWS_LC_FIPS_SYS_SMALL=1, and warns when it is set.
    • Partially addresses aws/aws-lc-rs#745; the default size under opt-level=3 footprint is unchanged.
  • Export native library build metadata from the -sys crates by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1187, including original commits from @​glebpom in aws/aws-lc-rs#1184
    • Downstream build scripts compiling C code against AWS-LC can now locate our artifacts via DEP_AWS_LC_* / DEP_AWS_LC_FIPS_* (libdir, libcrypto_path, link_kind, and libssl_path with ssl), consistently across the CC, CMake, and system-library build paths. Existing linker directives are unchanged. On Windows, the *_path values are the link-time artifact (import library), not the runtime DLL.
  • Key wrap hardening by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1190 and aws/aws-lc-rs#1191
    • KeyEncryptionKey::unwrap no longer underflows on ciphertexts shorter than 8 bytes. Since the ciphertext is untrusted input, builds with overflow-checks = true would panic instead of returning the documented Err(Unspecified); default release builds were unaffected.
    • KeyEncryptionKey now zeroizes its key material on drop, consistent with the other key types in this crate.
  • docs(signature): correct outdated note about signing a separate digest by @​WesleyRosenblum in aws/aws-lc-rs#1186

Upstream AWS-LC (v5.5.0)

aws-lc-sys v0.44.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.5.0 (previously v5.2.0). See also the release notes for v5.3.0 and v5.4.0.

Build Improvements

  • Fix bindings copy from read-only prebuilt AWS-LC install by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1194
    • Copies into OUT_DIR now remove any stale destination first and leave the fresh copy writable, so building against a read-only prebuilt install (e.g. the Nix store) no longer fails with Permission denied on a build-script rerun. An OUT_DIR already poisoned by an earlier build now recovers without a cargo clean.

prs.title: feat(loop): keep the cached system prefix byte-stable across model calls
prs.body:
## Summary

- The gateway coalesces every system-role message into one leading system block — the provider-cached prompt prefix. Two sources rewrote that block on individual model calls: inline loop-control nudges emitted *ahead* of the identity section, and the runtime context's minute-precision clock. `prompt_cache_activity` measured the consequence: hit rate collapsing 82% → 29% (~3.5× input cost).
- **Bundle ordering** (`ironclaw_loop_contracts`): runtime context and inline messages now emit **after** the thread messages, so per-call context rides the conversation tail.
- **Gateway coalescing** (`ironclaw_loop_host`): only the **leading run** of system messages folds into the system block. A system message positioned after the first non-system message stays at its transcript position as a host reminder.
- **A host reminder is a distinct role, not a user message** (`Role::HostReminder`). It renders in the user shape on the wire — no vendor API has a role for it — but three production consumers ask "what did the user last ask?" by scanning back for `Role::User`: `unavailable_requested_capability_guard`, `SmartRoutingProvider::classify`, and the trace-replay request hint. Since the reminder is the final message on nearly every call, a plain user-role message would feed all three the runtime clock instead of the real request. The distinct variant also makes the compiler enumerate every provider's rendering decision.
- **Every mock-LLM test now asserts prompt-cache reuse.** A cache regression is invisible to functional assertions — the model still answers correctly, it just costs 3.5× more — so `tests/e2e/mock_llm.py` observes each request's cached prefix and the autouse `assert_prompt_cache_reuse` fixture fails any test whose system block changes without a tool-surface change to explain it.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature (the cache-reuse gate)
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Closes #6985 — P0 #2 of the pi-harness adoption program (`docs/research/pi-agent-deep-dive.md` §7.3, PR #6991). Companion to #6997 (explicit cache breakpoints): breakpoints only pay off once the prefix stops churning.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all --tests --examples -- -D warnings` (default-feature lane, which PR CI skips)
- [x] `cargo build`
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `ironclaw_llm`, `ironclaw_loop_host`, `ironclaw_loop_contracts`, `ironclaw_turns`, `ironclaw_agent_loop`, `ironclaw_runner`, the full `ironclaw_reborn_integration_tests` package, `ironclaw_architecture`
- [ ] `cargo test --features integration` — Not applicable: no database-backed or schema behavior changed.
- [x] Manual testing: reverted the gateway to the old `Role::User` framing and confirmed all three `prompt_prefix_stability` tests fail for the right reason (the runtime clock displacing the user's actual ask as the last user message), then restored.

## Test Strategy

**User behavior:** A long conversation stays cheap. Per-call context (the clock, loop-control nudges) reaches the model without re-billing the whole prompt on every iteration, and host guidance never displaces the user's own message in the transcript.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior — prompt composition and message ordering changed for every model call.
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions — host guidance is demoted from the system block; the `<system-reminder>` frame is now an escaping boundary for untrusted embedded content.
- [x] External provider — every provider adapter renders the new role; two needed a same-role merge.
- [x] Cross-component behavior — `loop_contracts` → `loop_host` → `ironclaw_llm` adapters → provider wire.

Tests added or updated:
- **Unit or contract:** `provider::tests::host_reminder_*` (4 — delimiter escaping, surgical escaping that spares ordinary angle brackets, degenerate frames, and `renders_as_user()` vs `== Role::User` pinned apart); `anthropic_oauth::tests::host_reminder_merges_*` (2); `rig_adapter::tests::host_reminder_merges_into_the_trailing_user_message`; `llm_gateway.rs` gateway coalescing + the new `gateway_frames_a_compaction_summary_without_letting_it_escape`; `agent_loop_host_contract.rs` runtime-context ordering, with a thread message added to the fixture so the thread boundary is actually exercised.
- **Reborn integration:** `reborn_integration_prompt_prefix_stability` (3) — a repeated-call warning and the runtime clock each ride the tail at `Role::HostReminder` *positioned after every thread message*, system prompts stay byte-identical across loop iterations and across turns, and the tail reminder does not displace the real user message. `golden_payload` snapshots regenerated (role only).
- **Recorded fixture:** Not applicable: no model-choice or request-shape fixture behavior changed; the QA fixture scrub passes unchanged.
- **Browser E2E:** `test_prompt_cache_gate.py` (12) — self-tests for the new gate, plus the shared host-reminder predicate across both mock paths. Not a browser test, but it is the `tests/e2e` tier.
- **Backend or runtime:** Not applicable: no storage, migration, or runtime-lane behavior changed.
- **Live canary:** Not applicable: no live provider contract changed.

**What the tests prove:**
1. The cached prefix is byte-stable across loop iterations and across turns of one conversation, while the nudge and clock still reach the model.
2. They reach it at the tail, at `Role::HostReminder`, positioned after every thread message — so neither cache reuse nor the last-user-message consumers are harmed. Verified red-before-green against the old behavior.
3. Content embedded in a reminder (a compaction summary quoting a transcript, a tool result echoing fetched web content) cannot close the frame and have the remainder read as ordinary conversation.
4. No provider receives consecutive user messages (the `rig_adapter` comment records that Anthropic rejects them; `bedrock` already merged, the two Anthropic-shape adapters did not).
5. The cache gate itself catches the real regression, permits a tool-surface change, and does not false-positive across conversations.

**Commands run:**
```
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo clippy --all --tests --examples -- -D warnings
cargo test -p ironclaw_llm -p ironclaw_loop_host -p ironclaw_loop_contracts \
           -p ironclaw_turns -p ironclaw_agent_loop -p ironclaw_runner --no-fail-fast
cargo test -p ironclaw_reborn_integration_tests --no-fail-fast
cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture
cd tests/e2e && pytest scenarios/test_prompt_cache_gate.py
```

## Security Impact

Host guidance that used to sit in the system block now sits at a transcript position in the user shape. Two mitigations, both tested:

- **Structural:** the `Role::HostReminder` variant keeps host code able to tell host guidance from user speech, which a text marker alone cannot. Without it, a user could not spoof anything, but the *host's own* consumers would mistake the reminder for the request.
- **Textual:** `ChatMessage::host_reminder` applies the `<system-reminder>` frame itself and neutralizes the two delimiters inside the payload, so embedded content (compaction summaries quoting a transcript, tool results echoing fetched web content) cannot break out. Escaping is surgical — only the two exact delimiters, case-insensitively — so code and markup in a summary survive intact.

Note this does **not** make the frame unforgeable in user-authored input: a user can still type the literal marker. Nothing downstream grants the frame authority beyond what the model infers, and the structural role is what host code trusts, so this is a prompt-level consideration rather than a privilege boundary. Filed as a follow-up rather than expanded here.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] **Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types:** `Role::HostReminder` is constructed only by `ChatMessage::host_reminder`, which is the sole place the frame is applied — a caller cannot build a half-formed one.
- [x] **Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive:** `ChatMessage::host_reminder` is that primitive; `escape_reminder_delimiters` is its escaping half. Pinned by `host_reminder_neutralizes_embedded_delimiters` and the compaction-summary gateway test.
- [x] **Hashes declare purpose:** N/A — no hashing added. (The mock's conversation key is a grouping fingerprint in test code, not a trust or binding hash.)
- [x] **New/changed variants: downstream match sites audited.** Adding `Role::HostReminder` made the compiler enumerate all 9 exhaustive match sites (`rg -n "match msg.role" crates/ironclaw_llm/src`), each of which now states its rendering decision. Non-exhaustive `== Role::User` comparisons were audited by hand: the three last-user-message consumers are *intentionally* left keying on `Role::User` and now carry comments saying why.
- [x] **`serde(default)` fields fail closed:** N/A — no new serde fields. `Role` gains a variant with an explicit `#[serde(rename = "host_reminder")]`; no provider serializes `Role` directly to the wire (each converts explicitly), so no payload shape changed.
- [x] **Queues/maps/buffers/counters bounded:** the mock's cache-observation maps are test-only and reset per test by the autouse fixture.
- [x] **Error class semantics:** unchanged.
- [x] **Sandbox/native/host names:** `HostReminder` names exactly what it is — host-authored, transcript-positioned guidance.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

Every model call in the product goes through this path, so the ordering change is broad even though the diff is small. The provider adapters are the sharpest edge: all nine now render `Role::HostReminder`, and `anthropic_oauth` / `rig_adapter` gained a same-role merge they did not have (`bedrock` already had one). If a provider's merge were wrong, the symptom would be an API 400 on consecutive user messages, which the new adapter unit tests cover directly.

Known unrelated issue observed while testing: `golden_gated_turn_approve` overflows the default stack on macOS debug builds — reproduces on the branch *before* these changes, and passes under `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`. Not introduced here; flagging rather than fixing in this PR.

## Rollback Plan

Revert the PR. The change is behavioral-only with no persisted state, no migration, and no wire-format change, so a revert is clean. The golden snapshots revert with it.

## Review Follow-Through

Addressed in this revision:
- **Architecture ceiling (13,306 → 13,390 lines):** the 84-line increase in `ironclaw_loop_contracts` is the minimum typed contract needed to distinguish leading subagent direction/goal material from volatile tail loop-control messages. The serialized `LoopInlineMessageRole` vocabulary and deterministic `InstructionBundleBuilder` ordering are owned by this contracts crate; moving either into `loop_host` would duplicate or bypass the shared provider-facing contract. No dependency edge or unrelated logic was added.
- **serrrfirat (High)** — host reminders replacing the real request for last-user consumers. Fixed structurally with `Role::HostReminder`; the three consumers now carry comments explaining why they must keep matching `Role::User`, and `tail_reminder_does_not_displace_the_real_user_message` pins it.
- **serrrfirat (Medium)** — missing Test Strategy section. Restored above with every tier completed.
- **CodeRabbit (Major)** — embedded `</system-reminder>` escaping; tail-ordering assertions rather than presence+exclusion; per-request boundaries in `assert_system_prompts_identical`; both mock paths sharing one reminder predicate; the duplicate `[[exemption]]` entry.
- **CodeRabbit (Minor)** — complete-frame requirement in the reminder predicate; the thread-message boundary in the `agent_loop_host_contract` fixture.
- **Copilot** — `assert_system_prompts_identical` now finds the first differing **byte** and clamps excerpts to char boundaries (the old version collapsed to `[non-boundary]` exactly when the prompt contained multi-byte characters, which it always does — the runtime text has em dashes).

Reviewer judgment still welcome on: whether the `<system-reminder>` marker should additionally be stripped from user-authored input (see Security Impact — I judged it out of scope for this PR); and whether #6997 places its cache breakpoints *before* the tail reminder, since a breakpoint at or after it can never hit.

---

**Review track**: C (runtime)

version 1.8.6

Changes since 1.8.5:

  • update_mmap and update_mmap_rayon (and by extension b3sum) now use seek rather than metadata to get the length of a file/mapping, and they tolerate mmap failures. AWS-LC-FIPS module updated to 4.x

This release switches aws-lc-fips-sys (used via the fips feature) from the AWS-LC-FIPS 3.x branch to AWS-LC-FIPS 4.0.

  • If your project requires FIPS compliance, please consult your local FIPS compliance experts before upgrading. Refer to the CMVP Modules In Progress List for its current status, and to FIPS.md for security policies and supported operating environments.
  • Consumers who need to remain on the FIPS 3.x module should pin aws-lc-rs to <1.18.0. See the Cargo Book on Specifying Dependencies.

    • PqdsaKeyPair, PqdsaPublicKey, PqdsaPrivateKey, PqdsaSigningAlgorithm, PqdsaVerificationAlgorithm, and the ML_DSA_44 / ML_DSA_65 / ML_DSA_87 algorithms (and their _SIGNING counterparts) now live in aws_lc_rs::signature. ML-DSA no longer requires the unstable feature, and is now available under fips -- the FIPS 4.0 module provides ML-DSA, which is what had kept these APIs unstable. See our updated API documentation.
    • Please migrate any use of aws_lc_rs::unstable::signature to aws_lc_rs::signature. The unstable::signature module remains as deprecated aliases and will be removed in a future release.
    • PqdsaKeyPair::to_pkcs8 has been renamed to to_pkcs8v1, since elsewhere in the module an unqualified to_pkcs8 means PKCS#8 v2. A deprecated to_pkcs8 alias remains available under the unstable feature.
    • Existing unstable consumers continue to compile, with deprecation warnings. Two cases need a source change: builds using #![deny(warnings)], and code that glob-imports both signature::* and unstable::signature::*, which now needs an explicit import to disambiguate.
    • Behavior change: PqdsaVerificationAlgorithm::parsed_verify_digest_sig now always returns Unspecified. Digest-then-verify is not an operation defined by FIPS 204 -- pure ML-DSA signs the message itself, and the pre-hash variant (HashML-DSA) uses a distinct domain separator that this API does not implement.
  • Add out-of-place AEAD sealing by @​iainmcgin in aws/aws-lc-rs#1183
    • Adds seal_separate_out_of_place to LessSafeKey and TlsRecordSealingKey. Every sealing entry point was previously in-place, so a caller whose plaintext was borrowed or shared had to copy it into a scratch buffer purely to make it mutable. This mirrors the existing open_separate_gather, so the sealing and opening directions now match.
  • Add rsa::KeyPair::from_components for constructing RSA key pairs from raw components by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1175
    • Adds rsa::KeyPairComponents and rsa::KeyPair::from_components, matching ring 0.17, so a signing key can be built from formats such as JWK without first encoding the components as DER. Unlike ring, d and the CRT parameters are validated at construction using RSA_check_key, so keys with inconsistent or placeholder values that ring accepts may be rejected. Unnecessary generic bounds were also removed from PublicKeyComponents.
  • Automatically optimize aws-lc for size when opt-level is "s" or "z" by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1159
    • The builder now enables AWS-LC's size-optimized configuration (OPENSSL_SMALL, and no AVX-512 assembly on x86_64) whenever Cargo is already building for size. In CI, a small binary exercising SHA-256, AES-256-GCM, and ECDSA P-256 is 36-50% smaller at opt-level=z than at opt-level=3: 50% on x86_64 Linux, 48% on aarch64 macOS, 39% on x86_64 Windows, 36% on aarch64 Linux. Your own savings depend on how much of AWS-LC your binary retains.
    • No algorithms are removed and outputs are unchanged; the trade-off is slower elliptic-curve performance. Set AWS_LC_SYS_SMALL=1/=0 to force it on or off independently of opt-level.
    • FIPS builds do not opt in automatically: aws-lc-fips-sys requires an explicit AWS_LC_FIPS_SYS_SMALL=1, and warns when it is set.
    • Partially addresses aws/aws-lc-rs#745; the default size under opt-level=3 footprint is unchanged.
  • Export native library build metadata from the -sys crates by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1187, including original commits from @​glebpom in aws/aws-lc-rs#1184
    • Downstream build scripts compiling C code against AWS-LC can now locate our artifacts via DEP_AWS_LC_* / DEP_AWS_LC_FIPS_* (libdir, libcrypto_path, link_kind, and libssl_path with ssl), consistently across the CC, CMake, and system-library build paths. Existing linker directives are unchanged. On Windows, the *_path values are the link-time artifact (import library), not the runtime DLL.
  • Key wrap hardening by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1190 and aws/aws-lc-rs#1191
    • KeyEncryptionKey::unwrap no longer underflows on ciphertexts shorter than 8 bytes. Since the ciphertext is untrusted input, builds with overflow-checks = true would panic instead of returning the documented Err(Unspecified); default release builds were unaffected.
    • KeyEncryptionKey now zeroizes its key material on drop, consistent with the other key types in this crate.
  • docs(signature): correct outdated note about signing a separate digest by @​WesleyRosenblum in aws/aws-lc-rs#1186

Upstream AWS-LC (v5.5.0)

aws-lc-sys v0.44.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.5.0 (previously v5.2.0). See also the release notes for v5.3.0 and v5.4.0.

Build Improvements

  • Fix bindings copy from read-only prebuilt AWS-LC install by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1194
    • Copies into OUT_DIR now remove any stale destination first and leave the fresh copy writable, so building against a read-only prebuilt install (e.g. the Nix store) no longer fails with Permission denied on a build-script rerun. An OUT_DIR already poisoned by an earlier build now recovers without a cargo clean.

Issues Being Closed

  • Expose out-of-place AEAD sealing -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1182

prs.title: fix(triggers): add unattended scheduled-run protocol
prs.body:
## Summary

- append a loop-owned unattended-run protocol when the trusted turn origin is `ScheduledTrigger`
- tell scheduled runs to execute with bounded assumptions, produce a self-contained recorded result, and preserve all host gates
- keep interactive prompt behavior unchanged and document the trigger/prompt ownership contract

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Related #6879

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings` — targeted owning-crate clippy was run instead
- [ ] `cargo build` — covered by the targeted test and clippy builds below
- [x] Relevant tests pass: composition prompt regression, loop-host prompt assets, triggered-submit integration, composition prompt boundary
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` — Not applicable: no database-backed owning-crate integration feature changed
- [ ] Manual testing — Not applicable: behavior is deterministic prompt assembly and is covered at the identity-source caller seam
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `review-pr` or `pr-shepherd --fix` was run before requesting review — not run

## Test Strategy

User behavior: Scheduled routines are explicitly told that no human is present, must perform the stored task instead of ending with a question, and must produce a self-contained recorded result. Interactive runs retain their existing ask-the-user behavior.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: Added `scheduled_trigger_origin_appends_unattended_protocol_only_to_triggered_runs`; extended prompt-asset guards for the new Markdown asset.
- Reborn integration: Existing `reborn_integration_triggered_submit` suite passes (18 tests). The harness intentionally wires `EmptyIdentityContextSource`, so the new prompt assertion lives at the real `HostIdentityContextSource` caller seam instead of being vacuous in this suite.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no provider-dependent model decision is needed to verify origin-based prompt assembly.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no browser surface changed.
- Backend or runtime: Not applicable: no persistence backend, runtime lane, or configuration shape changed.
- Live canary: Not applicable: deterministic prompt selection is fully covered hermetically.

What the tests prove: A trusted `ScheduledTrigger` context receives the unattended protocol, an explicit `Inbound` context does not, the asset remains valid and distinct, existing triggered submission behavior remains green, and prompt text stays outside the composition crate.

Commands run:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_composition scheduled_trigger_origin_appends_unattended_protocol_only_to_triggered_runs --lib`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host system_prompt_assets --lib`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_triggered_submit`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --test reborn_composition_boundaries composition_root_embeds_no_prompt_content`
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_loop_host -p ironclaw_composition --lib --tests -- -D warnings`
- `python3 scripts/ci/docs_publication_boundary.py`

## Security Impact

None. This does not change authorization, approvals, authentication, permissions, secrets, tool execution, or delivery routing. The protocol explicitly preserves existing host gates and forbids guessing credentials, permissions, or destinations.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: Not applicable; no types or constructors changed.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive: Not applicable; the new text is a host-owned static prompt asset and user content handling is unchanged.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose; trust/binding/authenticity uses SHA-256/BLAKE3 or separate authenticity check: Not applicable; no hashes changed.
- [x] New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: Not applicable; no variants changed.
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields fail closed or have migration tests: Not applicable; no serialized fields changed.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters have bounds and overflow-safe arithmetic: Not applicable; none changed.
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors have stable class semantics: Not applicable; no errors changed.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe trust boundary: `ScheduledTrigger` remains the existing trusted-origin discriminator; no runtime lane names changed.

## Database Impact

None. No schema, migration, query, or backend behavior changes.

## Blast Radius

Limited to default system-prompt assembly for runs whose trusted product origin is `ScheduledTrigger`, plus the loop-host prompt asset registry and trigger contract documentation. Interactive, inbound-channel, and WebUI turns do not receive the new protocol.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this commit. There is no migration or persisted-state compatibility concern; removing the conditional append restores the previous prompt behavior immediately.

## Review Follow-Through

A `[SILENT]`-style suppression sentinel is intentionally not included in this slice because no deterministic delivery-layer consumer exists yet; prompt-only support could deliver the literal marker. That should land with explicit suppression semantics in a follow-up.

---

**Review track**: B

prs.title: fix(loop-host): unify token estimation
prs.body:
## Summary

- Replace the loop host's conflicting token estimators with one shared estimator.
- Restore the documented ASCII rate of four characters per token while retaining a conservative surcharge for multibyte input.
- Route prompt-context, model-schema, disclosure, and inspector accounting through the same estimator and pin the caller-facing budget behavior with a contract test.
- Keep transcript selection contiguous; grouping-aware handling of individually oversized messages remains a follow-up because skipping a middle message can orphan provider tool calls from their results.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [x] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Related #7485

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings` (scoped all-target/all-feature command below passed)
- [ ] `cargo build` (covered by test and clippy builds)
- [x] Relevant tests pass: full `ironclaw_loop_host` suite and direct assistant inspector consumer suite
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` if database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed (not applicable: no database or runtime-lane behavior changed)
- [ ] Manual testing: not applicable; deterministic accounting is covered at unit and caller-contract seams
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `review-pr` or `pr-shepherd --fix` was run before requesting review

## Test Strategy

User behavior: ASCII-heavy prompts and tool schemas no longer consume twice their documented token budget, so valid context is not evicted prematurely.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: estimator edge cases plus `thread_context_port_uses_documented_ascii_token_rate`, driven through `ThreadBackedLoopContextPort`.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: the production caller path is reachable directly through the loop-host contract test; no composition or storage backend behavior changed.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: provider usage fixtures include system prompts and schemas, so they cannot isolate the raw transcript estimator invariant.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no browser behavior changed.
- Backend or runtime: Not applicable: no persistence backend or runtime lane changed.
- Live canary: Not applicable: no external provider call is needed to verify deterministic accounting.

What the tests prove: empty, short, ASCII, Unicode, ceiling, and saturation behavior are pinned; a 40-character ASCII message is admitted by the real thread context adapter into an exact 10-token budget; the owning crate and inspector consumer remain compatible. The dependency audit also confirms the merge-queue RustSec advisory is resolved by `lru 0.18.2`.

Commands run:

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host
cargo test -p ironclaw_assistant --lib inspector_store::tests -- --nocapture
cargo clippy -p ironclaw_loop_host -p ironclaw_assistant -p ironclaw_turn_runner --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
git diff --check
cargo deny --all-features check
cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --locked
```

The broader downstream test sweep also found two pre-existing current-main failures unrelated to this diff: `trace_reads_are_available_as_product_views` requires `TRACE_COMMONS_TEST_TOKEN`, and `trace_capture::tests::capture_skips_when_policy_missing_or_disabled` creates a queue directory even when run alone. All other tests reached in those sweeps passed.

## Security Impact

Resolves RUSTSEC-2026-0253 by updating the lockfile from `lru 0.18.1` to `0.18.2`. No permissions, network calls, secrets, file access, tool execution, or sandbox policy changed.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

N/A: this changes deterministic token accounting only. It adds no trust-bearing types, prompt envelopes, hashes, status variants, serde fields, queues, errors, or runtime boundary names. Arithmetic remains saturating.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

Prompt transcript budgeting, model tool-schema estimates, deferred tool disclosure accounting, and assistant inspector estimates now share the same implementation. The primary compatibility risk is admitting more ASCII context than the previous accidental two-characters-per-token bound; Unicode input retains an explicit conservative surcharge.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this commit to restore the previous conservative prompt estimator and the separate schema estimator. No data migration or persisted wire shape is involved.

## Review Follow-Through

Issue #7485 also proposes continuing past an oversized transcript message. That is intentionally not included: skipping an arbitrary message can create a non-contiguous provider transcript and orphan tool-call/result pairs. A follow-up should define grouping-aware truncation at the transcript seam before changing that behavior.

---

**Review track**: B (maintainer-requested bug fix and focused refactor)

prs.title: fix(product): fail closed and hash gate projection identities
prs.body:
## Context

A run can block on more than one approval or auth gate. This PR was originally
opened to fix a specific collision: every run notification of the same kind on
the same run derived an identical, undiscriminated projection id
(`run-notification:approval:<run_id>`, `run-notification:auth:<run_id>`), so
two same-kind gates on one run landed on the same durable delivery row.

Since this PR was opened, `main` independently closed the same collision with
its own general fix (re-landed as part of `0b5fcde99`, "feat!: a run acts as
its invoker — remove shared-route subject binding (#7157 follow-ups)", #7377,
now on `upstream/main` at `89285c8e7`+). That fix made
`run_notification_projection_id` fold a `discriminator` into the id for every
discriminated kind, gate kinds included: embed it verbatim when short, or fall
back to a bounded, non-cryptographic hash (FNV-1a, with a truncated readable
prefix) when it would overflow `ProjectionUpdateRef`'s length cap. So on
`main` today, two same-kind gates already get distinct, non-colliding ids —
this PR is **no longer closing a live collision**.

What upstream's general mechanism does *not* give the two gate kinds
specifically, and what this PR still adds:

- **Fail-closed validation.** The generic path is infallible: a gate-kind
  notification built with no discriminator silently falls back to the old
  undiscriminated id, quietly reintroducing the exact collision on the path
  least likely to be noticed. This PR makes a missing or invalid gate ref a
  hard error (`MissingGateRef` / `InvalidGateRef`) for `ApprovalNeeded` and
  `AuthRequired`.
- **Cryptographic-strength, domain-separated hashing.** The generic fallback
  is FNV-1a — fast and stable, not collision-resistant — and only activates
  for discriminators over 96 bytes; below that it embeds the raw discriminator
  verbatim, so the durable projection id literally contains the gate ref
  string. This PR always folds the gate ref through a domain-separated,
  length-framed SHA-256 digest for the two gate kinds, so the durable id never
  carries the raw ref, regardless of its length.

## The fix

Bind the projection id to the specific gate. For `ApprovalNeeded` and
`AuthRequired`, the canonical `TurnGateRef` is folded into the id through a
domain-separated, length-framed SHA-256 digest:

```
run-notification:<kind>:<run_id>:<sha256_hex>
```

The digest input is three `u64`-big-endian length-framed parts — a versioned
domain tag, the kind suffix, and the canonical gate ref. Length framing is what
stops two different `(suffix, gate_ref)` pairs from concatenating into the same
byte string. Hashing rather than embedding the ref keeps it out of the
persisted delivery metadata.

The helper is fallible for these two kinds and **fails closed**. A gate-kind
notification with no gate ref returns an error instead of falling back to any
undiscriminated shape. Both production callers — the observer and the
triggered driver — surface that error as an invalid-projection-ref failure.

## Non-gate identities

`FinalReplyReady`, `ProgressUpdate`, `DeliveryStatus`, and any `RunBlocked`
notice with no discriminator keep the exact legacy
`run-notification:<suffix>:<run_id>` string, pinned by
`non_gate_run_notification_projection_ids_remain_byte_for_byte_stable`.

Discriminated non-gate notices (`RunBlocked`'s `reauth` / `auth-unavailable` /
`failed` stand-ins) now route their discriminator through `bounded_discriminator`
(upstream's generic mechanism): verbatim for any discriminator up to 96 bytes,
which covers every discriminator this codebase currently produces, so their
*wire format* is unaffected by that mechanism. This is pinned by
`non_gate_discriminated_projection_ids_embed_short_discriminators_verbatim` and
`over_long_non_gate_discriminators_stay_deliverable_and_distinct`.

One exception is not byte-for-byte unchanged, and it isn't this PR's doing: the
`RunBlocked` reauth/auth-unavailable stand-ins used to discriminate on a bare
fixed label (`"reauth"`, `"auth-unavailable"`) with no gate ref at all — so a
run parked on a *second* same-kind auth gate collided on this notice too.
Upstream's fix (same `0b5fcde99`) closed that gap by changing these
discriminators to `reauth:{gate_ref}` / `auth-unavailable:{gate_ref}`
(`triggered.rs:1030`, `triggered.rs:1066-1069`). That changes the resulting
projection id compared to its pre-fix shape — e.g. for `gate:auth-oauth-1`,
`run-notification:blocked:reauth:<run_id>` becomes
`run-notification:blocked:reauth:gate:auth-oauth-1:<run_id>` — even though it's
still embedded verbatim (well under the 96-byte threshold). This is a wanted
change, and it lands on this branch via the upstream merge rather than via any
commit in this PR.

## Tests

- `prompts.rs`: pinned SHA-256 digest construction indirectly via the contract
  suite; fail-closed coverage (`gate_kinds_reject_an_absent_gate_ref`,
  `approval_projection_preserves_the_safe_canonical_invalid_gate_reason`);
  non-gate stability (`non_gate_run_notification_projection_ids_remain_byte_for_byte_stable`);
  bounded-discriminator behavior for non-gate kinds
  (`non_gate_discriminated_projection_ids_embed_short_discriminators_verbatim`,
  `over_long_non_gate_discriminators_stay_deliverable_and_distinct`); multiple
  `RunBlocked` notices per run staying distinct
  (`run_blocked_notices_in_one_run_do_not_share_a_projection_id`).
- `run_delivery_contract.rs`: pinned digest vectors for one approval ref and
  one auth ref (`approval_gate_projection_identity_matches_the_pinned_digest_vector`,
  `auth_gate_projection_identity_matches_the_pinned_digest_vector`); two
  distinct same-kind gates per kind rendering and owning distinct durable rows
  while replays reuse their original row, on both the live observer
  (`observer_delivers_distinct_same_kind_gates_and_replays_reuse_their_identity`)
  and the triggered driver
  (`triggered_driver_delivers_distinct_same_kind_gates_once_each`); a second
  gate announcing instead of deduping against the first
  (`observer_delivers_a_prompt_for_each_distinct_approval_gate`,
  `observer_delivers_a_prompt_for_each_distinct_auth_gate`,
  `triggered_second_gate_announces_instead_of_deduping_against_the_first`);
  fail-closed skip when a gate-kind state carries no gate ref
  (`observer_skips_delivery_when_a_gate_kind_has_no_gate_ref`).

## Relationship to upstream's independent fix

This PR's commits were originally authored as part of #7029, now **closed**
and superseded by #7395 — which carried forward #7029's remaining value (a
TOCTOU claim-loss fix and a `Failed`-row reopen mechanism in
`delivery_coordinator.rs`), unrelated to projection identity.

Independently, `main` landed its own general fix for the same collision class
(`0b5fcde99`, part of #7377's re-land of the #7157 follow-ups), adding
`bounded_discriminator` for every discriminated notification kind and closing
the `RunBlocked` reauth/auth-unavailable gap described above. This branch was
then merged against that state (merge commit `2a8cd448c`). The resolution kept
**both** mechanisms: this PR's fail-closed, SHA-256-hashed identity for
`ApprovalNeeded`/`AuthRequired` specifically, and upstream's generic
`bounded_discriminator` for every other discriminated kind — which the merge
had to keep correctly wired, since upstream's `RunBlocked` fix now feeds a
gate ref into `bounded_discriminator` too, reintroducing the exact
overlong-discriminator risk `bounded_discriminator` exists to bound.

Net effect: `main`'s own general fix already prevents the two-same-kind-gate
collision for every discriminated kind, gate kinds included — merging this PR
does not fix a currently-dropped prompt. It raises the bar for the two gate
kinds specifically to fail-closed validation and a cryptographic-strength,
domain-separated digest that never persists the raw gate ref in the
notification's durable identity.

prs.title: fix(product): stop releasing the connect-nudge throttle on ref-less delivery
prs.body:
## Summary

`post_notice` collapsed "nothing sent" and "sent, but no vendor ref came back" into the same `None`. The connect-nudge anti-duplicate throttle released its reservation on any `None`, so a genuinely-delivered notice with no ref (web push always; Slack whenever `chat.postMessage` succeeds without a `ts`) incorrectly reopened the throttle and let a duplicate "please connect" nudge through.

Fix: `post_notice` now returns `NoticeEgress` (`NotSent` / `Sent { durably_recorded, message }`), classified from `CoordinatedDeliveryOutcome` via an exhaustive match (no wildcard, so a new variant fails to compile here instead of defaulting fail-open). The connect-nudge release condition now keys off `!egress.reached_vendor()` instead of handle presence — it releases only on proven non-delivery, holds on any `Sent` regardless of ref or durability confirmation. The two working-indicator call sites use `into_retraction_handle()` to keep their existing behavior unchanged.

## Tests

- Headline regression: a ref-less `Sent` accept must hold the reservation, not release it for a duplicate. I reverted the release condition to the old buggy logic and confirmed the test fails (duplicate nudge observed); restored it and confirmed it passes.
- `DeliveredUnconfirmed` (vendor accepted, durable write failed) must also hold the reservation.
- Unit test on `notice_egress_from_outcome` against every `CoordinatedDeliveryOutcome` variant.
- Pin `into_retraction_handle()` behavior at the working-indicator call site for a ref-less accept.

`cargo test -p ironclaw_assistant` is green (1017 tests), clippy and fmt are clean. One test (`triggered_run_crossing_terminal_during_timeout_grace_delivers_cancellation_notice`) is flaky; I confirmed it's flaky identically on unmodified `upstream/main`, unrelated to this change.

Fixes #7473.
